# Rule Category Register

Per-policy register of the rule-categorization values (domain + rule-type) applied to GEM rules. The categorization **vocabulary is now a schema controlled-vocabulary** — `gem:RuleDomain` and `gem:RuleType`, with their value individuals, were codified in `GEM_ontology.ttl` at S69 — and the values are promoted to the graph as `gem:ruleDomain` / `gem:ruleType` triples on each `gem:PolicyRule` individual.

This file operates under a **hybrid source-of-truth model**: the per-policy assignment tables below are the **Plan-turn authoring surface** where a new policy's rules are first categorized, but once a rule is minted as a `gem:PolicyRule` individual the **graph is authoritative** for that rule's categorization, and its table rows become provenance/historical record. New policies' rule categorizations are authored here at their Plan turn, then promoted to the graph on minting.

## Status

- **Promoted to schema (S69).** The two axes are controlled-vocabulary classes (`gem:RuleDomain`, `gem:RuleType`) in `GEM_ontology.ttl`; their value individuals carry enforced meaning (typed individuals, validated by the audit's value-side check and by SHACL). Per-rule assignments are promoted to the graph on minting, after which the graph is authoritative for that rule (see header).
- **Free to evolve** — anyone (project lead, future SME) can propose, modify, or retire categories. Add new ones to the lists below as new policies surface them; a new value also needs codifying as a `gem:RuleDomain` / `gem:RuleType` individual in `GEM_ontology.ttl`.
- **Two axes** (per rule): domain applicability + rule type. Both may take one or more values per rule.
- **Coverage may be partial** only for policies **not yet extracted**. Every policy that has minted `gem:PolicyRule` individuals in the graph MUST have its `### <identifier>` section here, authored in the **same session that minted those rules** (enforced by the `register_section_coverage` audit check — a missing section is RED). New policies' rules are categorized at their Plan turn and the section is written at their Generate turn. Existing entries are revisited only when a category is renamed/retired or when a rule is recategorized.
- **Per-policy ordering** is alphabetical/chronological by policy identifier as policies are extracted. Within a policy, rules are ordered by their `Rn` identifier.

## Two axes

### Axis 1 — Domain applicability

Which clinical activity within the policy a rule applies to. A rule may apply to one or more domains. Domains are named at the policy's scope, not at the schema's scope; a policy that spans multiple activities gets multiple domain values across its rules.

Current domain vocabulary:

- `screening` — applies to STI laboratory screening only (NCD 210.10)
- `hibc` — applies to HIBC behavioral counseling only (NCD 210.10)
- `cross-cutting` — applies to both/either service within a multi-domain policy

Extend with new domain values as new multi-activity policies arrive. Single-domain policies don't need a domain tag (the policy itself names the domain); domain tagging is most useful when one policy spans multiple activities.

### Axis 2 — Rule type

What kind of evaluator criterion the rule expresses. A rule may carry one or more rule-type values.

Current rule-type vocabulary:

- `coverage-scope` — what is covered, at what level
- `eligibility` — who/when is eligible
- `frequency` — how often / repeat-screening intervals
- `setting-definition` — what setting is required (positive definition + exclusions)
- `credentialed-actor` — who can order/perform/provide
- `service-definition` — defines a service itself
- `service-standard` — technical standards (FDA, CLIA, etc.)
- `risk-factor` — enumerates risk factors
- `risk-determination` — who/how determines risk
- `documentation` — documentation requirements
- `non-coverage` — what is NOT covered
- `cost-sharing` — patient cost obligations
- `concurrent-services` — what services can be billed on the same date / together
- `statutory-framing` — scope-defining reference to statute
- `definition` — generic catch-all for definitional rules not covered above
- `procedural` — program-administrative process distinct from substantive claim-eligibility rules (CED study admin, protocol submission, CMS publication) *(schema since S69; listed here S90)*
- `outcome-measure` — how a study measures or characterizes an outcome *(schema since S69; listed here S90)*
- `study-design` — content, structure, or analytical plan a study must follow *(schema since S69; listed here S90)*
- `study-quality` — methodological integrity of a study (e.g. CMS Coverage with Evidence Development) *(schema since S69; listed here S90)*
- `payment-rule` — whether / how much / how often Medicare pays for a covered item: separate-payment eligibility, payment frequency/timing, fee structure *(added S90, A52466)*
- `coding-correctness` — how a claim must be coded: required/prohibited codes and modifiers, code-selection and units-of-service rules, and incorrect-coding denials *(added S90, A52466)*

Extend with new rule-type values as new policies surface them.

#### Retired rule-type values

- `credential-definition` — *Retired 2026-06-14 / Session 56.* Originally tagged rules that defined a provider credential. Retired when SKILL.md §Rule Patterns → "What belongs as a rule" corollary #2 was extended from `gem:ClinicalConcept` to `gem:ProviderCredential`: a credential's statutory or policy definition is preserved on the credential individual's `gem:description`, and rules that name the credential execute by matching the claim's provider, not by re-reading the definition. Last and only use: NCD 210.10 R16 (§1833(u)(6)) and R17 (§1833(x)(2)(A)(i)), both dropped in S56.

### Scope-boundary sentences: capture vs. drop

A standalone sentence about the boundary between this policy and another policy or regulation is categorized by whether it asserts a **coverage effect** or merely **directs the reader elsewhere**:

- **Policy-scope non-alteration / non-withdrawal clause** — a sentence asserting that *this* policy does not alter, withdraw, or change coverage that another named policy or regulation provides (e.g., "This policy does not alter Medicare coverage … according to … section 240.2 and 310.1"; "This policy does not withdraw Medicare coverage … according to local coverage determination (LCDs) or the regulations … in 42 CFR 405.201-405.215 …"). **Capture** as a single `coverage-scope` rule, verbatim, preserving the cross-reference as written (SKILL.md §Rule Patterns → "What belongs as a rule" corollary #4). The clause asserts an executable coverage-effect boundary — it constrains how this policy interacts with the named framework — which is material to the downstream "denial overrides approval" conflict-resolution step if this policy is ever matched against a claim governed by that framework. Drop only a trailing navigational tail if present (e.g., "For information about LCDs, refer to <URL> …"). Precedents: `gemi:ncd240.2.1_r2` (S105, "does not alter" 240.2/310.1); `gemi:ncd310.1_r9` (S105, "does not withdraw" LCDs / Category B IDE regulations).
- **Navigational scope-boundary pointer** — a sentence whose only content is routing the reader to where another matter is handled (e.g., "Coverage … for the use of E0470 and E0471 for diagnoses other than OSA are addressed in the Respiratory Assist Devices (RAD) LCD …"). **Drop.** The pointer is non-executable, and the named policy is already a `gem:referencesPolicy` target, so its provenance is preserved without a rule. Precedent: L33718 D4 (S94).
- **Definitional pointer** — a standalone sentence whose only content is that a term this policy uses is defined somewhere else (e.g., *"Complex rehabilitative power-driven wheelchairs are defined in 42 CFR §414.202."*). **Drop.** It asserts no coverage effect; it routes the reader to a meaning. **The definition is not lost** — SKILL.md §Rule Patterns → "What belongs as a rule" corollary #2 puts the sentence verbatim on the named `gem:ClinicalConcept` (or `gem:ProviderCredential`) as governing text, which is where a reader of that individual looks for it. **The line to hold is between a sentence that *states a rule and cites a regulation* and one whose whole content *is* the citation:** `gemi:a54969_r1` — *"42 CFR Section 410.32 indicates that diagnostic tests may only be ordered by the treating physician…"* — is the first and is a rule; a bare *"X is defined in §Y"* is the second and is not. **Drop it even when the term it defines gates a rule of this policy.** That is the case the bullet exists for: NCD 280.16's `_r1` turns on *complex rehabilitative power-driven wheelchair* and an evaluator cannot execute it without knowing what one is — and the pointer still yields no rule, because it adds nothing executable that the citation alone does not already carry. Precedents: NCD 210.10 R15/R16/R17 (S56 — statutory credential definitions dropped, content preserved on `gemi:credentialPrimaryCarePhysician` / `gemi:credentialPrimaryCarePractitioner`); NCD 280.16 B2 (S158).

The test is executability: a non-alteration/non-withdrawal clause constrains a coverage outcome (keep); a bare "addressed elsewhere" pointer only routes the reader (drop); a definitional pointer only routes the reader to a term's meaning (drop). The first two both preserve the named policy via `gem:referencesPolicy`, and the difference between them is only whether the sentence *also* carries a coverage-effect assertion. **The third does not, and that asymmetry is the reason it needs its own bullet rather than a clause on the second:** the corpus mints **no individual for a CFR section** — 253 distinct `gem:referencesPolicy` targets and not one of them is a regulation — so a definitional pointer's referent has nothing to be referenced, and corollary #2's placement of the sentence on the named `gem:ClinicalConcept` is not a redundant second copy but the **only** place the citation survives. Drop the sentence *and* omit the concept and 42 CFR §414.202 leaves the graph entirely.

## Conventions for extending this file

- **New policy added:** append a new `### <policy identifier>` section in the order policies are extracted. Each section starts with a one-line description, a "Categorized DATE (Session N)" stamp, and a rule-count line, followed by the table.
- **New category added:** add to the relevant axis vocabulary above with a one-line definition. Note in the table where it first applies.
- **Category renamed/retired:** update the vocabulary list and apply the rename across all per-policy tables. Note the rename in `gem_edit_log.md`.
- **Rule recategorized:** edit the relevant cell. Significant recategorizations should be noted in `gem_edit_log.md`.
- **Policy migrated to PolicyRule individuals:** add an italic stamp immediately under the section heading recording the migration date, session, URI range of the minted `gem:PolicyRule` individuals, and the authoritative live source (`GEM_policy_instances.ttl`). After migration, the per-policy table is archival; new `gem:ruleType` or `gem:ruleDomain` assignments edit the graph, not the table.

#### Notes

- **Heading-repeated rules:** R10–R18 (Research Questions) repeat "Research Questions:" as their natural-prose prefix; R19–R21 (Patient Inclusion Criteria) repeat "The following criteria must be used to identify patients demonstrating TRD:"; R24–R30 (Patient Exclusions) repeat "Patients must not have:". All 19 are Pattern 2 per canonical definition (single-sentence with heading-repeated prose prefix).
- **Letter-labeled rules:** R33–R45 (CED Standards a–m) carry the δ-prefix scaffold (`[Section B scope: standards of scientific integrity (a–m) CMS uses to approve and post CED studies for VNS for TRD] <letter>. <verbatim>`), parallel to NCD 160.7's convention for its letter-labeled B.2.a–e conditions. Each is a single-sentence Pattern 1 rule. This is the transitional convention pending ζ schema extension (first-class `gem:Rule` individuals with `gem:parentRule` structural links). The wording was chosen as Section-parallel to NCD 160.7's `[Section B.2 ...]` form, using the source-authoritative phrase "standards of scientific integrity" (criterion g; R47 back-reference) as the named scope group within Section B, with the (a–m) annotation disambiguating the sub-block from Section B's other contents. (δ-prefix applied 2026-06-13, Session 53, §4.2(xix).)
- **R1 / R32 / R47** are Pattern 3 multi-sentence cohesive paragraphs. R32 introduces the 13 CED Standards; R47 describes the principal investigator's protocol submission process; R1 defines VNS.
- **Source-typo preservation** is documented separately below.

#### New axis-2 rule_type values introduced by NCD 160.18

- **`study-design`** — Rules that govern the content, structure, or analytical plan a study must follow (e.g., research-question requirements, trial-design specifications, separate-analysis requirements, post-trial obligations like the placebo-VNS active-VNS offer).
- **`study-quality`** — Rules that govern the methodological integrity of a study (used here for all 13 CED Standards of Scientific Integrity — purpose, evidence support, design appropriateness, sponsor competence, regulatory compliance, scientific-integrity standards, written protocol, exclusionary toxicity-test framing, registration, public release, subpopulation discussion, generalizability discussion).
- **`outcome-measure`** — Rules that define how the study measures or characterizes an outcome (e.g., "Response is defined as ≥ 50% improvement", "Remission is defined as below threshold", and the 9 Research Questions each of which defines an outcome the study must analyze).
- **`procedural`** — Rules that describe a program-administrative process distinct from the substantive claim-eligibility rules (e.g., AHRQ supports the studies, PI submits the protocol to CMS, approved studies are posted on the CMS website).

#### Source-typo notes preserved verbatim

- **R42 (CED Standard j)**: source has *"Agency for Healthcare Quality (AHRQ)"* — the actual AHRQ name is *"Agency for Healthcare **Research** and Quality"*. PDF text preserved verbatim per source-fidelity; the typo is in the CMS source document, not in the extraction.
- **R43 (CED Standard k)**: source has *"in a publicly accessibly manner"* — grammatically should be *"accessible"* (adjective modifying *"manner"*). PDF text preserved verbatim per source-fidelity.

- **No new axis-2 rule_type values.** All 22 rules use the existing vocabulary: `coverage-scope`, `documentation`, `non-coverage`, `service-definition`, `service-standard`, `setting-definition`, `statutory-framing` (7 distinct values).
- **R2 dual tagging.** R2 carries both `non-coverage` (the operative denial outcome) and `setting-definition` (the POS 31/32 facility setting is the rule's denial trigger). Per S60 B6 Thread 2, the policy-tracking footprint for POS Codes structured data starts with A52519 (alongside TN 2476's positive-list pattern); the deferred_proposal "Place of Service Codes (structured data)" tracks both patterns.
- **R6/R7 distinct rules.** R6 ("deliver-before-WOPD → denied") and R7 ("no payment even if WOPD later obtained") are kept as separate Rn entries despite their adjacency in source: R6 establishes the trigger; R7 extends with the no-rescue qualifier. Splitting matches the source's sentence-by-sentence pattern (Pattern 1 each).
- **R8 polarity.** Unique among the FR-1713 rules: a coverage-supporting rule (an unrelated supplier with WOPD CAN bill). Tagged `documentation` + `coverage-scope` rather than `non-coverage`.
- **R11/R13/R16/R17/R19/R20 definitional grouping (Pattern 2).** Multi-sentence service-definition rules kept whole because the constituent sentences form a single semantic unit at the HCPCS code level. R16/R19/R20 additionally carry coverage-scope or non-coverage because the definition includes a boundary statement (R16: "do not use E0485/E0486"; R19: smallest-size-necessary rule; R20: A9272 all-inclusive + A9270 routing for everything else).
- **R21 framing + list combined.** The CVR framing sentence + the "Effective for claims with dates of service on or after January 1, 2012: K0743" list-style continuation is captured as a single rule (Pattern 2) — the list is operative content qualified by the framing; splitting would leave both halves grammatically incomplete. R21's `gem:ruleDescription` string carries the terminating period to make it a complete sentence.
- **A7047 coding rule cross-reference.** R16's "Do not use the oral appliance HCPCS codes E0485 or E0486 for this interface" is also represented as the `gem:ruleDescription` on `gemi:a52519_a7047CodingRule_r1` (PolicyRule on `gemi:a52519_a7047CodingRule`, the PolicyCodingRule anchor scope; migrated S83 from a `gem:ruleDescription` triple on the PolicyCodingRule itself). The policy-level R16 captures the verbatim source; the anchor-scope PolicyRule carries a normalized restatement scoped to the A7047 anchor. Both forms are retained; the source-text fidelity is in R16, the anchor-scoped form is on the PolicyRule.
- **Group 1A `gem:ruleDescription`.** The normalized statement "For HCPCS Codes A7002, A7047 and E0600, ICD-10-CM code G47.33 does not support medical necessity." is carried on `gemi:a52519_group1A_r1` (PolicyRule on `gemi:a52519_group1A`, the PolicyGroup anchor scope; migrated S83 from a `gem:ruleDescription` triple on the PolicyGroup itself). This is the structural data complement to the policy's source-table content; it does not duplicate any of the 22 R-numbered rules above (which are policy-level rules, not Group-scoped).

#### Notes

- **No new axis-2 rule_type values.** All 40 rules use the existing vocabulary: `coverage-scope`, `credentialed-actor`, `documentation`, `eligibility`, `non-coverage`, `service-definition`, `service-standard` (7 distinct values).
- **B1 = Option B applied to four lists.** Three small (2-item) coding directives + one 4-item documentation list, all split per item with Pattern 2 synthesized prefix. The 2-item coding lists yield 2 rules each (R26-R27 New Implant, R31-R32 Revision, R36-R37 Removal); the 4-item documentation list yields 4 rules (R20-R23). The coding directives' synthesized prefixes preserve the verbatim source lead-ins ("New implantation of a Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulator (HNS) for treatment of OSA code one of the following:" / "Revision or replacement during the life cycle of HNS components for treatment of OSA is reported with one of the following (as applicable):" / "Removal of component(s) of an HNS for treatment of OSA is reported with one of the following (as applicable):"); the documentation list uses the source's verbatim lead-in ("The patient's medical record must document all of the following:").
- **B3 = Option (b) applied to all 4 ABN modifier blocks.** GA (6 sentences = R7-R12), GX (2 sentences = R13-R14), GZ (1 sentence = R15), GY (3 sentences = R16-R18). Each rule uses Pattern 1 with `"Modifier <X>:"` Pattern 2 synthesized prefix. GZ uses the prefix for uniformity even though it's a single-sentence block. Establishes a consistent throughline with B1: finer-grained per-sentence/per-item capture with heading prefix is the project's preferred granularity, even when the source structure is a paragraph of dependent sentences rather than a bulleted list.
- **B2 verbatim-cross-reference capture.** R30 captures the source DNS prose ("All those not listed under the ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity section of this article.") verbatim on `gemi:a58075_groupNewImplant`, even though the rule's content is already implicit in the closed-list semantic of the Group's 17 `gem:exclusivelyCoversCondition...` triples. Tom's articulating principle (2026-06-16, S63): when source prose carries a cross-reference, capture the verbatim reference rather than inlining or substituting the referenced content.
- **B5 = Option (a) shared sentence on both Groups.** R34 (on `groupRevision`) and R40 (on `groupRemoval`) carry identical verbatim text: "Note: CPT codes related to component(s) removal, replacement or revision do not require a dual diagnosis." Both Groups are materially governed by the rule per source semantics; the verbatim-capture posture captures once per scope.
- **B6 = Option (a) — Revision Group placement for R35.** The "Replacement or revision...considered medically necessary..." rule scopes specifically to revision/replacement claims; Removal is not mentioned in the sentence and the rule does not extend to it. Tom's articulating principle (2026-06-16, S63): policies are jigsaw puzzle pieces — silence in one policy is not negation, it's incompleteness; the complete picture emerges from combining rules across policies.
- **R3 in-rule §1833(e) citation kept.** "A claim submitted without a valid ICD-10-CM diagnosis code will be returned to the provider as an incomplete claim under Section 1833(e) of the Social Security Act." The §1833(e) citation is in-rule (defines the statutory pathway under which the return-as-incomplete action is taken) and is preserved verbatim per corollary #1 in-rule exemption. Precedent: L36524 R35.
- **R8 in-rule statutory citations kept.** GA sentence 2 names sections 1862(a)(1), 1862(a)(9), 1879(e), and 1879(g) of the Social Security Act as the statutory provisions under which GA-flagged services are denied; in-rule citations preserved per corollary #1 in-rule exemption.
- **kg/m^2 normalization.** R28's verbatim text uses `kg/m^2` (caret form), matching the existing `gemi:a58075_groupNewImplant` `gem:description` which already quotes this dual-diagnosis sentence in caret form. Source PDF renders the superscript-2 as a separate text-layer token; visually `kg/m²`.
- **R33 / R38 leading-asterisk drop.** Source uses `*Append modifier 52...` with a leading asterisk as a footnote marker. The asterisk is typographic (footnote pointer) rather than content, and is dropped from the rule string. Pattern 1, verbatim otherwise.
- **ASCII-hyphen normalization on modifier names.** Source PDF mixes en-dash and ASCII hyphen inconsistently in `-GA` / `-GX` / `-GY` / `-GZ` / `CMS-R-131`. All normalized to ASCII hyphen in the captured rule strings.
- **Methodology drops (silent, per SKILL.md):** CMS National Coverage Policy citations (Title XVIII §1833(e) standalone statutory anchor when not in-rule, Pub 100-04 Ch 20 navigational reference); Article Text intro sentence ("The information in this article contains billing, coding or other guidelines that complement the LCD L38276" — navigational, the L38276 link is already on `gemi:a58075` via `gem:referencesPolicy`); empty-section markers (ICD-10-PCS Codes N/A, Additional ICD-10 Information N/A, Bill Type Codes N/A, Revenue Codes N/A, Other Coding Information N/A); Revision History R1-R9 (change-log artifacts); Associated Documents (the L38276 LCD reference is already a graph link; NCDs N/A); Statutory Requirements URLs / Rules and Regulations URLs / CMS Manual Explanations URLs / Other URLs (all N/A); Public Versions / Keywords (metadata); Copyright notices.

Single-domain policy (home oxygen therapy and oxygen equipment for hypoxemic patients); domain axis omitted per convention. NCD with detailed clinical-criteria sections (§B Group I 3 criteria, §B Group II 3 conditions, §C 4 non-covered indications) and MAC-discretion content (§D). Two project-wide methodology insights articulated during this pass — registered as skill-refinement carry-forwards for future SKILL.md codification: (1) the IF/THEN heuristic for rule-granularity decisions ("count the IF statements a downstream Python evaluator would generate from the source paragraph"); (2) the parallel-vs-sequential decision-shape distinction (parallel decisions share an outcome or framing across N rules; sequential decisions stand alone). Eight borderlines resolved: B1 = drop both credential-definitional sentences per corollary #2 (DME-not-qualified, hospital-exception); B2 = 2 rules (R5+R6) for time-of-need definition under shared-framing-plus-per-case-body decomposition; B3 = Option B per-item for 4 lists with intros absorbed where executability requires; B4 = 2 rules (R8+R9) for Group I sleep criterion under shared-outcome-plus-per-case-qualifying-tree decomposition; B5 = 1 rule (R10) for Group I exercise criterion (single qualifying scenario); B6 = 3 rules (R19+R20+R21) for §D MAC discretion paragraph under sequential-decision decomposition; B7 = 2 rules for §B testing-requirements paragraph (R2 = S1+S2; R3 = S3); B8 = 1 rule (R22) for §D portable-oxygen sentence (single IF with disjunctive outcome shapes). - **B1 = drop both credential-definitional sentences per corollary #2.** The §B sentences *"A durable medical equipment (DME) supplier is not considered a qualified provider or supplier of laboratory services for purposes of this National Coverage Determination (NCD)."* and *"This prohibition does not extend to the results of blood gas tests conducted by a hospital certified to do such tests."* are dropped — both are credential-definitional content already preserved on `gemi:credentialQualifiedLaboratoryProviderOrSupplier` and `gemi:credentialHospitalCertifiedForBloodGasTests` respectively. Precedent: NCD 210.10 (S56) dropped two §1833 credential-definition sentences for the same reason.
- **B2 = 2 rules under shared-framing-plus-per-case-body decomposition.** R5 and R6 each carry the same 2-sentence shared framing (the rule + general time-of-need definition) plus a distinct patient-class sub-case (inpatient vs. outpatient). Each rule is independently executable for its patient class — the definition is folded *into* the rule per corollary #1 (footnote-belongs-with-rule). New methodology pattern: "*shared framing + per-case body*" — articulated by Tom and named at B2.
- **B3 = Option B per-item with intros absorbed where executability requires.** Three of four lists absorb their intro into each item: Group II (PO2 range / SpO2 framing essential for executability), §C (non-coverage assertion essential), §D portable options (B8 — revised to single rule). Group I list intro drops (transitional label only; each criterion is self-contained). Single sentence per item for Group I/II; 2-sentence body (condition + rationale prose) for §C bullets 1-3 per corollary #3 (verbatim-capture; rationale prose stays with bullet).
- **B4 = 2 rules under shared-outcome-plus-per-case-qualifying-tree decomposition.** R8 (Statement A) and R9 (Statement B) each capture the shared outcome footer (Sentences 2 + 3 of the sleep bullet) verbatim including *"In either of these cases"*. The plural back-reference is preserved verbatim per corollary #3; the back-reference resolves correctly when both rules sit in the graph together (jigsaw-puzzle-piece principle in microcosm). Tomorrow's structured form (see `gem_structured_rule_guide.md`) will replace the discourse-level *"either"* with a structural link from both `gem:Rule` individuals to one shared `gem:CoverageOutcome`.
- **B5 = 1 rule for Group I exercise criterion.** One IF/THEN (single qualifying scenario + outcome conditional), one rule, multi-sentence body.
- **B6 = 3 rules under sequential-decision decomposition.** §D MAC discretion paragraph's three sentences are sequential decisions: initial discretion (R19), duration limit (R20), renewal eligibility (R21). Each is independently executable; no shared framing needs duplication. The B2 shared-framing pattern is for *parallel* sub-cases of one decision; sequential decisions stand alone. New methodology pattern: "*parallel-vs-sequential decision-shape distinction*" — articulated by Tom and named at B6.
- **B7 = 2 rules for §B testing-requirements paragraph.** R2 = S1 + S2 (rule + soft-expectation about typical form, Pattern 3); R3 = S3 (alternative test acceptance, Pattern 1). The "*Such a test is usually...*" soft framing in S2 stays with S1 per corollary #3 (adjacent contextual content); S3's "*however, is also acceptable...*" introduces an alternative test type with its own compound acceptance condition.
- **B8 = 1 rule for §D portable-oxygen sentence.** Revising B3's initial proposal: applying the IF/THEN heuristic (introduced at B4) reveals that *"either (1) by itself, or, (2) to use in addition to a stationary oxygen system"* is one IF with two coverage shapes, not two IFs. One rule, with the source's enumeration retained inside the verbatim string. In tomorrow's structured form, the two shapes will likely be modeled as alternative `gem:CoverageOutcome` shapes attached to one `gem:Rule`.
- **R12 "AVFL" and unbalanced parenthesis preserved verbatim per source PDF.** Source text reads *"(P wave greater than 3 mm in standard leads II, III, or AVFL;"* — no closing paren before the semicolon, and "AVFL" where the standard ECG lead name is "aVF". Most likely a PDF text-extraction artifact (closing `)` misread as `L`), but per project methodology (PDF is authoritative for verbatim), the rule string captures the PDF text exactly. Tom approved 2026-06-17: *"We'll follow the policy until someone corrects it."* The existing `gemi:groupII` description still has the corrected "AVF)" form (a pre-S48 paraphrasing artifact); discrepancy logged for future cleanup.
- **No clinical-concept mints.** Rule-description backfill scope only; the 40 existing `gem:ClinicalConcept` individuals on NCD 240.2 are reused via existing `gem:refersToClinicalConcept` triples. No new concepts (including no "time of need" concept) introduced.
- **Methodology drops (silent, per SKILL.md):** §A General descriptive prose ("oxygen can make meaningful contributions..." — not a rule); transitional labels ("Patients exhibiting hypoxemia are defined using the clinical criteria below:", "Group I:", "Group II:" standalone heading absorbed into rules per B3); §D metadata "(This NCD was last reviewed July 2022.)"; §D standalone navigational cross-reference "(See §280.1 and the Medicare Benefit Policy Manual, Chapter 15, 'Covered Medical and Other Health Services,' §110.)" — §280.1 is already a `gem:referencesPolicy` triple, Pub 100-02 Ch 15 added to worklist entry [11] discovered_in for `gemi:pub100_02_ch15`; Claims Processing Instructions / Transmittal Information / Revision History 1987-2022 / NCAs / Other Versions sections (administrative metadata, change-log artifacts, version history per SKILL.md §Three Code Contexts revision-history exclusion).

Notes:

- **No new axis-2 rule_type values.** All 42 rows use existing vocabulary: 10 distinct tags — coverage-scope, credentialed-actor, service-definition, service-standard, documentation, non-coverage, statutory-framing, concurrent-services, frequency, eligibility.
- **Scope-column form (A58075-style).** Following A58075 precedent (S63): cross-cutting rules captured once per Group scope per the verbatim-capture posture; the table preserves the source structure where the article restates identical documentation/denial language in each scope section. The 9 cross-cutting rules appear at both their General R-number (R17, R18, R20, R22, R26-R30) and their CTS R-number (R34, R35, R36, R37, R38-R42); cross-references inline in the Source/topic column.
- **Cycle-B migration scope.** Cycle B will mint `gemi:a54969_r1`/`_r2`/`_r3` and remove the 3 policy-level `gem:ruleDescription` triples. R4-R42 (Group-scope) remain as `gem:ruleDescription` triples on their respective `gem:PolicyGroup` subjects pending Phase 4. The migration stamp inserted in Cycle B will reference *"Policy-scope rules: `gemi:a54969_r1` – `gemi:a54969_r3`. R4-R42 (Group-scope) await Phase 4."* (A58075-stamp-form precedent).
- **R1–R3 `statutory-framing` per B2 principle.** Tag applied where a statute/regulation/transmittal is syntactic subject (R1 "42 CFR 410.32 indicates that"; R2 "PM B-01-28 sets forth") OR explicitly the legal framework being applied for a determination (R3 "within the meaning of §1862(a)(1)(A)" for the G0255 non-coverage determination relayed from NCD 160.23). Principle formalized this session: tag applies when statute/regulation/transmittal is syntactic subject of the rule sentence OR explicitly named as the legal framework being applied for a determination; does NOT apply when citation is supporting authority for a substantive criterion (precedents A52519 R4 + NCD 240.4.1 R1 vs L36524 R35 + A58075 R3).
- **R23 (discouraged-practices multi-bullet list).** Captured as one Pattern 3 rule per the graph state (`gemi:a54969_groupGeneralNCS_EMG` carries this as one `gem:ruleDescription` string). The L36524 companion-document precedent (R29-R34) split similar content into six per-item rules at extraction time; A54969's extraction captured it as one bulleted-paragraph rule. This is an extraction-layer granularity difference between companion documents, not a categorization-layer borderline — the categorization pass tags what is in the graph.
- **R25 (fragment-form rule).** *"Testing every beneficiary referred for pain."* is a noun phrase without a finite verb, mirroring how the source's discouraged-practice list captures single-noun-phrase items. Tagged `non-coverage` (the practice is discouraged → may be denied); not paired with `documentation` because the issue is over-testing, not missing documentation.
- **R26–R30 / R38–R42 (denial-trigger list).** Five fragment-style entries from a source "Reasons for denial" enumeration (5 unique × 2 Scopes = 10 rows; one of the 5, the F-wave/H-reflex/E&M-charges entry at R28/R40, packs three triggers into one sentence). Each tagged `non-coverage, documentation` because the trigger is a documentation failure that produces denial.
- **R13–R15 PT-supervision tags.** Tagged `credentialed-actor` (who can perform — PT vs physician) + `service-standard` (the 6A/7A regulatory designations are technical standards from the MPFS supervision framework). The PM B-01-28 framework introduction in policy-R2 establishes the umbrella; R13/R14/R15 attach the specific code designations.
- **R3 + R23 + R24 + R25 + R26–R30 / R38–R42 non-coverage spectrum.** A54969 carries 13 distinct `non-coverage`-tagged rules across all Scopes — the highest non-coverage share of any companion-article-style table to date (cf. L36524 with 10, A58075 with 0 at `non-coverage` tag despite ABN modifier denial rules). The high share reflects A54969's role as the coding/denial-criteria complement to L36524.
- **R31 frequency tag.** CTS-only 95905 rule carries *"payable only once per limb studied"* — a frequency limit alongside the service-definition content for CPT 95905. Tagged `frequency` accordingly.
- **R32 dual-polarity tagging.** CTS coverage rule (`eligibility` + `coverage-scope` for G56.01/02/03) plus explicit denial for other diagnoses (`non-coverage`). All three captured.
- **Methodology drops (silent, per SKILL.md):** §CMS National Coverage Policy URL citations (Pub 100-02 Ch 15 §80, Pub 100-04 Ch 12, Pub 100-08, 42 CFR 410.32 standalone — A54969's substantive 410.32 content lives in R1); CMS National Coverage Policy intro sentence; Article Text intro sentence (*"The information in this article contains billing, coding or other guidelines that complement L36524"* — navigational; L36524 link already on `gemi:a54969` via `gem:referencesPolicy`); empty-section markers; Revision History R1-R13 (change-log artifacts); Associated Documents (L36524/L35170/L35172/NCD 160.23/PM B-01-28/TN 2663 all already on `gemi:a54969` via `gem:referencesPolicy`); URL sections / Public Versions / Keywords / Copyright (metadata).
- **Ordering caveat.** Rule ordering within each Group reflects thematic grouping (coding → supervision → service-standards → documentation → frequency → coverage scope → non-coverage → denial triggers) rather than source-section order; the article PDF was not consulted during this categorization pass. Phase 4 migration may re-order to source-document order if desired; the R-number assignments are persistent for migration URI minting.

#### Notes

- **T1 (TOB lists) — three distinct sub-patterns applied.** Pure positive coverage list (R2: "only allow TOBs X/Y/Z") and additive coverage list (R40: "additionally allow RHC/FQHC TOBs") → `coverage-scope` + `procedural`. Negative-list-with-denial (R3, R46) → `non-coverage` + `procedural`. **Identification/classification rule** (R35, R36) → `procedural` alone, not `coverage-scope` — the rule classifies claim types for operational handling, not as positive coverage scope.
- **T2 (POS lists).** Positive (R49) → `setting-definition` + `coverage-scope`. Negative-with-denial (R50) → `setting-definition` + `non-coverage` + `procedural`. POS treated as a clinical setting indicator per the precedent in A52519 R2 (POS 31/32 nursing facility → `setting-definition`).
- **T3 (payment-method rules: R31, R41, R44, R45, R72).** All `procedural` per approval. Payment methodology — contractor-pricing, all-inclusive-rate, OPPS, reasonable-cost, 115%-MPFS — is a system instruction to contractors about how to compute reimbursement; not coverage-scope, not cost-sharing (the latter reserved for *patient* cost obligations like deductible/coinsurance).
- **T4 ("Effective for DOS" framings: R1, R26, R29, R31, R57, R60, R70).** None tagged `statutory-framing`. The "Effective for dates of service…" clause is a temporal modifier scoping when the substantive rule applies; it does not foreground a statute/regulation as subject, nor is it the legal framework being applied for a determination. Per S81 B2's "syntactic-subject or framework-being-applied" test, this fails both prongs. Likewise CR 7228 / TR 2148 cross-citations embedded in denial-message rules (R3, R23, R24, R28, R30, R37, R39, R46, R50) are supporting authority for a substantive procedure → not `statutory-framing`.
- **T5 (R59 provider-education publishing) → `procedural`.** Operational instruction to contractors about MLN Matters article publishing, with no documentation-of-claim semantics.
- **T6 (R6, R25, R69 explanatory "Contractors shall note").** All `procedural`. R6 borderline: also carries definitional content ("V74.5/V73.89 identifies tests as screening rather than diagnostic"); ruled `procedural`-only per T6 approval. Refinement option: add `definition` to R6 if a definitional reading is preferred.
- **Cardinality distribution (TN 2476):** 22 singles (30%) + 32 doubles (44%) + 17 triples (23%) + 2 quadruples (3%) = 73 rules / **145 `gem:ruleType` triples**. Skews higher-cardinality than the corpus average (corpus: 51% / 39% / 10% / 0.4%); the two quadruples (R70, R72) are composite Manual-paragraph rules combining 4 substantive criterion-types each. **No quintuples** — §4.19 unprecedented-cardinality threshold not crossed.
- **`statutory-framing` notably absent.** Despite the S81 expectation that TN 2476 would test the principle heavily, the result is clean: zero applications. All "Effective for DOS" framings and CR/TR cross-citations fail the syntactic-subject / framework-being-applied test under S81 B2. The principle held without modification.
- **R51 next-eligible-date — frequency tagging rationale.** The eligibility-date calculation underlies G0445 frequency enforcement (BR 04.15 frequency limits implemented via the next-eligible-date apparatus); tagged `procedural` (the calculation is a system instruction) + `frequency` (it operationalizes the frequency cap).
- **R29 / R72 / R45 NOTEs.** R29's "G0445 in Jan 2012 MPFSDB" and "TOS = 1" are auxiliary metadata embedded in the rule; tagged via the rule's substantive content (`coverage-scope` + `eligibility`) without adding `service-definition` for the metadata fragment. R72's distinct-dx E&M requirement contributes `documentation` to the composite tag set. R45's deductible/coinsurance sentence contributes `cost-sharing`.
- **Cross-references R25 ↔ R69.** Both rules carry the ICD-10 transition tracking content, R25 in the CR portion (BR 04.10-ish area) and R69 in the §170.2 Manual portion. Captured separately per the verbatim-preservation posture (each lives in a distinct source location).
- **Methodology drops (silent, per SKILL.md):** Effective Date / Implementation Date metadata; "Background" narrative section; Recurring Update Notification / "Make sure your billing staff are aware" guidance; MLN Matters article URL pattern in R59 navigational metadata; revision history; chapter-cross-reference navigational sentences; copyright.

#### Notes

- **Two new axis-2 rule_type values** introduced (added to the Axis 2 list above): `payment-rule` (B1 — dispensing-fee / payment-timing cluster) and `coding-correctness` (B2 — modifier and code-selection directives). The B2 investigation established that `procedural` is scoped to *program-administrative* process, not coding-correctness; A52519's anchor rule `gemi:a52519_a7047CodingRule_r1` (currently tagged `procedural` for a coding directive) is a candidate recategorization to `coding-correctness`, logged for a future pass.
- **B3** — the three JW/JZ scenarios (R33–R35) captured as Pattern 3 with their worked numeric examples retained verbatim (the rounding and overpayment specifics live only in the examples).
- **B4** — the generic 3-part coverage boilerplate, the Article/LCD scoping preamble, and the "refer to A55426" documentation pointer dropped as framing (corollary #1); the rule list begins at the first operative rule.
- **B5** — single-domain; domain axis omitted (consistent with the A52519 DMEPOS-article precedent).
- **R21 boundary** matches the A52519 R4 precedent — captured through "...which is periodically updated"; the broken "available here" navigational link dropped.
- **R26 (ensifentrine J7601)** — Pattern 3, the full nested criterion ("1 and either 2 or 3", with a/b and i–v sub-items) captured inline verbatim as a single rule per the IF/THEN heuristic (one Boolean expression: 1 AND (2 OR 3)); no δ-prefix scaffold, since the sub-items are not split into separate rules.
- **Chunk B (Coding Guidelines, R39–R68; originally R39–R80, added S90).** 30 rules — equipment/accessory/drug coding directives and service-definitions; no new schema. Distribution: service-definition 5, coding-correctness 27, non-coverage 8. *(Originally 42 rules / service-definition 17; 9 descriptor-redundant service-definition rules dropped in the S98 corpus review, 3 concept-redundant service-definition rules dropped in the S99 concept-path review.)*
- **B-B1 (revised S98 — HCPCS-descriptor corpus review; S99 — concept-path corollary #2 review).** The original ~17 "HCPCS code X describes/includes Y" `service-definition` captures (made S90 under the pre-extension "full verbatim lives nowhere else" rationale) were reviewed against the co-resident HCPCS `skos:prefLabel` descriptors under the S97-extended corollary #2. **9 pure device-identity definitions dropped** (the descriptor carries the identity, no rule-bearing increment): E0565, E0570, E0572, E0574, E0575, K0730 (EQUIP) and A7012, A7016, A4218 (ACC/DRUG). **S99 concept-path follow-up:** the 4 concept-only definitions left untouched at S98 (no single HCPCS code, governed by the *original* `gem:ClinicalConcept` corollary #2) were reviewed — **3 dropped** after extending their concept descriptions to full verbatim: old R49 → `conceptCompoundedInhalationSolution`, old R54 → `conceptUnitDoseForm`, old R55 → `conceptConcentratedForm`; **R39 retained** (two-device framing — no single concept is its definition home; the "two types are X and Y" partition is emergent across `conceptNebulization` / `conceptPneumaticCompressorNebulizer` / `conceptUltrasonicOrElectronicNebulizer`, not a discrete fact on any one concept; corollary #3 verbatim-capture posture). **5 retained overall:** R43/R44 (A7003-6 / A7004 unit-of-service composition + A7006/A7004 code-selection), R45/R48 (E0585/E0580 coding directives, dual-typed `coding-correctness`), and R39 (two-device framing).
- **B-B2** — three framing/navigational sentences dropped (the J-code/NCPDP scoping preamble, the two "contact PDAC contractor" pointers, and the "following is guidance" list intro), parallel to the B4 A55426-pointer precedent.
- **Granularity (Chunk B)** — the E0585/A7007/A7017/E0580 paragraph splits into R45–R48; the KO/KP/KQ paragraph into R56 (requirement + invalid-code denial) and R57 (concentrated-form exclusion). Worked examples retained verbatim inside R53, R61, R62 (B3 posture). *(Rule numbers reflect the S98 and S99 renumbers; pre-S98 these were R53–R56, R67/R68, R64/R72/R73.)*
- **Inter-rule formatting** — A52466's rule individuals (R1–R68; R1–R80 before the S98/S99 drops) normalized to blank-line separation to match corpus style (Chunk A had written R1–R38 without blank-line separators).
- **Chunk C (anchor-scope review across the 16 PolicyGroups, S91).** 0 rules. A52466's Coding Information section is entirely already-modeled structure: the per-Group ICD closed-lists (16 PolicyGroups, `gem:exclusivelyCoversCondition`) and the "DO NOT Support Medical Necessity" blanket denial (35 HCPCS → policy-level `gem:excludesProcedure`, all 35 verified present in the graph). Only two prose paragraphs exist in the section and neither is a rule under the IF/THEN test: (1) the Support-section Group 1 Paragraph boilerplate ("The presence of an ICD-10 code listed in this section is not sufficient by itself to assure coverage. Refer to the LCD section…") restates the closed-list semantics already carried by the structure — a listed ICD earns coverage unless an explicit denial elsewhere overrides that specific result (the downstream "denial overrides approval" resolution); (2) the DO-NOT Group 1 Paragraph's three statements are the implicit per-Group ICD complement, the 35-HCPCS blanket denial (already `gem:excludesProcedure`), and the open-world default — none claim-evaluable beyond the existing triples. Groups 2–16 carry **no** Group-Paragraph narrative (anchor line + code table only). No `CODING GUIDELINES:` content blocks exist in the section; the `CODING GUIDELINES:` strings near source line 6125+ are Revision-History-Explanation sub-headings (change-log entries), not policy content. Completes A52466's rule backfill — 68 policy-scope rules (Chunks A+B; 80 at S91; 9 descriptor-redundant service-definition rules dropped S98, 3 concept-redundant service-definition rules dropped S99), 0 anchor-scope rules (Chunk C).

### L33797 — Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment

*Migrated S92 (2026-06-26). `gemi:lcd33797_r1` – `gemi:lcd33797_r54`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-06-26 (Session 92). 54 rules, all at policy level (no anchored coding scopes). Single-domain policy (home oxygen therapy and oxygen equipment); domain axis omitted per convention. Direct-to-`gem:PolicyRule` authoring (fresh mint of `gemi:lcd33797_r1`–`r54`) onto an already-extracted `planDone` policy that carried zero rule coverage. L33797 operationalizes NCD 240.2; the parent NCD (22 rules, S64/S77) and L33612 (DMEPOS GENERAL boilerplate — SWO/WOPD/correct-coding/POD, S59/S75) served as templates. No new axis-2 `rule_type` values introduced; 9 distinct tags used (96 `gem:ruleType` triples): coding-correctness, coverage-scope, credentialed-actor, documentation, eligibility, frequency, non-coverage, payment-rule, service-standard. First multi-borderline stress-test of the S91 record-and-proceed factored decision-tree process; all borderlines confirmed by Tom in one batch.

#### Notes

- **All rules on policy level.** `gemi:lcd33797` has no anchored coding scopes. Its Coding-Information "Group 1/Group 2" are equipment/accessory HCPCS code lists (already the 40 `gem:coversProcedure`), not HCPCS-anchored ICD closed-lists — ICD-10 codes were relocated to Policy Article A52514 in revision R6. No "For HCPCS codes X:" anchors → no `gem:PolicyGroup`; no anchored coding-correctness prose → no `gem:PolicyCodingRule`. Groups I–IV are `gem:QualificationGroup` individuals (out of the `gem:ruleDescription` domain `gem:CMSpolicy ∪ gem:AnchoredCodingScope`), so their criteria rules live on the policy — same disposition as NCD 240.2's groupI/groupII.
- **DP-A = drop the generic three-prong test.** "For any item to be covered by Medicare, it must 1) be eligible for a defined Medicare benefit category, 2) be reasonable and necessary…, and 3) meet all other applicable Medicare statutory and regulatory requirements." dropped — zero precedent corpus-wide (verified), generic Medicare-wide program framing; the R&N standard is operationalized by the Group I–IV rules. (Parallel to A52466 B4.)
- **DP-B = drop credential-definitional supplier/hospital sentences; capture the operative prohibition.** "A supplier is not considered a qualified provider or a qualified laboratory…" and "These prohibitions do not extend to blood gas studies performed by a hospital certified…" dropped per corollary #2 — both preserved verbatim on `gemi:credentialQualifiedLaboratoryProviderOrSupplier` and `gemi:credentialHospitalCertifiedForBloodGasTests` respectively (exactly NCD 240.2 B1). R19 ("Blood gas studies performed by a supplier are not acceptable. In addition, the qualifying blood gas study may not be paid for by any supplier.") **captured** — operative prohibition not preserved on any credential (`gemi:credentialDMESupplier`'s description carries A52467 home-sleep-test text, not this).
- **DP-C = conjunctive multi-condition gates → one rule each.** R2 (4-condition initial-coverage gate), R28 (3-condition IDTF self-administration delivery gate), R35 (titration-PSG criteria) each captured as one Pattern-3 rule: "all of the following" = one IF under the IF/THEN heuristic; the A./B. internal OR inside R35 criterion 2 stays in-rule. OR-joined *alternative* qualifying paths do fork (Group I 4 criteria → R5–R8; Group II 3 B-conditions → R9–R11; Group IV 4 denials → R14–R17).
- **DP-D = drop the overnight-oximetry restatement.** The p11 sentence "Overnight oximetry performed as part of home sleep testing or as part of any other home testing is not considered as eligible… (see the 'Overnight Oximetry Studies' section above…)" dropped as a near-duplicate of R27's second sentence with an explicit navigational back-reference; no operative content beyond R27.
- **DP-E = drop definitions preserved on existing concepts.** The "blood gas study refers to…", TESTING-SPECIFICATIONS "Blood gas study/Oximetry/Overnight oximetry shall refer to…", "Baseline saturation is defined as…", and the APPENDICES blood-gas-study definition dropped per corollary #2 — content preserved on `gemi:conceptBloodGasStudy`, `conceptOximetryTest`, `conceptOvernightOximetry`, `conceptBaselineSaturation`, `conceptArterialBloodGasStudy`. Operative parts kept where they recur (R26 2-hour minimum; R27/R31 overnight exclusions).
- **DP-F = OSA "treated" (R33) and "unmasked" (R34) captured as two distinct rules.** R34 materially elaborates R33: adds the unmasking mechanism, specifies polysomnography, and adds "must be demonstrated before…" — a distinct evaluator criterion per the verbatim-capture posture (corollary #3).
- **DP-G = liter flow >4 LPM → one rule (R42).** Higher-allowance trigger + the ≥4-LPM qualifying-study requirement + the not-met payment-limit fallback are one criterion with its denial-complement (L33612 R1 coverage+denial-as-one-rule convention).
- **DP-H = exercise testing → R23 (protocol) + R24 (recovery).** R23 captures the full exercise-oximetry protocol paragraph (3-study documentation list + same-session + in-person credentialed-actor + only-#2-qualifies + available-on-request) as one Pattern-3 rule; splitting the mid-paragraph in-person sentence out would force a non-contiguous verbatim. R24 = "recovery" testing not valid.
- **DP-I = drop the Associated-Information DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS block.** §1833(e) statutory framing (corollary #1) + the generic "medical records will reflect the need… available upon request" recap + GENERAL/POLICY-SPECIFIC navigational pointers to A55426/A52514 + the APPENDICES definition (DP-E) + the UTILIZATION GUIDELINES "Refer to CILMN" pointer all dropped. The substantive DMEPOS documentation rules (SWO/WOPD/correct-coding/POD) are already captured as R50–R54 from the GENERAL section.
- **R36/R37 split.** Concurrent-use eligibility (R36 — meet all other oxygen requirements) and the sleep-test-only → stationary-only equipment limitation (R37) are distinct decisions, captured as two rules.
- **Group III methodologic NOTE dropped.** The "DME MACs use the same methodologic principles of evidentiary review… see Appendix A of the NCA Decision Memo… CAG-00296R2" NOTE dropped as procedural/methodological framing + navigational. (CAG-00296R2/R3 are not among L33797's 9 existing references — the original extraction's reference web; re-opening it is out of rule-backfill scope.)
- **"AVF)" captured as-is.** L33797's Group II B2 source reads "…II, III, or AVF);" — correctly balanced, unlike NCD 240.2 R12's "AVFL" OCR artifact. R10 captures "AVF)".
- **No clinical-concept / credential / reference / schema mints.** Pure rule backfill on the existing `gemi:lcd33797` entity; the 56 clinical concepts, 9 credentials, 9 references, 4 QualificationGroups, and all policy metadata are reused unchanged.

Its Coding-Information Group 1/Group 2 are equipment/accessory HCPCS lists (already the 22 `gem:coversProcedure` + 3 `gem:excludesProcedure`), not HCPCS-anchored ICD closed-lists — ICD-10 fields were removed in R7 (2020-01-01) and live in companion Policy Article A52517. No "For HCPCS codes X:" anchors → no `gem:PolicyGroup`; no anchored coding-correctness prose → no `gem:PolicyCodingRule`. The named clinical-disorder scenarios (Restrictive Thoracic Disorders, CSA/CompSA, Hypoventilation Syndrome, CRF-COPD) are prose coverage criteria → policy-level rules. Same disposition as L33797.
- **DP1 = drop the CILMN opening.** The generic three-prong test ("For any item to be covered by Medicare, it must 1)…2)…3)…") dropped — zero precedent corpus-wide (= L33797 DP-A, A52466 B4). The §1862(a)(1)(A) purpose/framing sentences (corollary #1) and the "other payment rules…discussed in the following documents…Refer to the Supplier Manual / DME MAC web sites" navigational pointers dropped. **No master R1 synthesized from the CILMN** — the master coverage rule is the operative R2 ("A RAD (E0470, E0471) is covered for those beneficiaries with one of the following clinical disorders…").
- **DP2 = drop DEFINITIONS pure definitions (corollary #2 / L33797 DP-E).** FIO2, FEV1, FVC, CSA, CompSA, Apnea, Hypopnea, AHI, CAHI definitional sentences dropped — not evaluator criteria, and each is preserved verbatim on its `gem:ClinicalConcept` description (most introduced by L33800 itself; verified at Plan time). The two *operative* DEFINITIONS sentences kept: R3 (AHI/CAHI <2-hour validity, parallels L33797 R26) and R4 (discontinuation → stop billing). Navigational "See the Sleep Tests section below…" dropped.
- **DP3 = named-disorder conjunctive gates → one rule each (DP-C).** R5 (Restrictive Thoracic A–C), R6 (CSA/CompSA PSG A–B), R7 (Hypoventilation E0470), R8 (Hypoventilation E0471): "all of the following" = one IF under the IF/THEN heuristic; internal `OR` (B's a/b/c; the C-or-D alternation) stays in-rule. Each gate folds its criteria + covered-for-first-3-months outcome + denial complement into one rule (L33612 R1 / L33797 R42 coverage+denial convention). R9 = CRF-COPD cross-reference to NCD 240.9 (corollary #4).
- **DP4 = Ventilators framing dropped; operative content captured.** The "Section 240.9 outlines initial and continuing usage criteria…" framing lead-in and the "Each of these disease categories…overlap conditions…will vary as well" explanatory framing dropped. Captured: R10 (NCD 280.1 coverage quote), R11 (treatment-plan choice + claim-review documentation), R12 (FSS exclusion + ventilator-not-eligible denial), R13 (incorrect-coding denial).
- **DP-FSS = one cohesive rule (R12).** The FSS paragraph (payment-category exclusion + ventilator-reimbursement-ineligibility denial, with the in-rule statute `(Social Security Act 1834(a)(3)(A))` kept per corollary #3) captured as one Pattern-3 rule — same subject (ventilators delivering PAP), one cohesive source paragraph (L33797 R43 payment+denial-as-one-rule precedent). A strict IF/THEN reading could fork it into 2 (payment-category vs R&N-denial); the cohesive-paragraph reading was confirmed.
- **DP-accessories = one cohesive table rule (R19).** The usual-maximum-amount table (15 codes) + the single "billing greater than usual maximum → denied" sentence captured as one frequency/non-coverage rule, with the per-code amounts inline. The per-code amounts are data the one denial rule references; 15 per-code Pattern-2 rules (strict IF/THEN reading) deferred — when structured frequency triples are eventually adopted (deferred proposal), the per-code data migrates there rather than into 15 rule strings. Confirmed.
- **GENERAL (R21–R25) + REFILL (R26–R32) follow L33612 verbatim-precedent.** Identical shared DMEPOS boilerplate; per-sentence decomposition matched to L33612 R20–R31 sentence boundaries. R22 keeps its extra "Refer to the LCD-related Policy Article…" sentence per corollary #4. R32 captures L33800's "three (3) - month" verbatim (L33612 R31 used "3-month").
- **DP-borderlines confirmed (capture/drop).** R40 captured (Miscellaneous treating-practitioner-statement retention — a distinct records-retention rule, no L33797 precedent either way); the rest of the Associated-Information DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS block dropped (§1833(e) framing + generic recap + GENERAL/POLICY-SPECIFIC navigational pointers to A55426/A52517 + APPENDICES/UTILIZATION "Refer to CILMN" = L33797 DP-I; substantive doc rules already R21–R25). Sleep-Tests para-1 navigational sourcing pointer dropped (operative rules R38/R39). Replacement section-scope sentence + Supplier-Manual navigational pointer dropped (R33/R34 self-contained). Coding-Information Group 1 disclaimer ("The appearance of a code in this section does not necessarily indicate coverage") and the bare HCPCS modifier definitions (EY/GA/GZ/KX) dropped — modifier definitions preserved on the modifier individuals; L33797 captured 0 modifier-definition rules from its 16 modifiers.
- **No clinical-concept / credential / reference / schema mints.** Pure rule backfill on the existing `gemi:lcd33800` entity; the 70 clinical concepts, 4 credentials, 7 references, 22 coversProcedure / 3 excludesProcedure, 4 modifiers, and all policy metadata are reused unchanged.

### L33718 — Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea

*Migrated S94 (2026-06-26). `gemi:lcd33718_r1` – `gemi:lcd33718_r42`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-06-26 (Session 94). 42 rules, all at policy level (no anchored coding scopes). Single-domain policy (PAP devices — CPAP/bi-level for obstructive sleep apnea); domain axis omitted per convention. Direct-to-`gem:PolicyRule` authoring (fresh mint of `gemi:lcd33718_r1`–`r42`) onto an already-extracted `planDone` policy that carried zero rule coverage. L33718 is the OSA/PAP sister LCD to L33800 (RAD, S93) and L33797 (oxygen, S92) within the same DME MAC family; L33800 (S93) and L33612 (DMEPOS GENERAL/REFILL boilerplate, S59/S75) served as the immediate templates. The companion Policy Article A52467 carries the ICD-10 diagnosis lists (relocated from this LCD in R6, 2019-01-01); the concurrent-oxygen section cross-references the Oxygen LCD (`lcd33797`). No new axis-2 `rule_type` values introduced; 8 distinct tags used (94 `gem:ruleType` triples): coverage-scope, credentialed-actor, documentation, eligibility, frequency, non-coverage, payment-rule, service-standard (no coding-correctness — L33718 has no ventilator-miscoding rule). Third consecutive DME MAC sister-LCD backfill under the S91 record-and-proceed factored decision-tree process; all decision points confirmed by Tom in one batch.

| Rule | Source / topic | Pattern | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | :--- |
| R1 | §Definitions (operative): AHI/RDI calculated on <2 hrs sleep/recording requires ≥30 events (no symptoms) or ≥10 events (with symptoms) — 2-hour-equivalent validity | 1 | eligibility, service-standard |
| R2 | §Initial Coverage (E0601): A–C conjunctive gate (A in-person clinical evaluation by treating practitioner pre-sleep-test; B sleep test AHI/RDI≥15 w/ ≥30 events, or AHI/RDI 5–14 w/ ≥10 events + symptom/comorbidity documentation; C supplier instruction) → covered for OSA; not met → denied | 3 | coverage-scope, credentialed-actor, documentation, eligibility |
| R3 | §Initial Coverage (E0470): criteria A–C plus D (E0601 tried and proven ineffective on facility/home therapeutic trial; "ineffective" = documented failure to meet therapeutic goals despite optimal therapy) → covered; not met → denied | 3 | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R4 | §Initial Coverage (E0471): bi-level with back-up rate not R&N if primary diagnosis is OSA; billed with OSA dx → denied | 1 | coverage-scope, non-coverage |
| R5 | §Initial Coverage: E0601 ineffective during initial titration/home trial → substitution of E0470 requires no new initial in-person clinical evaluation or sleep test | 1 | documentation, eligibility |
| R6 | §Initial Coverage: E0601 used >3 months then switched to E0470 → new initial in-person clinical evaluation required (no new sleep test); new 3-month trial begins | 1 | documentation, eligibility |
| R7 | §Sleep Tests: sleep test must be facility-based polysomnogram (Type I) or inpatient/home-based sleep test (HST) (Types II, III, IV, Other) | 1 | eligibility, service-standard |
| R8 | §Sleep Tests: PAP coverage for OSA limited to claims where OSA diagnosis based on all 5 (valid test per NCD 240.4.1; FDA-approved diagnostic device; results meet current criteria; ordered by treating practitioner; conducted by qualified Medicare sleep-test provider) | 3 | credentialed-actor, documentation, eligibility, service-standard |
| R9 | §Continued Coverage >3 months: 31st–91st-day clinical re-evaluation by treating practitioner documenting benefit from PAP therapy required for continued coverage | 3 | coverage-scope, credentialed-actor, documentation, eligibility |
| R10 | §Continued Coverage >3 months (DOS ≥ Nov 1, 2008): clinical benefit demonstrated by (1) in-person re-evaluation documenting OSA symptom improvement and (2) objective adherence evidence reviewed by treating practitioner | 3 | credentialed-actor, documentation, eligibility |
| R11 | §Continued Coverage >3 months (operative): adherence defined as PAP use ≥4 hrs/night on 70% of nights during a consecutive 30-day period within first 3 months | 1 | eligibility, service-standard |
| R12 | §Continued Coverage >3 months: criteria not met → continued coverage of PAP device + related accessories denied | 1 | non-coverage |
| R13 | §Continued Coverage >3 months: re-evaluation after 91st day demonstrating benefit (criteria 1 and 2) → continued coverage commences with date of that re-evaluation | 1 | coverage-scope, credentialed-actor, eligibility |
| R14 | §Continued Coverage >3 months: beneficiaries failing initial 12-week trial may re-qualify only with both (1) in-person re-evaluation to determine failure etiology and (2) repeat facility-based (Type 1) sleep test (diagnostic/titration/split-night) | 3 | credentialed-actor, eligibility, service-standard |
| R15 | §Continued Coverage >3 months: E0601 ineffective on trial → E0470 substitution does not change trial length unless <30 days remain; >30 days → re-eval 31st–91st day + adherence doc before 91st day from E0601 start; <30 days → re-eval + adherence doc before 120th day from E0601 start | 3 | documentation, eligibility, service-standard |
| R16 | §Continued Coverage >3 months: E0601 used >3 months then switched to E0470 → re-evaluation 31st–91st day from E0470 initiation + adherence documentation during the 3-month E0470 trial | 1 | documentation, eligibility |
| R17 | §Continued Coverage >3 months: discontinuation of PAP usage at any time → supplier ascertains + stops billing equipment and related accessories/supplies | 1 | non-coverage, service-standard |
| R18 | §Continued Coverage >3 months: PAP device dispensed before Nov 1, 2008 meeting then-current initial + post-3-month criteria → continues covered for DOS on/after Nov 1, 2008 while beneficiary continues use | 1 | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R19 | §Concurrent Oxygen: simultaneous oxygen + PAP coverage requires all CILMN requirements of BOTH the Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment LCD and this PAP LCD be met | 1 | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R20 | §Concurrent Oxygen: OSA must be sufficiently treated so the underlying condition causing hypoxemia is unmasked, demonstrated before PSG oxygen-saturation results qualify for oxygen therapy/equipment | 3 | coverage-scope, eligibility, service-standard |
| R21 | §Concurrent Oxygen: qualifying oxygen-saturation test may occur only during a titration PSG (split-night or stand-alone) meeting all 4 (≥2-hr titration; AHI/RDI reduced to ≤10/hr or further reduced; nocturnal oximetry only after optimal PAP settings; SpO2 ≤88%) | 3 | eligibility, service-standard |
| R22 | §Concurrent Oxygen: beneficiary must meet all other oxygen-coverage requirements; those qualifying via sleep-test-only testing are eligible only for stationary equipment reimbursement | 3 | coverage-scope, eligibility, payment-rule |
| R23 | §Concurrent Oxygen: overnight oximetry from home sleep testing or any other home testing not eligible for home oxygen/equipment qualification | 1 | non-coverage, service-standard |
| R24 | §Replacement: PAP device replaced within 5-yr RUL (loss/theft/irreparable damage) → no new clinical evaluation, sleep test, or trial period | 1 | documentation, eligibility |
| R25 | §Replacement: PAP device replaced after 5-yr RUL → in-person treating-practitioner evaluation documenting continued use/benefit; no new sleep test or trial period | 3 | credentialed-actor, documentation, eligibility |
| R26 | §Beneficiaries Entering Medicare: pre-FFS-enrollment PAP recipients seeking rental/replacement/accessories must meet both (1) documented pre-enrollment sleep test meeting current AHI/RDI criteria and (2) post-enrollment in-person evaluation documenting OSA diagnosis + continued use; either not met → denied | 3 | credentialed-actor, documentation, eligibility |
| R27 | §Beneficiaries Entering Medicare: in these situations no clinical re-evaluation or objective adherence documentation is required | 1 | documentation, eligibility |
| R28 | §Accessories: accessories covered when device coverage criteria met; criteria not met → accessories denied | 1 | coverage-scope, eligibility, non-coverage |
| R29 | §Accessories: usual-maximum-amount table (15 HCPCS codes, per-code N-per-M-months) + quantities greater than usual maximum → denied | 3 | frequency, non-coverage |
| R30 | §General: SWO communicated before claim; billing without completed SWO → denied | 1 | documentation, non-coverage |
| R31 | §General: WOPD for DMEPOS base items; delivery without WOPD → denied (+ Policy Article pointer) | 3 | documentation, non-coverage |
| R32 | §General: WOPD listing base item for separately-billed accessories/supplies; missing → denied | 3 | documentation, non-coverage |
| R33 | §General: correct-coding requirement (CMS HCPCS / LCDs / Policy Articles / DME MAC articles); non-compliant → denied/incorrectly coded | 1 | documentation, non-coverage, service-standard |
| R34 | §General: Proof of Delivery (POD) supplier standard; available to contractor on request; missing → denied | 3 | documentation, non-coverage |
| R35 | §Refill: recurring DMEPOS billing must be prospective, not retrospective | 1 | documentation |
| R36 | §Refill: contact beneficiary + document affirmative response before dispensing refill (17 HCPCS codes listed inline); not auto-ship; ensures continued R&N | 3 | documentation |
| R37 | §Refill: contact no sooner than 30 calendar days prior to expected end of current supply | 1 | documentation |
| R38 | §Refill: deliver no sooner than 10 calendar days prior to expected end of current supply (any delivery method) | 3 | documentation |
| R39 | §Refill: refill request + affirmative response required before new supply; items without valid documented refill request → denied | 3 | documentation, non-coverage |
| R40 | §Refill: must not dispense exceeding expected utilization; monitor atypical patterns; verify with treating practitioners | 3 | credentialed-actor, documentation |
| R41 | §Refill: regardless of utilization, must not dispense more than a three (3)-month quantity at a time | 1 | frequency |
| R42 | §Refill: non-heated (E0561) or heated (E0562) humidifier covered when ordered by treating practitioner for covered PAP (E0470/E0601) device | 1 | coverage-scope, credentialed-actor |

#### Notes

- **All rules on policy level.** `gemi:lcd33718` has no anchored coding scopes and no `gem:QualificationGroup` individuals. Its Coding-Information Group 1 (E0470/E0471/E0601) and Group 2 (accessories) are equipment/accessory HCPCS lists (already the 21 `gem:coversProcedure` + 1 `gem:excludesProcedure` E0471), not HCPCS-anchored ICD closed-lists — the ICD-10 fields were relocated to companion Policy Article A52467 in R6 (2019-01-01) and removed from the coding section in R7. No "For HCPCS codes X:" anchors → no `gem:PolicyGroup`; no anchored coding-correctness prose → no `gem:PolicyCodingRule`. The E0601/E0470/E0471 coverage tiers are prose coverage criteria → policy-level rules. Same disposition as L33797/L33800.
- **D1 = drop the CILMN opening.** The generic three-prong test ("For any item to be covered by Medicare, it must 1)…2)…3)…") dropped — zero precedent corpus-wide (= L33797 DP-A, L33800 DP1). The §1862(a)(1)(A) purpose/framing sentences (corollary #1) and the "other payment rules…discussed in the following documents…Refer to the Supplier Manual / DME MAC web sites" navigational pointers dropped. **No master rule synthesized from the CILMN** — the operative master coverage rules are R2 (E0601 gate) and R3 (E0470 gate).
- **D2 = drop DEFINITIONS pure definitions (corollary #2 / L33797 DP-E / L33800 DP2).** Apnea, Hypopnea, AHI, RDI, and RERA definitional sentences dropped — not evaluator criteria, and each is preserved verbatim on its `gem:ClinicalConcept` description (most introduced by L33718 itself; verified at Plan time). The AHI definition's "Sleep time can only be measured in a Type I or Type II sleep study" sub-clause is preserved on `gemi:conceptApneaHypopneaIndex` and dropped here. The one *operative* DEFINITIONS sentence kept: R1 (AHI/RDI <2-hour validity, parallels L33800 R3 / L33797 R26).
- **D3 = drop the "PAP device" term-scope definition** (genuine-tie borderline, lean-drop confirmed). "In this policy, the term PAP device will refer to both E0601 and E0470 when used for OSA" is definitional and load-bearing only via the inline parentheticals that subsequent rules already carry (e.g. R9 "a PAP device (E0470 or E0601)"); capturing it would add no IF a downstream evaluator generates.
- **D4 = drop the non-OSA scope-exclusion pointer** (genuine-tie borderline, confirmed). "Coverage…for the use of E0470 and E0471 for diagnoses other than OSA are addressed in the Respiratory Assist Devices (RAD) LCD and related PA" is a navigational scope-boundary pointer, not denial language; the RAD LCD (`gemi:lcd33800`) is already a `gem:referencesPolicy` target.
- **G1 = R10 / R11 kept as two rules** (genuine tie, lean-split confirmed). R10 (clinical-benefit demonstrated by criteria 1 and 2) and R11 (the numeric adherence threshold, ≥4 hrs/night on 70% of nights over 30 days) are distinct testable facts; R11 is a standalone operative threshold like L33800 R3, not mere elaboration of R10's criterion 2 (parallels the L33800 R15/R16 separation).
- **G2 = R12 denial complement kept separate** (genuine tie, confirmed). "If the above criteria are not met, continued coverage…denied" follows the multi-sentence continued-coverage requirement block (R9–R11) and stands alone, mirroring L33800 R17.
- **G3 = R22 as one cohesive rule** (genuine tie, confirmed). The all-other-oxygen-requirements clause + the sleep-test-only → stationary-equipment-only payment limitation share one subject (oxygen-with-PAP eligibility/payment) and are captured together; a strict IF/THEN reading could fork the payment limitation into its own rule.
- **G4 = R26 entering-Medicare denial folded into the gate** (genuine tie, confirmed). "If either criteria 1 or 2 above are not met, the claim will be denied" folds into R26 as a self-contained "both must be met / else denied" gate, per the L33800 R5–R8 named-disorder-gate convention.
- **G5 = R27 carve-out kept separate** (genuine tie, confirmed). "In these situations, there is no requirement for a clinical re-evaluation or…adherence" is a distinct exemption clause for the entering-Medicare cohort, not part of the R26 coverage gate.
- **G6 = R15 substitution trial-timing as one rule** (genuine tie, confirmed). The single E0601→E0470 substitution scenario with its >30-day / <30-day conditional fork is captured as one rule with the fork in-rule; a strict reading could split the two forks.
- **G7 = DP-accessories: one cohesive table rule (R29).** The usual-maximum-amount table (15 codes) + the single "quantities greater than usual maximum → denied" sentence captured as one frequency/non-coverage rule with the per-code amounts inline (L33800 R19 precedent). The 15 per-code Pattern-2 rules (strict IF/THEN reading) are deferred — when structured frequency triples are adopted (deferred proposal), the per-code data migrates there rather than into 15 rule strings.
- **D5 = drop the Associated-Information documentation block.** §1833(e) framing + the GENERAL DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS recap list (SWO/Medical Record/Correct Coding/POD/Refill, all already substantive rules R30–R34/R35–R41) + the POLICY-SPECIFIC navigational pointer to A52467 + UTILIZATION "Refer to CILMN" dropped (= L33797 DP-I / L33800 DP-MISC). **No L33800-R40-equivalent records-retention rule exists in L33718** — L33800 R40 captured the RAD-specific 61-day treating-practitioner-statement retention, which L33718 does not contain.
- **D6 = drop the Epworth Sleepiness Scale appendix.** Appendix A is an informational assessment instrument reprinted with permission; no coverage criterion cites an Epworth cutoff (criterion B.2.a names "excessive daytime sleepiness" without a score threshold). `gemi:conceptEpworthSleepinessScale` already exists.
- **D7 = drop Coding-Information Group-1 disclaimer + bare modifier definitions.** "The appearance of a code in this section does not necessarily indicate coverage" and the EY/GA/GZ/KX HCPCS modifier definitions dropped — modifier definitions preserved on the modifier individuals; L33797/L33800 captured 0 modifier-definition rules.
- **GENERAL (R30–R34) + REFILL (R35–R41) follow L33800/L33612 verbatim-precedent.** Identical shared DMEPOS boilerplate; per-sentence decomposition matched to L33800 R21–R32 sentence boundaries. R31 keeps its extra "Refer to the LCD-related Policy Article…" sentence per corollary #4. **Two verbatim differences from L33800:** R36 carries the inline 17-HCPCS refill code list (A4604, A7027–A7039, A7044–A7046) which L33800 R27 omits; and R42 humidifier reads "covered when ordered" with **no "paid separately"** (→ no payment-rule tag, unlike L33800 R20 which is coverage-scope/credentialed-actor/payment-rule).
- **No clinical-concept / credential / reference / schema mints.** Pure rule backfill on the existing `gemi:lcd33718` entity; the 53 clinical concepts, 4 credentials, 9 references, 21 coversProcedure / 1 excludesProcedure, 4 modifiers, and all policy metadata are reused unchanged. policy_worklist.json unchanged (already current).

### A52492 — Tracheostomy Care Supplies - Policy Article

Direct-to-`gem:PolicyRule` authoring (no intermediate `gem:ruleDescription`-string stage) on the already-extracted `planDone` policy (zero prior rule coverage). #### Notes

- **Single-domain** (tracheostomy care supplies); domain axis omitted (= A52466 / A52519 DMEPOS-article precedent). Closest precedent A52466 (Nebulizers Article, S90).
- **B1 = drop coverage-preamble in full** (= A52466 B4). Generic three-prong test (D1), the §1862(a)(1)(A) scoping sentence (D2), and the Prosthetic-Benefit preamble (D3) dropped as framing (corollary #1). The one arguable piece — "the reasonable and necessary (R&N) requirements set out in the related Local Coverage Determination must be met" — is already encoded by `gem:referencesPolicy gemi:lcd33832`; no synthesized rule.
- **B2 = descriptor-definition cluster: corollary #2 DROP, with B-B1 exceptions (revised S98).** Diverges from A52466. A52466 originally captured ~17 descriptor sentences as `service-definition` rules *because its concepts carried only truncated `…`-snippets*; A52492's concept individuals already carry the **full verbatim** of the HME/valve/tube/kit descriptors, so corollary #2 bites and 9 descriptor definitions are dropped (D6–D16: A4625/A4629 kit contents, A7526 definition, HME-general, HME-composition, A7503, A7506, A7507, A7508, A7509, A7501). The two descriptors originally captured per B-B1 were re-reviewed in the S98 HCPCS-descriptor corpus pass: **A7504 (old R19) dropped** — pure code-identity ("filter that fits into A7503"), redundant with the `hcpcs:` descriptor; **A4481 (R17) retained** — "It is not an HME" is a code-selection distinction beyond the descriptor. Net `service-definition` rules = **2 (R17/R18)** vs A52466's 8 (post-S98).
- **B2 directive-bearing exceptions.** Three descriptor sentences carry embedded coding directives and are captured for the directive regardless of concept overlap: A4483 "should not be billed as an HME over a tracheostoma" (R18, service-definition + coding-correctness), A7526 "should not be used for billing twill ties…" (R16, coding-correctness — the A7526 *definition* itself dropped to `gemi:conceptTracheostomyCollarOrHolder`), and tracheostomy-tubes "all-inclusive" (R19, coding-correctness + coverage-scope — a bundling directive, not a pure definition).
- **B3 = AU-modifier granularity: 3 rules.** R4 (Article-Text denial framing, "rejected as missing information") and R14 (Coding-Guidelines requirement framing, "must be billed with the AU modifier") are restatements with material framing differences (corollary #3 → keep both); R15 is the distinct exclusivity directive ("the only codes for which the AU modifier may be used").
- **B4 = Column I/II capture shape.** One Pattern-3 rule (R11): governing sentence + the table pairs linearized into the rule string ("Column I A4625, Column II A4626.
