#### Notes

- **Single-domain** (intrapulmonary percussive ventilation system); domain axis omitted. Companion to LCD L33786; references NCD 240.5. Closest precedents A52510 (S100), A52494 (S100), A52492 (S96).
- **DP-A = drop coverage-preamble in full** (= A52494 / A52510 / A52466 B4). Three-prong test, §1862(a)(1)(A) scoping, and the §1861(s)(6) DME-benefit statutory-framing sentence dropped (corollary #1); R&N-in-LCD already encoded by `gem:referencesPolicy gemi:lcd33786`.
- **DP-B = corollary #2 device-definition drop (clean, no extension).** The CODING-GUIDELINES IPV definition ("An intrapulmonary percussive ventilation system (IPV) delivers a series of pressurized gas minibursts at rates greater than 100 cycles per minute to the respiratory tract.") is dropped — its **full verbatim already lives on `gemi:conceptIntrapulmonaryPercussiveVentilationSystem`** (and `gemi:conceptPressurizedGasMinibursts`), no extension needed.
- **R6 (kept all-inclusive increment).** The E0481 bundling directive ("E0481 includes the compressor, hand held units, tubing and all related accessories…") is the rule-bearing increment beyond the descriptor — captured as the two-sentence Pattern-3 form including both configurations, = A52494 R11 / A52492 R19 all-inclusive shape (coding-correctness + coverage-scope).
- **R5 source-fidelity:** omits "prior to delivery" (= A52494/A52510/A52517/A52492 R-form). **R1 boundary:** captured through "…which is periodically updated"; "available here" tail dropped (= A52466 R21 / A52492 R5).
- **No diagnosis-on-claim rule:** A52495's POLICY SPECIFIC DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS section contains only the general-doc-req pointer and the "Refer to the … Standard Documentation Requirements article" pointer — both navigational drops; no policy-specific documentation rule survives (contrast A52494 R6 / A52510 R7).
- **Drops (navigational/framing):** general-doc-req pointer; "Refer to the LCD-related Standard Documentation Requirements article"; FR1713 "available here" tail; PDAC-contractor pointer (= A52492 D18 / A52466 B-B2).
- **No closed-list ICD section** (all four ICD-10 coding sections and CPT/HCPCS are N/A) — no `gem:exclusivelyCoversCondition`, no `gem:PolicyGroup`; A52495 raises no structured⟷NL complement question and is **not** added to `deferred_proposals[84]`.
- **No new schema.** 5 axis-2 tags used (12 `gem:ruleType` triples): documentation 5, non-coverage 3, coverage-scope 2, statutory-framing 1, coding-correctness 1.

- **B3 = statutory-framing retained on R25.** The §1862(a)(1)(A) cite sits inside the testable rule (it is the authority the MAC's reasonable-and-necessary determination runs under), so the rule carries `statutory-framing` in addition to `coverage-scope, eligibility`. Contrast NCD 240.2 R19 (analogous MAC discretion) which had no explicit statute cite and so used only `coverage-scope, eligibility`.
- **B4 = HMV §II.(a) umbrella kept standalone (R14).** It adds "volume targeted mode" and "certain clinical characteristics" not fully carried by the (i) criteria; parallels NCD 240.2 R1 retaining its umbrella.
- **B5 = R15 leading "(i)" enumerator kept verbatim.** The gate-framing rule begins "(i) An HMV is covered…"; the bare enumerator is part of the source line and is retained.
- **B6 = no `setting-definition`.** "In the home" folds into `coverage-scope` per the NCD 240.2 R1 precedent; no separate setting rule-type is assigned.
- **B7 = continuing-usage/eval rule-type convention.** The cadence and evaluation rules carry `frequency` (timing + the 4h/24h-on-70%-of-days utilization), `documentation` (clinician "must establish"), and `credentialed-actor` (treating clinician), with `eligibility` added on R11 for its clinical-outcome substance. Post-second-evaluation rules (R13, R23) name no clinician and so omit `credentialed-actor`.
- **Verbatim source artifacts preserved (corollary #3; PDF authoritative).** R18: "…life-threatening condition if the patient or cannot be otherwise alerted…" (apparent dropped words). R24: "an or onasal mask" (for "oronasal") and "(e.g.,mouthpiece" (missing space). All confirmed in a raw (non-layout) extraction and captured exactly; surfaced to Tom 2026-06-29.
- **Soft-wrap de-hyphenation.** PDF line-broken hyphenated words were rejoined without an inserted space ("6-month", "2-week"); flagged as a candidate join-convention codification.
- **No clinical-concept mints.** Rule-backfill scope only; the 49 existing `gem:ClinicalConcept` and 2 `gem:ProviderCredential` individuals are reused via existing triples.
- **Methodology drops (silent, per SKILL.md):** §A device definitions (RAD / HMV — corollary #2, content on `gem:ClinicalConcept` individuals); §C "N/A" (confirmed-empty → zero rules, not gated); §D conforming-changes-to-280.1 sentence (B2); "(This NCD last reviewed June 2025.)" metadata; Claims Processing Instructions / Transmittal Information / Revision History / NCAs / Other Versions (administrative metadata and change-log artifacts per §Three Code Contexts revision-history exclusion).

### NCD 310.1 — Routine Costs in Clinical Trials

*Categorized S105 (2026-07-01). `gemi:ncd310.1_r1` – `gemi:ncd310.1_r33`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-01 (Session 105). 33 rules, all at policy level (no anchored coding scopes). Broad clinical-trial routine-cost NCD spanning many benefit categories; domain axis omitted per single-topic convention. Rule-backfill pass — `gemi:ncd310.1` was extracted `planDone` (72 `gem:refersToBenefitCategory`, 13 `gem:ProviderCredential`, 23 `gem:ClinicalConcept`, 5 `gem:referencesPolicy`) with zero `gem:ruleDescription` triples at session start; this pass backfilled all 33 on the existing policy entity (no scope-mint, no description rewrite, no concept/credential/benefit-category mint). The V3 (2024) text is a technical change over the substantive 2007/2000 content (CR13597 / TN12590). Enumerated lists are atomized one rule per item with a **δ-prefix scaffold** carrying the shared section scope (NCD 160.18 / 240.9 precedent): 3 routine-cost exclusions (R3–R5), 3 inclusions (R6–R8), 3 Section-A requirements (R12–R14), 7 desirable characteristics (R16–R22), 4 auto-qualified categories (R26–R29). Granularity (Tom-confirmed S105): **BL-1** full capture of the Section-B qualification machinery (panel, certification/registry, Chief-Clinical-Officer revocation, misrepresentation-denial, Medicare Advantage) as `procedural`-tagged rules (TN 2476 precedent); **BL-2** the routine-cost definition (R2) and the desirable-characteristics framing (R15) kept standalone, the bare "routine costs include:" header folded into the R6–R8 δ-prefix; **BL-3** the multi-clause panel (R23), misrepresentation (R32), and M+C (R33) provisions kept one rule each. Effective-date phrases kept verbatim per provision (7/9/2007 on R1; 9/19/2000 in the auto-qualified block's δ-scope). No new axis-2 vocabulary; 10 distinct tags used (coverage-scope, eligibility, study-design, non-coverage, procedural, service-definition, study-quality, statutory-framing, documentation, payment-rule).

| Rule | Source / topic | Pattern | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | :--- |

| R2 | §Indications: routine-cost definition — items/services otherwise generally available (benefit category exists, not statutorily excluded, no national non-coverage) provided in experimental or control arms | 1 | coverage-scope, service-definition |

| R6 | Routine-cost inclusion: items/services typically provided absent a trial (conventional care) (δ) | 1 | coverage-scope, service-definition |
| R7 | Routine-cost inclusion: items/services required for the investigational item, its clinically appropriate monitoring, or prevention of complications (δ) | 1 | coverage-scope, service-definition |
| R8 | Routine-cost inclusion: items/services for R&N care arising from the investigational item — diagnosis/treatment of complications (δ) | 1 | coverage-scope, service-definition |

| R10 | §Indications: for non-covered items/services, Medicare covers only treatment of complications + unrelated R&N care | 1 | coverage-scope, non-coverage |
| R11 | §Indications: NCD-noncovered item that is the focus of a qualifying trial — routine costs covered, item itself not | 1 | coverage-scope, non-coverage |
| R12 | §A requirement: trial subject/purpose evaluates an item within a Medicare benefit category, not statutorily excluded (δ) | 1 | eligibility, study-design |
| R13 | §A requirement: not designed exclusively to test toxicity/pathophysiology; must have therapeutic intent (δ) | 3 | eligibility, study-design |

| R19 | §A desirable characteristic: trial design appropriate to answer the research question (δ) | 1 | study-design |
| R20 | §A desirable characteristic: sponsored by a credible organization/individual capable of executing it (δ) | 1 | study-design |

| R22 | §A desirable characteristic: conducted according to appropriate standards of scientific integrity (δ) | 1 | study-quality |

| R24 | §B qualification: qualifying trials covered after the lead PI certifies criteria + enrolls the trial in the Medicare clinical trials registry | 3 | eligibility, documentation, procedural |
| R25 | §B qualification: auto-qualified trials — PIs need not certify but must enroll in the registry | 3 | eligibility, documentation, procedural |
| R26 | §B auto-qualified category: trials funded by NIH, CDC, AHRQ, CMS, DOD, VA (δ) | 1 | eligibility |
| R27 | §B auto-qualified category: trials supported by centers/cooperative groups funded by those agencies (δ) | 1 | eligibility |
| R28 | §B auto-qualified category: trials under an IND reviewed by the FDA (δ) | 1 | eligibility |
| R29 | §B auto-qualified category: IND-exempt drug trials under 21 CFR 312.2(b)(1), deemed qualified until criteria/certification exist (δ) | 3 | eligibility |
| R30 | §B: CMS via the NCD process may find certain items only R&N when provided in a trial meeting that NCD's requirements | 1 | coverage-scope, procedural |
| R31 | §B: Medicare covers routine costs of qualifying trials (auto-qualified / certified / NCD-required) unless the Chief Clinical Officer finds the trial fails criteria or endangers beneficiaries | 1 | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R32 | §B: PI misrepresentation → denial under §1862(a)(1)(E); beneficiaries held harmless (§§1879, 1842(l), 1834(j)(4)); billing providers liable; fraud investigation | 3 | non-coverage, payment-rule, procedural, statutory-framing |
| R33 | §B: Medicare Advantage (M+C) organizations must follow this NCD and cover these trial-linked services regardless of network; reporting allowed but no prior authorization | 3 | coverage-scope, procedural |

- **All rules on policy level.** `gemi:ncd310.1` has no anchored coding scopes; all 33 rules live on the policy.

Each item carries its parent section scope as a bracketed `[… scope: …]` prefix so it reads as a rule out of context (NCD 160.18 / 240.9 precedent); one rule per item.
- **BL-1 = full procedural capture (Tom-confirmed).** The Section-B qualification machinery is captured as rules — R23 (AHRQ panel), R24 (certification/registry), R25 (auto-qualification/registry), R30 (NCD-process determination), R31 (coverage conditioned on qualification + CCO revocation), R32 (misrepresentation-denial), R33 (Medicare Advantage). Precedent for `procedural` capture of qualification/administrative mechanics: TN 2476.
- **BL-2 = framing/definition rules kept.** R2 (routine-cost definition — the source refers back to it as "as defined above/below") and R15 (the "insufficient alone / auto-qualified presumption" logic) kept standalone; the bare "routine costs in clinical trials include:" list header is folded into the R6–R8 δ-prefix rather than minted as a separate rule.
- **BL-3 = multi-clause provisions kept as one rule each.** R23, R32, and R33 are each a single coherent provision, multi-tagged rather than split into sub-clause rules.
- **R9 = scope-boundary capture.** The "does not withdraw" clause is a policy-scope non-alteration clause captured as one `coverage-scope` rule (see § "Scope-boundary sentences: capture vs. drop"); its trailing navigational sentence (the LCD-search URL pointer) is dropped.
- **Verbatim source fidelity (corollary #3/#4; PDF authoritative).** Curly quotation marks preserved on R23 ("panel") and R30 ("reasonable and necessary"); section signs on R23 (§1142, §1862(a)(1)(E)) and R32 (§1862(a)(1)(E), §§1879, 1842(l), 1834(j)(4)); em-dash on R8 ("service—in particular"). Two Tom-confirmed verbatim deviations: R2 drops the trailing "except:" list-connector (the exclusions are atomized in R3–R5), and R9 drops the trailing navigational LCD-search sentence.
- **No concept / credential / benefit-category mints.** Rule-backfill scope only; the 72 `gem:refersToBenefitCategory`, 13 `gem:ProviderCredential`, 23 `gem:ClinicalConcept`, and 5 `gem:referencesPolicy` are reused via existing triples. `policy_worklist.json` unchanged; `policies_processed` stays 33 (backfill on an already-processed policy). **Completes the concept-only rule-backfill campaign** (ncd240.2.1 + ncd310.1 the last targets; ncd240.9 already carried rules).
- **Methodology drops (silent, per SKILL.md):** Tracking / Description metadata; the 72-item Benefit Category list (informational, already modeled as `gem:refersToBenefitCategory`; the source's own "may not be exhaustive" caveat); the V3 technical-change revision note; Transmittal / Revision History / NCAs / Other Versions (administrative metadata and change-log artifacts). CR13597 / CR5719 / CR1241 named in the revision history are out of scope for a rule backfill (CR handling gated by the deferred CR-extraction methodology).

The physician's office carries both polarities — exclusively-covered on R9 (PENS, a diagnostic procedure) and excluded on R15 (ongoing treatment) — different-service/different-phase, not a conflict (§Polarity rule 6 governs *within* one rule). **Borderline B1 (Tom):** R14's *"it is inappropriate for a patient to visit his/her physician, physical therapist, or an outpatient clinic on a continuing basis"* **states an expectation that is followed by a denial in R15**, so R14 takes no exclusion link and R15 is the sole operative denial. Three alternatives declined: an R14 exclusion on the outpatient clinic alone, the same plus the physician's office, and reading the clause as closing R14's set onto the home (`gem:exclusivelyCoversInHealthcareSetting`). *"Physical therapist"* is an actor, not a place, on both rules. R9's bare *"clinic"* and R15's *"outpatient clinic"* stay distinct individuals per catalog-phrasings. The five policy-level `gem:refersToHealthcareSetting` presence links are unchanged (S197 decision 8).

**Notes**
- **Atomization (B).** Closed-gate "not covered except (1)(2)" → a non-coverage base (R1) plus two δ-scoped exception rules (R2/R3), following the NCD 160.7 R10 pattern. Contrast the disjunctive OR-fold used for open coverage grants (NCD 80.11, NCD 190.2).
- **Concepts / credential.** 10 clinical-concept links, all reuse (§140.1 governing text; incl. `conceptPregnancyResultingFromRape` / `conceptPregnancyResultingFromIncest` composites); 0 mints. `credentialPhysician` (reuse) for "as certified by a physician".

- **No codes; publication + source.** `publicationNumber "100-3"`; `dc:source` full URL (Tom-provided). Version 2, effective/implementation 2006-06-19, 2 pp; benefit category Physicians' Services.
- **Cross-version silent-deletion audit (S136, 2026-07-10).** Compared V1 (10/01/1998–06/19/2006, TN 108) → V2 (06/19/2006–present, TN 48) — one MCD-version transition. **Finding (interpretive / moderate, higher than 40.2): silent deletion of nine CPT codes.** V1 closes the coverage provision with “This restricted coverage applies to CPT codes 59840, 59841, 59850, 59851, 59852, 59855, 59856, 59857, and 59866.”; V2 drops the sentence. **Provenance:** V1 — the version TN 108/CR 778 (03/1999) produced with the rape/incest/life-endangerment restriction — still lists all nine codes, so the 1999 instruction added the restriction but kept the codes; the removal is TN 48/CR 4278 (03/2006, the Technical Corrections pass). **Silent at two levels:** the MCD revision note says only “Technical Corrections to the NCD Manual,” and the R48NCD.pdf transmittal body itself (read by Tom, S136) does not mention the CPT removal. Coverage-neutral (the determination — abortions not covered except conditions 1 and 2 — is preserved verbatim in V2) and consistent with the MMA §731 removal-of-coding-from-NCDs pattern already noted in this policy’s `gem:description`. **GEM consequence:** none of the nine codes exist anywhere in the graph (not in `cpt.ttl`, no `gem:coversProcedure` / `refersToHCPCSprocedure` link), so the current V2-only graph cannot map a claim bearing any of these abortion CPT codes to NCD 140.1 by procedure code; a 1998–2006 date-of-service claim would have. These are the operative procedure codes the restricted coverage applies to (V1’s wording), making this higher-materiality than 40.2’s E2100/E2101. Parallels NCD 40.2 Finding A and NCD 20.29 Finding 2. V2 also adds the “CIM 35-99” predecessor heading (additive); nothing else subtractive. **Disposition (Tom, S136): record-only (A)** — no graph change; current-version-only fidelity retained. Backfill (option C) would require provisional `cpt.ttl` mints and is gated on the paused multi-version-management decision.

Mirrors NCD 210.1's separation of eligibility/frequency rules from the service grant. `riskFactor` reused (pre-existing axis-2 value).
- **R3 captured as documentation (B2).** The "must indicate low/high risk status by including the appropriate diagnosis code" NOTE is a mandatory claims-content requirement an evaluator tests, not mere billing mechanics — captured as a `documentation` rule (parallel to NCD 210.1 R4/R6 documentation rules). The Item 24E / CMS-1500 reference is retained verbatim inside the rule string.
- **R6 §1861(nn) definition captured (B3).** The statutory "woman as described in §1861(nn)" definition carries unique eligibility content (pap smear in the preceding 3 years indicating cancer/abnormality, or high risk) that is not on any named entity — `conceptWomanOfChildbearingAge` carries only the different "woman of childbearing age" definition. Captured as `definition`/`eligibility`; R1 additionally carries the "(§1861(nn))" cross-reference verbatim (corollary #4). Genuine borderline against a corollary #1/#2 drop.
- **Definitions dropped (corollary #2).** The "woman of childbearing age is one who is premenopausal…" definition (content on `conceptWomanOfChildbearingAge` + `conceptPremenopausal`) and the "other qualified practitioner, as defined in 42 CFR 410.56(a)…" definition (content + term-of-art alias on `credentialOtherQualifiedPractitioner`) are not minted as rules. The AMA/CMS "Documentation Guidelines for Evaluation and Management Services" attribution sentence is dropped (provenance, not an evaluator criterion).
- **Concepts pre-seeded (reuse-only).** 46 clinical-concept links: 44 reuse individuals section-tagged "TN 48 §210.2" in their descriptions (0 mints), plus 2 shared concepts named in §210.2 but authored for other sections — `conceptPapSmear` (§190.2; "has had a pap smear test") and `conceptHIVInfection` (§190.14; literal "including HIV infection", B4). Pre-seeded `conceptHistoryOfHIVInfection` links regardless; bare `conceptHIV` not added (appears only inside "HIV infection").
- **Credentials.** 7 links: `credentialPhysician` (reuse) + `credentialAuthorizedPractitioner` (minted, B5 — "ordered by a physician (or authorized practitioner)", distinct catalog phrasing from "other qualified practitioner") + `credentialOtherQualifiedPractitioner` (reuse, §210.2 pre-seed) + CNM/PA/NP/CNS (reuse; licensed via the §210.2 term-of-art alias in the "other qualified practitioner" definition — NCD 210.1 §C precedent).
- **References / revision.** `referencesPolicy gemi:tn48NCD` (current Transmittal Information field). TN 48 is also this NCD's current transmittal and already carries `gemi:tn48NCD gem:revisesPolicy gemi:ncd210.2` — both directions asserted (no superseded-revision case, unlike NCD 190.14). No Related National Coverage Documents or Cross Reference section; no CMS-manual-chapter citations. `ncd190.2 gem:referencesPolicy gemi:ncd210.2` (190.2's Cross Reference) is inbound only — §210.2 does not reciprocate. Revision-history-only TNs/CRs not minted (three-contexts; CR-methodology gate).

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |

| R1 | Initial Indications & Limitations coverage grant: intravenous levocarnitine covered only for ESRD patients on dialysis for a minimum of three months who have documented carnitine deficiency, along with signs and symptoms of either erythropoietin-resistant anemia (persistent hematocrit <30% with treatment, unresponsive to standard erythropoietin dosage with iron replacement, other causes investigated and treated) or hypotension on hemodialysis interfering with intended dialysis despite usual measures (at least 2 episodes in a 30-day period). Folds both indication disjuncts (ζ-pending) | coverage-scope, eligibility |

| R5 | Continued-treatment coverage grant: a patient currently receiving intravenous levocarnitine is covered if the qualifying indication was administered AND either the medical record documents a pre-dialysis plasma free carnitine level <40 micromol/L prior to initiation OR the treating physician certifies (documents in the medical record) that discontinuation would drop the pre-dialysis carnitine level below 40 micromol/L with recurrent erythropoietin-resistant anemia or intradialytic hypotension | coverage-scope, eligibility, documentation, credentialed-actor |

R1's "documented carnitine deficiency" is a bare eligibility-gate adjective (no `documentation` tag; contrast NCD 210.2 R3).
- **conceptHematocrit shared-add (B1).** 22 clinical-concept links: 21 reuse individuals section-tagged "TN 48 §230.19" in their descriptions (0 mints), plus 1 shared concept — `conceptHematocrit` (literal "hematocrit" in "persistent hematocrit <30% with treatment"), which was absent from the §230.19 pre-seed. CIM 45-32 predecessor and benefit-category boilerplate → description prose only.

### NCD 300.1 — Obsolete or Unreliable Diagnostic Tests

*Extracted S126 (2026-07-06). `gemi:ncd300.1_r1`–`gemi:ncd300.1_r2`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-06 (Session 126). 2 rules, both at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; the policy references no inline HCPCS/ICD codes — coding was removed from the NCD per MMA §731, predecessor CIM 50-34). Single-domain policy (obsolete/unreliable diagnostic tests; Diagnostic Tests (other)); domain axis omitted per convention. `gemi:ncd300.1` was a `planPromote` NCD stub — the **last** TN 48 campaign stub — promoted to a fully-extracted `planDone` policy (stub metadata expanded in place; workflow entry flipped `planPromote → planDone`). Same-era promotion: Version 2 **is** the TN 48 version (current Transmittal Information field = TN 48), so — unlike NCD 260.1 (S125) — no divergence and no new current transmittal. 3 distinct axis-2 `rule_type` values (4 `gem:ruleType` triples): non-coverage (2), payment-rule (1), procedural (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. No δ-scope (the two test enumerations are flat lists — no letter-labels, nesting, or in-rule cross-references — so folded verbatim into their parent rule, members queryable via concept links). Benefit category: Diagnostic Tests (other) (reuse, from NCD 310.1). Provider credential: none. 38 clinical-concept links, **all reuse** of the TN 48 §300.1 pre-seed individuals (28 subsection-A tests + 10 subsection-B tests; 0 mints). **This promotion closes the TN 48 stub-promotion campaign** (0 stubs remaining).

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | §300.1(A) Diagnostic Tests. Conditional non-coverage: the 28 listed obsolete tests are not routinely paid (replaced by more advanced procedures); payable only if the medical need is satisfactorily justified by the performing physician, with the satisfactory-justification determination made by the QIO (services subject to QIO Review) or otherwise by the A/B MAC. 28-test list folded verbatim | non-coverage, payment-rule, procedural |
| R2 | §300.1(B) Cardiovascular Tests. Absolute non-coverage: the 10 listed phonocardiography and vectorcardiography tests are not paid (outmoded, little clinical value). 10-test list folded verbatim | non-coverage |

**Notes**
- **B1 (rule count — 2, QIO/MAC folded into R1).** Subsection A is captured as one Pattern-3 multi-sentence rule: the do-not-routinely-pay default, the medical-justification exception, and the QIO-vs-A/B-MAC determination authority form a single conditional-non-coverage unit. The QIO/MAC split names *who* determines justification; it is not a separate claim-matchable branch (one justification gate under the IF/THEN heuristic), so it is folded rather than split into its own rule.
- **B2 (R1 rule types).** `non-coverage` (obsolete tests, not routinely paid = polarity) + `payment-rule` ("do not routinely pay" / "may be paid only if" = payment-conditional, the feature that distinguishes A from B) + `procedural` (the QIO/A-B-MAC determination-authority framework, program-administrative). Subsection B (R2) carries `non-coverage` alone (absolute, no payment-conditionality).
- **B3 (credentials — 0, no credentialed-actor).** The performing physician (who justifies medical need), the QIO, and the A/B MAC are review/justification authorities, not a coverage-gating provider credential; no policy-level `requiresProviderCredential` and no per-rule `credentialed-actor` tag (NCD 150.5 precedent: MAC medical staff = review authority, not minted as a credential).
- **B4 (TN 96 — not minted).** TN 96 (the Version 1 transmittal, effective 1997-01-01, appearing only in Revision History) is captured as description prose and earns no graph node and no `revisesPolicy` triple, consistent with prior TN 48-campaign promotions that left Version-1-era revision-history transmittals (e.g. TN 62 on NCD 80.11) prose-only. CR 4278 is already `gem:transmitsChangeRequest` on `gemi:tn48NCD` (untouched; CR-extraction methodology gate).
- **B5 (QIO/MAC justification-determination — no worklist change).** The QIO/A-B-MAC satisfactory-justification determination is captured verbatim in R1 with a `procedural` tag. It is distinct from `deferred_proposals` #91 (MAC-*discretion coverage* polarity, NCD 260.1 R3): here the contractor/QIO determines *justification for payment of an otherwise-non-covered test*, not *coverage* itself. It is a well-understood conditional-non-coverage-with-exception, not a novel unmodeled structure, so no new `deferred_proposals` entry and no `also_seen_in` append.
- **Both directions for TN 48.** `gemi:ncd300.1 gem:referencesPolicy gemi:tn48NCD` (current Transmittal Information field) added this session; the pre-existing `gemi:tn48NCD gem:revisesPolicy gemi:ncd300.1` lineage link is preserved — both directions, as TN 48 is the current (not superseded) transmittal here.
- **No codes; publication + source.** No inline HCPCS/ICD references (MMA §731). `publicationNumber "100-3"`; `manualSectionNumber "300.1"`; `dc:source` refreshed to the user URL `…?NCDId=204&NCDver=2` (URL-correction; replaces the stub's `?ncdid=204`). Version 2, effective and implementation 2006-06-19; 4 pp. Source apostrophe U+0027 (Bendien's, Bolen's).

### L33923 — Noninvasive Ear or Pulse Oximetry For Oxygen Saturation

*Extracted S127 (2026-07-06). `gemi:lcd33923_r1`–`gemi:lcd33923_r3`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-06 (Session 127). 3 rules, all at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; the LCD references no inline HCPCS/ICD codes — CPT 94760/94761/94762 and ICD-10 I16.0–I16.9 appear only in Revision History R1 and are excluded per the three-contexts rule). Single-domain policy (noninvasive ear or pulse oximetry for oxygen saturation); domain axis omitted per convention. First Coast Service Options (A/B MAC, Jurisdiction J-N; FL, PR, VI), Revision R3, effective 2019-10-01. Fresh full extraction (not a stub promotion). 3 distinct axis-2 `rule_type` values (7 `gem:ruleType` triples): coverage-scope (3), eligibility (2), procedural (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. No δ-scope (no letter-labels, nesting, or in-rule cross-references). No benefit category (LCD-level; benefit categories are asserted at NCD level in this corpus). Provider credential: none. 12 clinical-concept links (6 reuse + 6 mint). References: A57115 (paired Billing & Coding article — minted stub), Pub. 100-02 Ch 15 (reuse), Pub. 100-08 Ch 13 (minted manual-chapter stub).

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | Coverage Indications — Single and Multiple Determinations. Medically necessary when the patient has a condition resulting in hypoxemia and there is a need to assess the status of a chronic respiratory condition, supplemental oxygen requirements, and/or a therapeutic regimen | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R2 | Coverage Indications — Continuous Overnight Monitoring. Medically necessary when (a) intermittent arterial blood gas sampling is likely to miss important variations AND (b) the patient has a hypoxemia condition needing assessment of supplemental oxygen requirements and/or a therapeutic regimen | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R3 | Limitations. Reasonable-and-necessary coverage standard (SSA §1862(a)(1)(A)) per Program Integrity Manual (Pub. 100-08) Ch 13 §13.5.4, with contractor discretion to determine and describe covered circumstances | coverage-scope, procedural |

**Notes**
- **B-refs (L29370 prose-only).** "Sources of Information" names First Coast reference LCD number L29370. It is unresolvable on the current MCD (search miss) and is a superseded/pre-migration legacy identifier — most likely this policy's own pre-migration identity, not a distinct live policy. Recorded in `gemi:lcd33923`'s `gem:description` prose only; not minted, no `referencesPolicy`, no worklist entry (Session 127, Tom-confirmed Path 2).
- **B-rule3 (R3 kept, not dropped).** The Limitations paragraph is captured as R3 rather than dropped as boilerplate: it sits in the rule-bearing Limitations section and the §1862(a)(1)(A) reference sits *inside* the coverage rule ("covered … if reasonable and necessary under §1862(a)(1)(A)"), the keep-case under SKILL.md §Rule Patterns → "What belongs as a rule" corollary #1; the contractor-discretion clause is the `procedural` component.
- **B-cred (credentials — 0).** "Contractors shall determine and describe the circumstances" names the MAC as a review/determination authority, not a coverage-gating provider credential; no `requiresProviderCredential` (NCD 300.1 B3 / NCD 150.5 precedent). No physician/practitioner appears in current LCD prose (the ordering/referring-physician documentation duties live in the paired article A57115, not this LCD).
- **B-concepts (12 links; 6 mint).** Reuse: pulse oximetry, ear oximetry, oxygen saturation, arterial oxygen saturation, hypoxemia, supplemental oxygen. Mint: chronic respiratory condition, arterial blood gas sampling, arterial oxygenation, sleep study (singular-normalized from "sleep studies"), continuous overnight monitoring, therapeutic regimen. Dropped near-duplicate/device-mechanism terms: "ear oximeter" (≈ ear oximetry), "arterial pulsation" (device-mechanism prose), nailbed / photodetector / wavelengths of light.

Single-domain policy (neuromuscular electrical stimulation); domain axis omitted per convention. `gemi:ncd160.12` was a `planPromote` NCD stub (minted via NCD 280.1's "Muscle Stimulators" DME-reference entry), promoted **in place** to a fully-extracted `planDone` policy (stub metadata expanded; consolidated workflow entry flipped `planPromote → planDone`). **Version 2** extracted (effective 2006-10-01, implementation 2006-10-02, 4 pp; in-effect), superseding Version 1 (2003-04-01 to 2006-10-01). Current-version-only modeling (multi-version design still deferred); the V1→V2 completeness audit is recorded below. 6 distinct axis-2 `rule_type` values (10 `gem:ruleType` triples): coverage-scope (3), eligibility (2), credentialed-actor (2), definition (1), non-coverage (1), setting-definition (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. **Benefit category: none** ("No Benefit Category"). 1 provider credential (reuse): `credentialPhysicalTherapist`. 14 clinical-concept links — 8 mints + 6 reuse. 8 policy-to-policy references — 3 reuse-links (`cag00153R`, `ncd160.13`, `pub100_02_ch15`) + 5 stubs minted (`pub100_04_ch5` manual chapter; transmittals `tn55NCD` / `tn941CP` / `tn160CIM` / `tn26CIM`); 2 change-request stubs minted (`cr4014`, `cr2314`) wired via `transmitsChangeRequest`.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | §Item/Service Description: NMES device (electrode-delivered impulse over selected muscle groups); two categories — resting-state stimulation for muscle atrophy, and functional-activity enhancement in neurologically impaired patients (FES) | definition |
| R2 | §Treatment of Muscle Atrophy: coverage limited to disuse atrophy where nerve supply is intact + non-neurological disuse-atrophy causes; examples (casting/splinting, burn-scar contracture, hip replacement until orthotic training); cross-ref §160.13 | coverage-scope |
| R3 | §Use for Walking (SCI): NMES/FES walking coverage limited to SCI patients completing ≥32 one-on-one PT sessions over three months, directly performed by the physical therapist; goal is walking training, not reversing/retarding atrophy | coverage-scope, eligibility, credentialed-actor |
| R4 | §Use for Walking: covered only when the patient meets all nine enumerated characteristics (intact lower motor units L1↓; weight-bearing stability + independent upright posture; brisk contraction + sensory perception; motivation/commitment/cognition; independent transfer + ≥3-min standing tolerance; hand/finger control; ≥6-mo post-recovery SCI + restorative surgery; **without** hip/knee degenerative disease + no osteoporotic long-bone-fracture history; willingness to use long-term) | eligibility |
| R5 | §Use for Walking: not covered if any of five contraindications present (cardiac pacemaker; severe scoliosis or osteoporosis; skin disease or cancer at stimulation site; irreversible contracture; autonomic dysreflexia) | non-coverage |
| R6 | §Use for Walking: the one-on-one PT training is covered only in inpatient hospitals, outpatient hospitals, CORFs, and outpatient rehabilitation facilities | setting-definition, credentialed-actor |
| R7 | §Use for Walking: additional therapy after DME purchase is limited by general skilled-PT coverage policies | coverage-scope |

**Notes**
- **B-a (benefit category — none).** Version 2's Tracking field states "No Benefit Category"; recorded per the NCD 190.14 precedent with **no** `gem:refersToBenefitCategory` link. NMES/FES is functionally DME (§Use-for-Walking references "purchase of the DME"), but the formal field asserts no benefit category and the DME mention is descriptive prose; an SME may later relate it to the DME category.
- **B-b (credential — PT, reuse).** `credentialPhysicalTherapist` linked at policy level; R3 (one-on-one training "directly performed by the physical therapist") and R6 (settings where skilled therapists are employed) carry `credentialed-actor`. No MAC or DME-supplier credential is named in the document.
- **B-c (rule granularity — 7 rules; the 9-criteria and 5-exclusion lists each one rule).** R4 captures all nine inclusion characteristics as a single all-of `eligibility` rule; R5 captures all five contraindications as a single any-of `non-coverage` rule (disjunctive-fold precedent — the lists carry no letter-label cross-references). §"Use for Walking" is split into R3 (coverage grant + training precondition + goal) / R4 (inclusion set) / R5 (exclusion set) / R6 (settings) / R7 (post-DME therapy limit).
- **B-d (concepts — 8 mints, 6 reuse; Option-B inclusive).** Reuse: `conceptNeuromuscularElectricalStimulation`, `conceptElectricalStimulation`, `conceptDisuseAtrophy`, `conceptSpinalCord`, `conceptCardiacPacemaker`, `conceptSkinBurnThermal`. Mint: `conceptFunctionalElectricalStimulation`, `conceptSpinalCordInjury`, `conceptMuscleAtrophy`, `conceptOsteoporosis`, `conceptScoliosis`, `conceptContracture`, `conceptAutonomicDysreflexia`, `conceptDegenerativeJointDisease`. No separate long-bone-fracture concept (folded into the osteoporosis criterion). **Source-misspelling call:** criterion-5 term is printed "autonomic dysflexia" in **both** renditions; R5's `gem:ruleDescription` reproduces the source spelling verbatim (source-fidelity), while the minted concept normalizes to the clinically-correct "autonomic dysreflexia" (`conceptAutonomicDysreflexia`, note in its description). Flagged for confirmation.
- **B-e (reference-stub URI suffixes).** `tn55NCD` / `tn160CIM` suffixes derive from `dc:source` filenames (R55NCD.pdf — in-effect V2 deliverer, delivers CR 4014; R160CIM.pdf — superseded V1 deliverer, delivers CR 2314). `tn941CP` carries a **CP** suffix from the "Medicare Claims Processing" manual label (no `dc:source` filename in the NCD; precedent `tn961CP` / R###CP.pdf) — source URL pending. `tn26CIM` carries a **provisional** CIM suffix (06/1988 predates the NCD Manual; no filename) — source URL pending. `pub100_04_ch5` (Claims Processing Manual Ch 5, §10.1) minted as a `CMSmanualChapter` stub — source URL pending. `cag00153R`, `ncd160.13`, and `pub100_02_ch15` already existed (reuse-links; `cag00153R` was minted during NCD 280.1 with a verified URL). CR stubs `cr4014` (via `tn55NCD`) and `cr2314` (via `tn160CIM`) wired by `transmitsChangeRequest`; each CR's `dc:source` is its delivering-transmittal IRI. **TN AB-02-156** (Version 1's Program-Memorandum claims-processing instruction) is a V1-only reference and is **not** captured under current-version-only modeling.
- **Cross-version (V1→V2) silent-deletion audit.** Both versions supplied by Tom; a completeness safeguard for current-version-only modeling. **Conclusion: no V1 coverage silently withdrawn in V2** (effectively net-neutral — one correction, one documented cross-reference addition). *Preserved:* the NMES definition + two device categories; the muscle-atrophy/disuse-atrophy coverage limitation + examples + §160.13 cross-ref; the NMES/FES SCI-walking coverage grant (≥32 one-on-one PT sessions over 3 months, PT-delivered, walking goal); the nine inclusion characteristics; the five contraindications; the four covered settings; the post-DME therapy limitation. *Documented change:* V2 adds a cross-reference to §220 of the Medicare Benefit Policy Manual, Chapter 15 (Revision History 05/2006 — TN 55 / CR 4014). *The one undocumented substantive change* (absent from the TN 55 revision note, which records only the §220 addition): inclusion criterion 8 is reversed from "Persons **with** hip and knee degenerative disease…" (V1) to "Persons **without**…" (V2). Classified a **correction/reframe (note, not a finding)** per the silent-deletion methodology — the criterion is retained with its polarity reversed, nothing is removed, and V1's "with" is clinically incoherent (requiring degenerative disease as a walking-FES coverage criterion), so V2's "without" is the sensible reading. *Trivial:* criterion-1 typo "unite" → "units". *Administrative:* claims-processing pointer changed (V1 PM TN AB-02-156 → V2 TN 941). No NCD-level code impact (NCDs carry no claims-processing codes).
- **Source / boundary.** Canonical sources are the two user-supplied PDFs (V1 `NCDId=175&ncdver=1`, V2 `NCDId=175&ncdver=2`); `pdftotext -layout` confirmed faithful to the in-context renderings. Assessment compared the two NCD renditions plus their revision notes; the underlying transmittals / change requests were **not** fetched (per Tom's Q1 process rule: with nothing missing, related documents are deferred to future claims-analysis passes). `publicationNumber "100-3"`; `manualSectionNumber "160.12"`; `dc:source` is the version-agnostic `…?NCDId=175` (resolves to in-effect V2). Version 2, effective 2006-10-01; implementation 2006-10-02; 4 pp; `isInEffect true`.

| R1 | Item/Service Description and Indications and Limitations of Coverage (identical text in both): effective 2022-01-01, CMS determined that no NCD is appropriate at this time for Enteral and Parenteral Nutritional Therapy; in the absence of an NCD, coverage determinations are made by the MACs under 1862(a)(1)(A) (removal / MAC-discretion delegation) | coverage-scope, statutory-framing |

**Notes**
- **B1 (isInEffect true — retired-NCD convention applied).** Per Tom (S143: "follow 240.2.2 B1 convention"), `isInEffect` stays `true` because V3 is the latest, non-superseded version; the retirement is captured in the rule and description, not by flipping `isInEffect`. Single IF/THEN — the two identical text placements are one rule, not two (no verbatim-capture conflict: both occurrences are byte-identical).
- **B2 (cross-version subtractive audit — ZERO findings).** Tom supplied V1 (1984-07-11), V2 (2022-01-01) and V3 (2023-04-10). V1 carried substantial coverage content — parenteral nutrition daily-therapy reasonable-and-necessary criteria, the indwelling-catheter/home-infusion description, physician written order + documentation requirements, case-by-case MAC approval at intervals of no more than three months, infusion-pump medical-necessity and simplest-model payment basis, the one-month nutrient supply cap, premixed-solution payment conditions, enteral nutrition reasonable-and-necessary criteria and delivery routes, and the non-coverage of nutritional supplementation. All of it is absent from V3. **None of it is a finding:** V2 is an intervening version that explicitly documents *and* effects the removal ("Effective January 1, 2022 … no NCD is appropriate at this time"), which is exactly the condition the silent-deletion methodology excludes. Per the 240.2.2 B2 pattern the superseded content is change-log only, flagged here for the paused multi-version-management discussion, not modeled in the graph.
- **B3 (rule typing).** R1 carries `statutory-framing` (§1862(a)(1)(A) reasonable-and-necessary basis) alongside `coverage-scope` (MAC-discretion coverage delegation). Renaming is invasive; flagged, not actioned.
- **B5 (shared CR 12613).** `cr12613` receives inbound `gem:transmitsChangeRequest` from **both** `tn11272NCD` and `tn11426NCD` (every-deliverer convention); `dc:source` = the in-effect deliverer `tn11426NCD` (per the S131 shared-CR wiring rule). `tn11426NCD revisesPolicy tn11272NCD` records the rescind-replace. CR-extraction methodology still pending. Note the CR chains differ across the two retired siblings: 180.2 runs on CR 12613, 240.2.2 on CR 12607, though both were retitled by TN 11892.
- **B6 (Pub. 100-04 Ch. 32 — deferred to TN 11426).** V3's Revision History (05/2022) names "chapter 32 of the IOM for Pub. 100-04" and the companion Pub. 100-02 / Pub. 100-03 as the *objects of TN 11426's own revision*, not as material NCD 180.2 directs a claim reader to (contrast `pub100_04_ch5`, cross-referenced by NCD 160.12 as governing text). Per Tom (S143), the `gem:CMSmanualChapter` stub is minted when **TN 11426 is itself processed**, not here. Recorded in `tn11426NCD`'s description so the future extractor sees it.

Per Tom, V3's stated category is recorded as-is (`benefitCategoryProstheticDevices`, reuse) and the round-trip noted for source fidelity. Discovered at the stub's mint and carried forward into the promoted description; `gemi:conceptInfusionPump` remains NCD 280.1's own DME-table concept and was **not** reused here (280.1's concept is the pump, not this policy's subject).

That clause is stale — `deferred_proposals` #24 (policyStatus) was marked **obsolete** at S46 as superseded by `gem:nextPlannedStep` + `gem:isInEffect`. Removed from the promoted description; retirement remains recorded in prose per the 240.2.2 B1 convention.

No policy-to-policy cross-references beyond the three transmittals — V3 cites no other NCD (contrast 240.2.2's `referencesPolicy ncd240.2`). `publicationNumber "100-3"`; `manualSectionNumber "180.2"`; `dc:source` set from the stub's version-agnostic `…?NCDId=242` to the user-supplied `…?ncdid=242&ncdver=3&`. ### NCD 280.4 — Seat Lift

*Extracted S144 (2026-07-14). `gemi:ncd280.4_r1` – `_r5`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-14 (Session 144). 5 rules at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; no inline HCPCS/ICD codes — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (seat lift / Durable Medical Equipment); domain axis omitted per convention. `gemi:ncd280.4` was a `planPromote` NCD stub (minted via NCD 280.1's "Seat Lifts" DME-reference entry), promoted to a fully-extracted `planDone` policy (stub collapsed from the NCD 280.1 POLICY STUBS block into its own top-level section; workflow entry flipped `planPromote → planDone`). Longstanding Version 1 NCD; the Other Versions table lists Version 1 only, so **no cross-version subtractive audit applies** — the first promotion in the recent NCD campaign with genuinely nothing to audit against. 7 axis-2 `rule_type` values (9 `gem:ruleType` triples): coverage-scope (2), eligibility (2), credentialed-actor (1), documentation (1), service-standard (1), non-coverage (1), payment-rule (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit category: Durable Medical Equipment (reuse). 1 provider credential (`credentialPhysician`, reuse). 8 clinical-concept links — 6 mints + 2 reuses. 2 policy-to-policy references (`tn36` mint + reciprocal `revisesPolicy`; `pub100_02_ch13` reuse).

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | Indications and Limitations of Coverage: reimbursement for rental or purchase of a medically necessary seat lift, prescribed by a physician, for severe arthritis of the hip or knee / muscular dystrophy / other neuromuscular diseases, where therapeutic benefit is determined | coverage-scope; eligibility; credentialed-actor |
| R2 | Indications and Limitations of Coverage: establishing medical necessity — evidence must show the item is in the physician's course of treatment, is likely to effect improvement or arrest or retard deterioration, and that the severity of the condition is such that the alternative would be chair or bed confinement | documentation; eligibility |
| R3 | Indications and Limitations of Coverage: coverage limited to lift types that operate smoothly, can be controlled by the patient, and effectively assist standing up and sitting down without other assistance | coverage-scope; service-standard |
| R4 | Indications and Limitations of Coverage: the spring-release type with a sudden, catapult-like motion that jolts the patient upright is excluded from coverage | non-coverage |
| R5 | Indications and Limitations of Coverage: payment for units incorporating a recliner feature is limited to the amount payable for a seat lift without the feature | payment-rule |

**Notes**
- **B1 (Cross Reference is wrong on its face — recorded as stated).** The Cross Reference field reads *"See the Medicare Benefit Policy Manual, Chapter 13 §90."* Verified at extraction: Pub. 100-02 Ch. 13 is **Rural Health Clinic (RHC) and Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) Services**, and its **§90 is "RHC and FQHC Charges, Coinsurance, Deductible, and Waivers"** — neither bears on seat lifts (DME sits at Pub. 100-02 Ch. 15 §110; Ch. 14 is Medical Devices). The existing `gemi:pub100_02_ch13` stub (minted S118 off NCD 280.1) is correctly titled; the defect is CMS's. Per source-fidelity (Core Principle #8) the reference is **recorded as stated** and linked via `referencesPolicy gemi:pub100_02_ch13` — the `gemi:pub<pub#>_ch<chapter#>` convention keys on publication and chapter, not subject matter, so the URI resolves regardless. Not repointed to Ch. 15/Ch. 14: that would assert a reference CMS did not make. The mismatch is captured in `gemi:ncd280.4`'s `gem:description` for the SME. Second instance of this shape in the corpus after NCD 280.1's stale `§180.2` pointer (recorded at S143 in `gemi:ncd180.2`'s description). Tom-confirmed.
- **B2 (5 rules).** IF/THEN heuristic. The next-best reading is 3 (fuse R1+R2 into one medical-necessity rule and R3+R4 into one device-type rule), but a downstream evaluator writes five distinct IF statements: R2's evidentiary test and R4's device-type exclusion each gate independently of R1's patient-eligibility test. Tom-confirmed.
- **B3 (R3 `service-standard`).** The enumeration glosses `service-standard` as "technical standards (FDA, CLIA, etc.)" — regulatory exemplars, but "operates smoothly, can be controlled by the patient" is a technical standard on the device itself, so the gloss is read as exemplary rather than exhaustive. Paired with `coverage-scope` because the sentence's operative effect is to narrow what is covered. Alternative considered: `coverage-scope` alone. Tom-confirmed.
- **B4 (clinical concepts — Option-B inclusive; 6 mints + 2 reuses).** **Reuses:** `conceptSeatLift` (prefLabel "Seat Lifts", minted from NCD 280.1's DME-reference table) and `conceptNeuromuscularDisease` (prefLabel "neuromuscular disease", minted from L33800) — both plurality-only collisions against the policy's "seat lift" and "other neuromuscular diseases", so the existing URIs are reused per the singular-normalization rule (existing labels retained, not renamed), exactly as NCD 280.2 handled `conceptWhiteCane`. Both surfaced by the **Plan-time** URI-collision pre-flight; without it both would have been re-minted. **Mints:** `conceptSevereArthritisOfTheHip` + `conceptSevereArthritisOfTheKnee` (the policy's "hip or knee" names two distinct qualifying joints; split per the Option-B inclusive stance, mirroring NCD 180.2's enteral/parenteral split), `conceptMuscularDystrophy`, `conceptChairOrBedConfinement` (the clinical state named as the counterfactual in R2's severity test), and two equipment concepts — `conceptSpringReleaseSeatLift` and `conceptSeatLiftWithReclinerFeature` — being the two device variants the policy actually rules on (R4, R5). `gem:ClinicalConcept` covers equipment concepts; `conceptSpringReleaseSeatLift` is linked despite its non-coverage polarity per the concept-in-non-coverage-statement discoverability rationale. Tom-confirmed.
- **B5 ("section 60-9" — worklist, not minted).** The Revision History reads *"Moved statement on payment for certain seat lifts from section 60-9, and added cross-reference."* A legacy manual section with no publication number, so it cannot be resolved to a `gemi:pub<pub#>_ch<chapter#>` URI and cannot be minted under the mint-every-referenced-policy rule. Recorded as a `related_policies` worklist entry (`reference_type: Other`, narrative-only), which per `worklist_schema.md` stays on the list indefinitely — there is no graph entity to take over its tracking. Tom-confirmed.
- **B6 (TN 36 — source URL pending, minted unsuffixed).** TN 36 is the Transmittal Information field entry and the Revision History's delivering transmittal, so it is minted as a `gem:TransmittalPolicy` stub (`planPromote`, `isInEffect true`) with the reciprocal pair `tn36 revisesPolicy ncd280.4` / `ncd280.4 referencesPolicy tn36` (Proposal B Category A). A 1989 rendition predating the CMS online transmittal archive: no rendition URL was resolvable, so it is minted under the **source-URL-pending** rule, to be backfilled at TN 36's own pass. With no rendition URL there is no basis on which to choose a URI suffix, so it mints as `gemi:tn36CIM`, consistent with the unsuffixed majority — which nudges the open transmittal-URI-suffix item one entry further from `gem_reference.md`'s mandated `gemi:tn<NN><suffix>` scheme. Tom-confirmed.
- **No codes; publication + source.** No inline HCPCS/ICD references (NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). `publicationNumber "100-3"`; `manualSectionNumber "280.4"`; `dc:source` unchanged from the stub's `…?NCDId=221` (user-confirmed at extraction). Version 1, effective 1989-05-01; no implementation date posted; 2 pp; benefit category Durable Medical Equipment (reuse).
- **Deferred proposals.** Appended `NCD 280.4` to `deferred_proposals[64]` ("Device-type-conditional coverage rules", first seen NCD 240.4.1) — R3/R4 are that pattern exactly: coverage of a generic-named device class turning on detailed device-type characteristics. `deferred_proposals[59]` ("Device-type-specific conditional coverage (per-code patient-characteristics gate)") was considered and rejected — its gate is per-code and predicated on alternatives having failed, neither of which fits. One new entry logged: **"Feature-upgrade payment cap (pay-the-base-configuration rule)"** (first seen NCD 280.4), for R5's shape — payment for an upgraded configuration capped at the base configuration's allowance. Distinct from `[6]` (bundling/unbundling, `resolved`).

### NCD 30.1 — Biofeedback Therapy

*Extracted S147 (2026-07-15). `gemi:ncd30.1_r1` – `gemi:ncd30.1_r3`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-15 (Session 147). 3 rules at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; no inline HCPCS/ICD codes — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (biofeedback therapy); domain axis omitted per convention. `gemi:ncd30.1` was a `planPromote` NCD stub (minted during NCD 160.7's extraction from its Cross Reference section), promoted to a fully-extracted `planDone` policy. **First policy of the §4 item 3 cross-reference staleness sweep** — the stub's existence was the question, and it is answered: NCD 30.1 is live in the MCD at `NCDId=41` (Tom-verified), so this stub is *not* a stale cross-reference and its `isInEffect=true` is now attested by the document rather than inherited from NCD 160.7's citation. Longstanding Version 1 NCD. 3 distinct axis-2 `rule_type` values (3 `gem:ruleType` triples): coverage-scope (1), non-coverage (1), service-definition (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit categories: Incident to a physician's professional Service, Outpatient Physical Therapy Services, Physicians' Services (all reuse). No provider credential. 25 clinical-concept links — 22 mints + 3 reuses. 1 policy reference (Pub. 100-02 Ch. 15).

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | Indications and Limitations of Coverage, sentence 1: biofeedback covered only when reasonable and necessary for muscle re-education of specific muscle groups, or for treating pathological muscle abnormalities of spasticity, incapacitating muscle spasm or weakness, **and** more conventional treatments (heat, cold, massage, exercise, support) have not been successful | coverage-scope |
| R2 | Indications and Limitations of Coverage, sentence 2: not covered for treatment of ordinary muscle tension states or for psychosomatic conditions | non-coverage |
| R3 | Item/Service Description, paragraph 2: biofeedback therapy differs from electromyography (a diagnostic procedure recording the electrical properties of skeletal muscle); an EMG device may be used to provide feedback with certain types of biofeedback | service-definition |

**Notes**
- **B1 (the stub was misfiled as ANNOTATION-ONLY; reclassified and promoted).** `gemi:ncd30.1` sat in NCD 160.7's `ANNOTATION-ONLY STUBS` sub-section — defined in `SKILL.md` §File Layout Conventions slot 6 as stubs "not expected to be fully populated by their own extraction passes" — while carrying `gem:planPromote`, which asserts the opposite. The stub's own `gem:description` said "to be populated by its own extraction pass", so the block contradicted its own header. The cohort settles it: slot 6 named three NCD examples cited by NCD 160.7, and the other two — `ncd160.2` and `ncd160.7.1` — are both `planDone` today (1 and 15 rules). The classification has now proved wrong on all three. NCD 30.1 is treated as an ordinary policy stub, promoted to its own top-level section, and the now-empty ANNOTATION-ONLY sub-section under NCD 160.7 is collapsed. `SKILL.md` slot 6's stale example list corrected in the same Generate (an instance of handoff §4 item 2's hardcoded-list family). Tom-confirmed.
- **B2 (effective date — Other Versions vs. Tracking).** Tracking Information states the effective date of this version "has not been posted"; the Other Versions table gives Version 1 as 01/01/1966 – N/A. `policyEffectiveDate "1966-01-01"^^xsd:date` taken from the Other Versions column (NCD 270.4 / NCD 280.2 precedent, preserving the every-processed-policy-has-an-effective-date invariant); no `policyImplementationDate` (none given). Precedent-settled, not a borderline.
- **B3 (Item/Service Description ¶1 dropped).** The biofeedback definition ("provides visual, auditory or other evidence of the status of certain body functions…" plus the electrical-device transformation sentence) is dropped as a rule under corollary #2 — its full verbatim is carried on `gemi:conceptBiofeedbackTherapy`'s `gem:description`. R1 executes by matching the therapy, not by re-reading what biofeedback is. S99 precedent (R49/R54/R55 dropped after extending their concept descriptions to full verbatim).
- **B4 (Item/Service Description ¶2 kept as R3 — genuine borderline).** The EMG-differentiation paragraph is the S99 **R39** shape: a two-device framing whose content is emergent across a pair of concepts rather than a discrete fact on either. `conceptBiofeedbackTherapy` cannot be its definition home (the paragraph is partly about EMG); `conceptElectromyography` cannot either (it is partly about biofeedback, and its `gem:description` is already L36524's verbatim, which this pass does not overwrite). Corollary #2's escape hatch is therefore unavailable and corollary #3 (verbatim-capture posture) governs. Pattern 3 — the two sentences are one cohesive unit (the distinction, then its qualification). **Defensible alternative considered:** drop it, on the ground that the EMG definition proper already lives on `conceptElectromyography` and the residue is contrast rather than criterion. Tom took the keep.
- **B5 (Chapter 15 parenthetical dropped as a rule; reference retained).** *"(See the Medicare Benefit Policy Manual, Chapter 15, for general coverage requirements about physical therapy requirements.)"* is a bare navigational pointer — it routes the reader and asserts no coverage effect — so it is dropped under the executability test (§ "Scope-boundary sentences: capture vs. drop"; L33718 D4 precedent). `gem:referencesPolicy gemi:pub100_02_ch15` preserves the provenance (reuse; the chapter stub's 9th inbound edge). `conceptPhysicalTherapy` is linked from this sentence under the cross-reference-NOTE convention (presence, not governance; NCD 160.2 S113 precedent).
- **B6 (clinical concepts — Option-B inclusive; 22 mints + 3 reuses).** **Reuses:** `conceptElectromyography`, `conceptSkeletalMuscle` and `conceptWeakness` — all three exist from L36524 and all three are exact prefLabel matches to this policy's wording. **The conventional-treatment list.** R1's *"more conventional treatments (heat, cold, massage, exercise, support)"* names five members explicitly, so the composite-captured-whole rule does not shield them: each is independently named, not a word-part of a composite label. Presented as (a) category only, (b) category + all five, (c) category + `massage`/`exercise` only. **Tom: (b)** — `conceptConventionalTreatment` plus `conceptHeat`, `conceptCold`, `conceptMassage`, `conceptExercise`, `conceptSupport`. The argument against (b) was that `support` and `cold` are near-contentless as standalone individuals; the argument for it is that Option-B is the standing default, single-term recall is the design goal, and trimming by perceived usefulness is exactly what the anti-curation signal forbids. Remaining mints: `conceptBiofeedbackTherapy` (corollary #2 definition home, full ¶1 verbatim), `conceptAbnormalBodilyCondition`, the six body functions a biofeedback device transforms (`conceptHeartRate`, `conceptBloodPressure`, `conceptSkinTemperature`, `conceptSalivation`, `conceptPeripheralVasomotorActivity`, `conceptGrossMuscleTone` — the last two composite-flagged), `conceptElectromyographyDevice` (B7), `conceptMuscleReEducation`, `conceptPathologicalMuscleAbnormality`, `conceptSpasticity`, `conceptIncapacitatingMuscleSpasm`, `conceptOrdinaryMuscleTensionState`, `conceptPsychosomaticCondition` (singular-normalized where the source is plural), and `conceptPhysicalTherapy` (B5). The two non-coverage concepts are linked per the concept-in-non-coverage-statement discoverability rationale.
- **B7 (`electromyography device` minted, not folded into `electromyography`).** The existing `conceptElectromyography` (prefLabel "electromyography", from L36524) names the *procedure*; NCD 30.1's *"An electromyography device may be used…"* names the *device*. A different noun defaults to mint under the catalog-phrasings rule; any equivalence is the SME taxonomy pass's business, not extraction's.
- **Not minted.** "specific muscle groups" (a scope qualifier on `conceptMuscleReEducation`, not an independently named clinical entity) and the generic body-function / bodily-signal vocabulary of ¶1 (word-parts, per the composite rule).
- **No codes; no credentials; publication + source.** No inline HCPCS/ICD references (NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). No current-prose mention of a credentialed role performing a required step → zero `gem:requiresProviderCredential` links under the strict-prose rule (the three benefit categories name physician settings, but a benefit category is metadata, not a credential mention). `publicationNumber "100-3"`; `manualSectionNumber "30.1"`; `dc:source` unchanged from the stub's `…?NCDId=41` — Tom-verified live at this URL, which is what resolved the §4 item 3 question for this stub. Version 1, effective 1966-01-01; 2 pp. Document carries no Cross Reference, Transmittal Information, Revision History or NCA sections.

### NCD 160.24 — Deep Brain Stimulation for Essential Tremor and Parkinson’s Disease

Version 1, effective and implemented 2003-04-01 (both posted in Tracking — no Other-Versions inference needed, unlike NCD 30.1 / 280.2 / 270.4). 6 distinct axis-2 `rule_type` values (12 `gem:ruleType` triples): credentialed-actor (4), service-standard (3), eligibility (2), coverage-scope (1), non-coverage (1), setting-definition (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit categories: Physicians’ Services, Prosthetic Devices (both reuse). **4 provider-credential mints** (`credentialNeurosurgeon`, `credentialOperativeTeam`, `credentialPhysicianSpecializingInMovementDisorders`, `credentialHospitalMedicalCenter`). 56 clinical-concept links — 49 mints + 7 reuses. 13 policy-to-policy references — 9 reuse-links to revision-history transmittals already in the graph from NCD 160.18’s S131 pass, plus `tn167` (reuse, enriched) and 3 stubs minted (`tn128`, `pmAB03023`, `cag00124N`); 1 change-request stub minted (`cr2553`).

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | §Indications, opening: effective 2003-04-01, Medicare covers unilateral or bilateral thalamic VIM DBS for ET and/or Parkinsonian tremor, and unilateral or bilateral STN or GPi DBS for PD, only under the enumerated conditions | coverage-scope |
| R2 | §Indications, condition 1: DBS devices reasonable and necessary only if FDA-approved for DBS, or used per FDA-approved protocols governing Category B IDE DBS clinical trials | service-standard |
| R3 | §Indications, condition 2: thalamic VIM DBS requires **all** of a–c (ET or tremor-dominant idiopathic PD diagnosis; marked disabling tremor level 3–4 on Fahn-Tolosa-Marin despite optimal medical therapy; willingness/ability to cooperate) | eligibility |
| R4 | §Indications, condition 3: STN or GPi DBS requires **all** of a–e (PD diagnosis by ≥2 cardinal features; advanced idiopathic PD by Hoehn and Yahr or UPDRS part III; L-dopa responsive with defined "on" periods; persistent disabling symptoms or drug side effects despite optimal medical therapy; willingness/ability to cooperate) | eligibility |
| R5 | §Indications, exclusion list: not reasonable and necessary and not covered for ET or PD patients with **any** of six conditions (non-idiopathic PD / "Parkinson’s Plus"; cognitive impairment, dementia or depression; current psychosis or alcohol/drug abuse; structural lesions as etiology; previous movement-disorder surgery in the affected basal ganglion; significant contraindicating co-morbidities) | non-coverage |
| R6 | §Indications: DBS-implanted patients should not be exposed to diathermy (shortwave, microwave, ultrasound) or any type of MRI | service-standard |
| R7 | §Indications: DBS should be performed with extreme caution in patients with cardiac pacemakers or other electronically controlled implants | service-standard |
| R8 | §Indications, provider/facility criteria: neurosurgeons must be properly trained, have movement-disorder surgical experience including DBS therapy, and have stereotactic experience | credentialed-actor |
| R9 | §Indications, provider/facility criteria: operative teams must have training and experience with DBS systems (localization, implantation technique, device characteristics) | credentialed-actor |
| R10 | §Indications, provider/facility criteria: physicians specializing in movement disorders must be involved in both patient selection and post-procedure care | credentialed-actor |
| R11 | §Indications, provider/facility criteria: hospital medical centers must have brain imaging (MRI and/or CT), stereotactic-equipped operating rooms, and support services for intra/postoperative complications | setting-definition, credentialed-actor |

**Notes**
- **B1 (rule granularity — 11 rules; the criteria and exclusion lists each fold to one rule).** The register carries two apparently-conflicting precedents: NCD 160.7 (S50) atomized its §B.2 a–e into five δ-prefixed rules; NCD 160.12 (S139) folded a nine-criteria inclusion list into one `eligibility` rule and a five-item exclusion list into one `non-coverage` rule. **The conflict is only apparent — the discriminator is in-rule cross-references,** stated in 160.12’s B-c ("the lists carry no letter-label cross-references") and confirmed by 160.7’s own note (its items say "With respect to item a" and "required to satisfy item c", so the letters are semantically addressable and the items must exist separately). NCD 160.24’s lists carry **no** in-rule cross-references, so the S139 disjunctive-fold precedent governs and the IF/THEN heuristic agrees (one all-of gate = one IF; internal ORs do not fork). R3, R4, R5, R8 and R11 each fold their lettered/numbered items inline with the source labels preserved verbatim. Tom-confirmed.
- **B2 (NCDs named inside revision-history entries — NOT minted; Tom: (b)).** TN 12440’s Revision-History entry names **NCD 90.2** ("to make changes to NCD 90.2, Next Generation Sequencing, spreadsheet to align with revisions being made to CR 13278"); TN 1658’s names **NCD 210.3** and **NCD 20.33**. `SKILL.md` §Three Code Contexts → "Revision-history references" addresses this shape by name — *"a rescind-reason that names a different NCD … is not used to gate the mint"* — and reads as requiring the mint. **The S131 precedent pass did the opposite:** NCD 160.18 carries `tn12440` and the identical boilerplate entry, and `ncd90.2` is not in the graph. Rule text and establishing precedent disagree.
