**Notes**
- **B1 (R1 shape — Pattern 3, all three sentences).** One IF/THEN either way (IF IPV AND home setting THEN not covered), so the decision is only the string's extent. Sentence 3 opens *"Therefore,"* and is not self-contained, which is Pattern 1's defining requirement; corollary #3's verbatim-capture posture keeps CMS's stated evidentiary basis with the conclusion it grounds. NCD 240.3 R1 (rationale-and-conclusion kept whole, in one sentence) and NCD 280.2 R1 (the rationale sentence *is* the rule) are the two nearest shapes. **Defensible alternative considered:** Pattern 1 on the *"Therefore"* sentence alone, dropping sentences 1–2 as evidentiary motivation under the "context or motivation" test. Tom took Pattern 3.
- **B2 (Item/Service Description dropped as a rule).** The four-sentence paragraph is a pure device definition; its full verbatim is carried on `gemi:conceptIntrapulmonaryPercussiveVentilator`'s `gem:description`, and R1 executes by matching the device, not by re-reading what an IPV is. Corollary #2; NCD 30.1 B3 precedent. **Defensible alternative considered:** keep as R2 `service-definition` on the NCD 30.1 **B4** reading — sentence 2 (*"Instead of a therapist clapping or slapping the patient's chest wall, the IPV delivers…"*) is a two-therapy contrast, and B4 retained exactly that shape. B4's corollary-#2 escape hatch was *unavailable* there because `conceptElectromyography` already carried L36524's verbatim; here both `conceptIntrapulmonaryPercussiveVentilator` and `conceptChestPhysicalTherapy` are fresh mints from this pass, so each can carry what it needs and the hatch is open. Tom took the drop.
- **B3 (R1 — `setting-definition` alongside `non-coverage`).** The setting is load-bearing inside the antecedent, not decoration: a downstream evaluator writes `IF procedure == IPV AND place-of-service == home THEN deny`. **A52519 R2** is the direct precedent — a denial conditioned on the nursing-facility POS, tagged `non-coverage` + `setting-definition` (S60) — and the `gem:RuleType` definition of `settingDefinition` reads "positive definition + exclusions", which reaches exclusions on its face. Not a second rule; a second tag on R1. **Defensible alternative considered:** `non-coverage` alone, per **NCD 280.2 B2**'s no-over-tag posture. Distinguishable — 280.2's second flavour was definitional colour *about the item*, whereas here the setting is a condition *in the rule* — but a reader could fairly call "the home setting" a scope qualifier on a single non-coverage rule. Tom took both tags.
- **B4 (`tn100CIM revisesPolicy tn95CIM` asserted at mint).** *"05/1997 - Changed effective date of TN 95 to 07/14/1997. (TN 100)"* is a directly-stated transmittal-to-transmittal fact, which is the rationale behind SKILL.md §Revision-history references' mint-time carve-out; both endpoints are minted in this turn, as the mint-every-referenced-policy rule guarantees. **Defensible alternative considered:** withhold until TN 100's own pass — the carve-out's worked phrasing is *"rescinded and replaced"*, and changing an effective date is an amendment, not a replacement. Tom took the assert. No transmittal→NCD `revisesPolicy` is asserted in either direction (mint-now-analyze-later; §Link polarity).
- **B5 (`tn95CIM gem:isInEffect false`).** TN 100 is NCD 240.5's Transmittal Information entry and amended TN 95; TN 95 is a Revision-History-only predecessor. `tn132CIM` precedent ("Delivered the original Version 1 (superseded); `gem:isInEffect` false"). **Defensible alternative considered:** `true` — TN 95's substantive change (home use not covered) *is* the current text; only its effective date was superseded. The tension is real and is a reading of `isInEffect` itself: deliverer-of-record versus content-still-stands. Tom took `false` (deliverer-of-record). Worth a project-level note if the predicate is ever formally defined.
- **B6 (`mini-burst` + `respiratory gas` — two mints, not one composite).** The source reads *"delivers mini-bursts (more than 200 per minute) of respiratory gasses"*: the parenthetical interrupts between head and complement, so the source does not treat the phrase as a contiguous compound, and two individuals maximize single-term recall. **Defensible alternative considered:** one composite, mirroring **A52495**'s `gemi:conceptPressurizedGasMinibursts` — the same device, described by a sibling policy. That precedent's phrase *is* a contiguous compound noun ("pressurized gas minibursts"), which is what distinguishes it. Tom took the split. Both new individuals are near-neighbours of the A52495 pair; any equivalence is the SME taxonomy pass's business (catalog-phrasings).
- **B7 (`good pulmonary care` — qualifier retained).** Catalog-phrasings: the policy's own wording is captured. Corpus supports qualifier-retaining care concepts (`conceptStandardWoundCare`, `conceptConventionalCare`). **Defensible alternative considered:** drop to "pulmonary care" by analogy to NCD 30.1 B6's *"more conventional treatments"* → `conceptConventionalTreatment`. Distinguishable: "more" modifies the comparison, "good" attributes a standard to the care itself. Tom took the retain.
- **B8 (`home setting` / `hospital environment`) — DECIDED WRONG AT THE PLAN TURN; CORRECTED IN-SESSION.** The Plan turn recommended not minting, on the stated ground that "the graph carries zero setting-of-care individuals across 1,463 pre-pass concepts." That count was true and irrelevant. Settings are not `gem:ClinicalConcept` individuals — they are their own class family, **`gem:HealthcareSetting`** (introduced S117 as deferred-proposal [70]), linked by `gem:refersToHealthcareSetting`, with **8 individuals** and 14 links across 7 policies. `gemi:settingHome`'s own description names this policy's exact phrasing in scope: *"Covers both locus-of-furnishing statements ('covered in the home', 'in the home setting')…"*. The pre-flight queried one class and read its silence as a fact about the graph; it never asked whether another modeling slot existed. **A52519 — cited in this same register as B3's precedent — carries `refersToHealthcareSetting settingHome`**, so the disconfirming evidence sat inside a query already run. Compounding it, the correction's first count ("4 individuals") was also wrong: four more are typed `gem:ClinicSetting`, a subclass, and a bare `rdf:type` probe on an inference-free graph does not return them. **Correction applied S148:** `gemi:ncd240.5 gem:refersToHealthcareSetting gemi:settingHome`. **Still owed:** "the hospital environment" has no member to link — the vocabulary has only `settingOutpatientHospital`, and this policy's comparator is inpatient chest physiotherapy. It awaits `settingHospital` from the [70] settings rebuild (worklist, approved-unbuilt), which Tom scoped at S148 to a SKOS hierarchy plus a label normalization. B3 (`setting-definition` on R1) is unaffected and, if anything, reinforced. **Root cause, shared with three other S148 findings:** a claim about the graph that nothing executes — see the handoff §5.3 lesson.
- **B9 (`tn95CIM` / `tn100CIM` — provisional CIM suffix, not bare).** Three independent supports. **(i) Dating:** both Revision-History entries are 1997; the Pub. 100-03 NCD Manual did not exist until 2003, so the renditions belong to the predecessor Coverage Issues Manual (HCFA Pub. 6). **(ii) Corroboration:** cms.gov CIM renditions carry NCD 240.5's IPV text verbatim under "COVERAGE ISSUES – DURABLE MEDICAL EQUIPMENT", and `gemi:tn132CIM` / `gemi:tn150CIM` are already in the graph. **S148 correction:** the Plan turn recorded the section as §60-22, taken from an unverified `web_search` snippet. The **verified** R144CIM rendition (fetched; cover page "Coverage Issues Manual / Transmittal 144 / OCTOBER 4, 2001", footer CMS-Pub. 6) lists in its table of contents *"Intrapulmonary Percussive Ventilator (IPV) 60-21"* — §60-22 is Vagus Nerve Stimulation. The corroboration stands and is stronger on the verified document: a CIM rendition's own ToC lists the whole 240.5 / 280.x DME cluster. This was the same failure the S148 handoff's own lesson names, committed in the paragraph that names it. **(iii) Collision:** the graph already holds bare `gemi:tn96NCD` (`dc:source` R96NCD.pdf, 15 Oct 2008) and `gemi:tn103NCD` (R103NCD.pdf, eff. 2009-03-03), so the NCD-Manual series demonstrably has its own TN 95 and TN 100 in the 2008–09 range; bare minting would seat a 1997 CIM document in the slot adjacent to a 2008 NCD-Manual sibling. Precedent: `tn26CIM` / `tn132CIM` / `tn150CIM` — all "provisional CIM suffix", all source-URL-pending. **Defensible alternative considered:** bare `tn95` / `tn100`, per handoff §4 item 7's unsuffixed majority and TN 128's S147 reasoning ("no rendition URL → no basis to choose one"). TN 128 had no dating evidence; these two do. Tom took the CIM suffix. Bears directly on §4 item 7.
- **Source URLs pending (both stubs).** `web_search` established that CMS's public transmittal archive begins at 2000 ("The transmittals for 2000 through 2012 have been archived"), so no 1997 rendition is published. Neither stub carries `dc:source`; no URL was invented and none constructed by analogy (SKILL.md "No URLs by analogy"). Backfill at each transmittal's own analysis pass. `tn26CIM` precedent verbatim.
- **Content-propagation observations (both `reflected`).** TN 95's claimed change ("Provided that home use is not covered") is reflected — the current Indications section reads *"Therefore, IPV in the home setting is not covered."* TN 100's claimed change (effective date → 07/14/1997) is reflected — Tracking Information posts that date. Both recorded in the stubs' `gem:description` per §Content-propagation observation.
- **Not minted.** "a therapist" (a provider role, not a clinical concept — SKILL.md excludes "physician" by name); "clapping" / "slapping" (verb-predicates describing manual chest physical therapy, preserved verbatim on `conceptChestPhysicalTherapy` and `conceptChestWall`); "more than 200 per minute" (a numeric threshold — the measurement concept `conceptDeliveryRate` is modeled, the number is not).
- **No codes; no credentials; publication + source.** No inline HCPCS/ICD references (NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Zero `gem:requiresProviderCredential` links: the only role in current prose, *"a therapist"*, appears in a contrastive clause and is expressly **not** the performer of the governed step, so the strict-prose rule does not license a link (NCD 30.1 / 240.3 / 280.2 precedent, all zero). `publicationNumber "100-3"`; `manualSectionNumber "240.5"`; `dc:source` set from the stub's `…?NCDId=229` to the user-supplied `…?ncdid=229&ncdver=1&bc=0` — a URL confirmation/refresh at the policy's own Plan turn, explicitly a **non-finding** (§"Medicare URLs are not canonical; the user's URL is"). Version 1, effective 1997-07-14; 2 pp; text-layer PDF (Skia/PDF, `pdffonts` shows 4 embedded fonts — no OCR); 276 words; pure ASCII, no line-end hyphens (S102 de-hyphenation does not fire). The document carries no Coding Information, Cross Reference, Claims Processing Instructions or NCA sections. The MCD benefit-category disclaimer ("Please Note: This may not be an exhaustive list…") is not captured as a rule, consistent with NCD 240.3 / 280.2 / 30.1.

### NCD 200.2 — Nebulized Beta Adrenergic Agonist Therapy for Lung Diseases

*Extracted S150 (2026-07-16). `gemi:ncd200.2_r1`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-16 (Session 150). 1 rule at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; no inline HCPCS/ICD codes — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (nebulized beta adrenergic agonist therapy / Durable Medical Equipment); domain axis omitted per convention. `gemi:ncd200.2` was a `planPromote` NCD stub (minted during A52466 "Nebulizers - Policy Article" extraction, which cites it as a related national coverage document), promoted to a fully-extracted `planDone` policy (stub collapsed from the A52466 POLICY STUBS block into its own top-level section; workflow entry moved `planPromote / isInEffect=True → planDone / isInEffect=True`, both headers recomputed from the file). Version 1 NCD, effective 09/10/2007, implemented 01/22/2008 — the only version; the Other Versions table lists V1 alone. 2 axis-2 `rule_type` values (2 `gem:ruleType` triples): coverage-scope (1), statutory-framing (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit category: Durable Medical Equipment (reuse). No provider credential, healthcare setting, or qualification group. 4 clinical-concept links — 2 mints (`conceptNebulizedBetaAdrenergicAgonistTherapy`, `conceptLungDisease`) + 2 reuses (`conceptCOPD`, `conceptAsthma`). 2 policy-to-policy references, both new mints (`tn79NCD`, `cag00354N`); `cr5820` minted and wired from `tn79NCD` via `gem:transmitsChangeRequest`.

**The third "no NCD is appropriate" policy, and the first that was not retired to get there.** NCD 180.2 and NCD 240.2.2 reached this shape by *removal* — each had substantive coverage, CMS withdrew it, and a later transmittal retitled the section RETIRED. NCD 200.2 was **created** in this shape at Version 1 in 2007: §B and §C are both `N/A`, §D declines to determine, and no version ever said otherwise. Same operative content, opposite provenance. The distinction is not currently derivable from the graph — see B5.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | §D (Other), the whole section: after examining the available medical evidence CMS determines that no national coverage determination is appropriate at this time; §1862(a)(1)(A) decisions should be made by local MACs through a local coverage determination process or case-by-case adjudication; *See Heckler v. Ringer*, 466 U.S. 602, 617 (1984); *see also* 68 Fed. Reg. 63692, 63693 (November 7, 2003) | coverage-scope, statutory-framing |

**Notes**
- **B1 (rule count — 1).** §B and §C are both `N/A`; §D is the entire operative document. One IF/THEN for a downstream evaluator (IF claim is for nebulized beta adrenergic agonist therapy THEN no national rule applies; defer to the MAC), so the citations and the delegation clause stay with the determination they qualify (corollary #3, verbatim capture). **`ncd180.2_r1` and `ncd240.2.2_r1` are the direct precedents** — both fold the identical two-sentence determination-plus-delegation shape into one rule with the same two type tags. **Defensible alternative considered:** split the delegation sentence into R2 `procedural` — the NCD 240.2 §D MAC-discretion cluster (B6 / R19+R20+R21) is real precedent for MAC-discretion rules standing alone. Distinguishable: there the three rules answered *logically distinct questions* (initial discretion, duration, renewal) and each had independent claim consequence; here the delegation has no content beyond the determination's own negative space — it says only "because there is no national rule, the MAC decides," which is what "no NCD is appropriate" already means. Tom took 1.
- **B2 (clinical-concept scope — 4, not 2 and not 8).** The precedents take the **title's service + indication only**, not §A background prose: `ncd180.2` → enteral / parenteral nutritional therapy; `ncd240.2.2` → cluster headache + home oxygen. Applied here, the title yields `conceptNebulizedBetaAdrenergicAgonistTherapy` + `conceptLungDisease`. `conceptCOPD` and `conceptAsthma` are added as **reuses** because §A names them as the diseases at issue and both individuals already exist — but they are exemplars ("lung diseases **such as** COPD and asthma"), so `conceptLungDisease` carries the policy's actual scope and is not redundant with them. **Not minted:** `levalbuterol`, `racemic albuterol`, `beta adrenergic agonist`, `bronchodilator`, `metered dose inhaler`, `dry powdered inhaler` — all §A background with no coverage consequence in a policy that determines nothing; `conceptAlbuterol` already exists from A52466, which is where the nebulizer drug-level vocabulary lives. Composite-concept rule applied to the service name (captured whole, no constituent fabricated). Tom took 4.
- **B3 (`tn79NCD` manual token and URL).** `NCD` token, `gem:publicationNumber "100-03"`, per S149 D3. Priority 1, **verified** rendition filename: NCD 200.2's Transmittal Information posts the Coverage Transmittal Link, printed in the MCD rendition with a PDF line-wrap artifact (`Regulations-andGuidance`); Tom supplied the de-wrapped URL at the Plan turn and it matches the pattern 23 corpus transmittals already use. 2007 issue date — Pub. 100-03 existed from 2003, so the era gate does not disqualify and does not need to.
- **B4 (`tn79NCD` carries NO `gem:revisesPolicy` edge — a correction to this pass's own confirmed manifest).** The Plan turn's manifest said `revisesPolicy ncd200.2`; generation did not write it. `gem:revisesPolicy` is defined as linking "a CMS Policy to another CMS Policy **that it revises**," and TN 79 *created* §200.2 at Version 1 — there was no prior version to revise. **The corpus is split on this and offers no clean rule:** six V1 NCDs carry an inbound edge from their deliverer (`tn78CIM`→160.13/160.7, `tn144CIM`→230.18, `tn149NCD`→160.27, `tn167CIM`→160.24, `tn36CIM`→280.4) and six do not (210.10, 240.2.1, 240.4.1, 240.5, 240.9, 280.6). The six *with* edges are all CIM-era sections whose NCD-Manual V1 descends from pre-existing CIM content — those transmittals genuinely moved or restated something. **NCD 240.5 is the shape-match and the freshest precedent** (S148): its V1 deliverer TN 95 "provided that home use is not covered" — the same "provided X policy" Revision-History wording as TN 79 — carries no edge, and its description defers the question ("including whether it revised NCD 240.5") to the transmittal's own pass. Followed that. **Flagged for Tom:** this is an unguarded convention with a 6–6 corpus split and no written rule; the `referencesPolicy` link from `ncd200.2` preserves the connection either way, so nothing is lost if Tom prefers the edge.
- **B5 (the "no NCD" shape is not modeled, and now has three members).** `gem:isInEffect` is doing double duty and disagrees with itself across the three: 180.2 and 240.2.2 are `true` (the RETIRED-titled section still exists in Pub. 100-03), `ncd280.13` is `false` (retired 2012, incorporated into 160.27, section gone), and 200.2 is `true` (never retired at all). A reader cannot distinguish "active policy that declines to determine," "retired-in-place," and "retired-and-removed" without reading `gem:description` prose. Logged to `deferred_proposals` as **[97] Policy status vocabulary**. The S149 "prose that cites the corpus is a claim about the corpus" lesson applies: three policies now carry this distinction in prose and nothing checks it.
- **Source-fidelity finding (captured, not acted on).** The Revision History reads *"12/2007 - Provided noncoverage policy. Effective date 09/10/2007. (TN 79 ) (CR5820)"*. **CMS's own summary of the transmittal contradicts the document the transmittal delivered:** §C (Nationally Non-Covered Indications) is `N/A` and §D declines to determine rather than denying. Captured verbatim on `gemi:ncd200.2`, `gemi:tn79NCD` and `gemi:cr5820` per corollary #3; it does **not** drive `ruleType_nonCoverage`. Contrast NCD 240.5, where the parallel Revision-History wording ("provided that home use is not covered") *was* borne out and R1 is correctly `non-coverage`.
- **Document characteristics.** 3 pp (MCD rendition, footer 1/3–3/3); ~330 words of substantive text. The MCD benefit-category disclaimer ("Please Note: This may not be an exhaustive list…") is not captured as a rule, consistent with NCD 240.5 / 240.3 / 280.2 / 30.1. No Coding Information, Cross Reference, or Claims Processing Instructions section. The NCA section names CAG-00354N without an NCAId, so that stub's URL is pending.


### NCD 240.1 — Lung Volume Reduction Surgery (Reduction Pneumoplasty)

*Extracted S151 (2026-07-16). `gemi:ncd240.1_r1` … `_r14`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-16 (Session 151). 14 rules at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; no inline HCPCS/ICD codes — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (lung volume reduction surgery); domain axis omitted per convention. `gemi:ncd240.1` was a `planPromote` NCD stub (minted during A52467 extraction, which cites it as a Related National Coverage Document), promoted to a fully-extracted `planDone` policy (stub collapsed from the A52467 POLICY STUB block into its own top-level section; workflow entry moved `planPromote / isInEffect=True → planDone / isInEffect=True`, both headers recomputed from the file, not incremented). Version 3 NCD, effective 11/17/2005, implemented 03/02/2006; NCDId=119, 6 pp. 7 axis-2 `rule_type` values across 15 `gem:ruleType` triples: coverage-scope (4), credentialed-actor (3), eligibility (2), non-coverage (3), service-definition (1), payment-rule (1), statutory-framing (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit categories: Inpatient Hospital Services; Outpatient Hospital Services Incident to a Physician's Service; Physicians' Services (all reuse). 52 clinical-concept links — 42 mints + 10 reuses (`conceptArterialBloodGas`, `conceptBodyMassIndexBMI`, `conceptCOPD`, `conceptClinicalTrial`, `conceptEKG`, `conceptEchocardiogram`, `conceptExerciseTesting`, `conceptFEV1`, `conceptPO2`, `conceptPulmonaryEmphysema`). 9 provider-credential links — 8 mints + 1 reuse (`credentialTreatingPhysician`). No healthcare setting, no qualification group. 7 policy-to-policy references, all new mints (`tn44NCD`, `tn3NCD`, `tn102CIM`, `tn83CIM`, `tn768CP`, `cag00115R`, `cag00115R2`); `cr4149` and `cr2688` minted and wired from `tn44NCD` / `tn3NCD` via `gem:transmitsChangeRequest`.

**The corpus's first multi-version rule set.** Tom supplied all three renditions (V1 eff. 08/11/1997, V2 eff. 01/01/2004, V3 eff. 11/17/2005). Nine rules are V3's own text; **five are retained from V1/V2 under the S151 retention rule** — the first time GEM has carried rule text a policy's current version does not contain. See B1 and B2.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| R2 | V3 §B opening gate: effective for services on/after 01/01/2004, LVRS reasonable and necessary only when all of the following are met (note varying dates for facility criteria in §B.3) | coverage-scope |

| R9 | V3 §C.2: all other indications for LVRS not otherwise specified remain noncovered | non-coverage |

| R11 | **Retained (V1).** Itemization of what "services integral to the study" includes: qualification tests for randomization, LVRS, and follow-up tests necessary during participation | coverage-scope |
| R12 | **Retained (V1).** Services prohibited by the Act are not covered; pulmonary rehabilitation and pulmonary function testing are covered, oral steroids are not, as self-administrable and statutorily excluded under §1862(s)(2) | non-coverage, statutory-framing |

**Notes**
- **B1 (rule count — 14, not 9).** R1–R9 are V3's text. R10–R14 exist under the **S151 retention rule** (Tom, S151): *where an earlier version states a rule, concept, setting or beneficiary group, a later version does not, and no revision history in any version reports the change, nothing changed — the factor stands until a specific statement removes it.* Sequence is tested V1→intervening→newest: if V2 removes something V3 cannot re-add it; if V2 is silent, V3 inherits V1 unchanged. **Applied:** TN 44's Revision-History entry reports only *"Modified requirements for facilities eligible to perform lung volume reduction surgery"* — nothing about the NETT-participant leg V3 drops, so R10 stands. TN 3's entry reports only the coverage expansion — nothing about the four V1 factors V2 drops, so R11–R14 stand. **Not retained (two):** V1's blanket *"not generally covered … insufficient medical evidence"* default — V2 and V3 both restate the residual-noncoverage ground in narrower form (R9 catch-all + R1 approach limit), so it was specifically changed, not silently dropped; and V2's NHLBI-threshold/Medicare-lung-transplant facility criteria, whose replacement TN 44's entry **does** report. **Δ from the Plan turn:** the manifest said 13. B2' (rules declare themselves by existence; text = the last version that spoke to them) plus corollary #3 (capture all verbatim forms, never merge) forced R10 and R11 apart — V2 restated the NETT leg in condensed form, V1's itemization sentence is a separate silent absence, and merging V1 and V2 text into one `gem:ruleDescription` would be exactly the merge corollary #3 forbids. 13 → 14.
- **B2 (retained rules carry no provenance marker — Tom, S151).** A `gem:PolicyRule` declares itself by its existence; when a later version revises it the text changes, when a later version deletes it the individual is deleted. So R10–R14 are ordinary rule individuals with `dc:source gemi:ncd240.1` like the other nine, and nothing in the graph says "this came from V1." The narrative lives here and in `gem:workflowDescription` on `gemi:ncd240.1`. **Consequence worth naming:** the retention decision is not derivable from the graph — a reader cannot tell R13 from R1 without this register. That is the multi-version-management gap, logged as `deferred_proposals[98]`.
- **B3 (the assessment table folds to one rule; the exclusion list folds to one).** S139/NCD-160.24 discriminator: a list folds when no member is cross-referenced *from inside the policy's own rules*. §B.1's ten categories carry no in-rule cross-reference; §C.1's a–e likewise. §C.1.e references §B(1) — but that is an **outward** reference from C.1 to B.1, which is why B.1 is separately addressable and stands as R3 rather than folding into R2. Defensible alternative considered: split §B.1 into 10 rules on the table's own row structure. Rejected — the rows are assessment *categories*, not independently-dispositive conditions; a downstream evaluator generates one IF (does the patient satisfy the B.1 criteria set?), which is exactly how §C.1.e refers to it.
- **B4 (transmittal edges — the S151 transmittal-edge rule, and the closure of §4 item 14).** Tom's rule (S151): *the transmittal→policy edge is `gem:revisesPolicy` if the transmittal describes any change — New, Change/Revision, or Delete — and `gem:referencesPolicy` if it merely mentions the policy.* Applied: `tn83CIM` (New — created the section, 12/1995), `tn102CIM` (Change — noncoverage → coverage), `tn3NCD` (Change — expanded coverage), `tn44NCD` (Change — modified facility requirements) all take `revisesPolicy`; `tn768CP` (Claims Processing Instructions, mentions only) takes `referencesPolicy`. **This resolves the 6–6 corpus split S150 flagged as §4 item 14** — the split existed because V1-creating transmittals "had nothing to revise"; the rule counts New, so they take the edge. `tn83CIM` is the first application. Corpus backfill (85 derivable pairs, `ncd160.18` alone = 32) is `deferred_proposals[99]`, scheduled for the 80-policy checkpoint.
- **B5 (facilities are `gem:ProviderCredential`, not `gem:HealthcareSetting`).** Joint Commission LVRS certification, Medicare lung/heart-lung transplantation hospital approval, and NHLBI NETT approval are all *credentials a facility holds*, not places of service. Precedent: `credentialFacilityApprovedByCMSForLiverTransplants` (TN 48 §260.1), same shape — procedure-specific facility approval. Consequence: **NCD 240.1 is not gated by the [70] healthcare-settings rebuild**, and `gem:requiresProviderCredential` (domain `gem:CMSpolicy`) carries all nine links at policy level. One credential individual, `credentialFacilityApprovedByNHLBIForNETT`, serves both R6's "approved by the NHLBI to participate in the NETT" and R14's "approved as meeting the criteria established by HCFA and NHLBI for this study" — same facility set, two formulations; because the predicate hangs off the policy and not the rule, both verbatim wordings survive in their rules without a duplicate individual.
- **B6 (`gem:workflowDescription` — new annotation property, forward-compliant from this session).** `gem:description` was carrying two jobs: what the entity *is* (consumer-facing) and how the extraction got there (session provenance, token derivation, pending state, borderline calls). Measured before the change: **351 of 2,207 described subjects (16%) carried workflow prose**, concentrated where it does the most damage — 76/86 transmittals, 38/40 NCAs, 32/33 change requests. New `owl:AnnotationProperty gem:workflowDescription` (no domain/range, single-valued, ordered immediately after `gem:description`). NCD 240.1's 59 new individuals are born clean: 21 carry the new property, and their `gem:description` values say only what the entity is. Scope calls Tom confirmed: schema-term change history stays in `gem:description` (different audience, separate proposal if ever); "Source URL pending" → workflow; stub-pending prose → workflow, and mostly deletable since it duplicates `gem:nextPlannedStep`; retired/retired-in-place prose stays in `description`. Corpus backfill + the `description_workflow_leak` guard are `deferred_proposals[100]`, scheduled for the 80-policy checkpoint alongside B4's.
- **Cross-version subtractive audit (the finding that produced R10–R14).** Methodology per the S151 retention rule: a factor is a finding only if present in an earlier version, absent from the most-recent version, with no intervening version documenting or effecting the removal. Five findings, all retained. **`conceptCOPD` is a sixth, at concept level:** V1 and V2 both name chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; V3 says only "severe emphysema." No revision history reports the narrowing, so the link stands.
- **Transcription conventions (applied, and one deliberate inconsistency).** Sub/superscripts flattened to plain ASCII (`FEV1`, `PCO2`, `PO2`, `kg/m2`), matching the existing `conceptPO2` / `conceptFEV1`. Hyphen line-break artifacts **de-wrapped in prose** (`dobutamine-radionuclide`, `post-rehabilitation`, `non-upper lobe`, `video-assisted`, `self-administrable`) — the de-wrap of an English hyphenate is unambiguous. But R6's CMS facility-list URL is left **as the rendition prints it** (`Medicare-GeneralInformation`), because de-wrapping a URL is a hypothesis about a string that cannot be checked from the document — and this session's `tn3NCD` finding is the evidence for why that matters. Inconsistent-looking on purpose; flagged for Tom.
- **Source-fidelity findings (captured verbatim, not corrected).** (1) V3's §B.1 pulmonary-function row has an **unbalanced parenthesis** — *"(FEV1) ≤ 45% predicted ≥ 15% predicted if age ≥ 70 years)"* — where V2 renders the same criterion closed. Captured as V3 prints it, per the S139 "autonomic dysflexia" precedent. (2) V1 cites the self-administrable exclusion to **§1862(s)(2)** of the Act; §1862 has no (s) subsection (the "incident to" definition is §1861(s)(2)). CMS's own citation error, carried verbatim in R12. (3) V3 writes **"High Resolution Computer Tomography"**; the conventional expansion is *Computed*. Verbatim in R3 and in the concept's `gem:prefLabel`; normalized in the URI only (`conceptHighResolutionComputedTomography`).
- **`tn3NCD` source conflict (recorded per `gem_reference.md` §5.2).** V2's rendition posts the Coverage Transmittal Link as `…/Downloads/R3NCD.pdf`; the transmittal's actual published URL is `…/downloads/dwnlds/r3ncdpdf.pdf` — a non-compliant CMS filename, supplied and flagged by Tom at the Plan turn. Both carry the `NCD` token, so the URI is unaffected. **The lesson is method, not URL:** S150's `tn79NCD` reconstruction matched by luck, and this pass carried it forward as a method. It is a hypothesis. Note also that `tn3NCD`'s priority-1 token exists **only because Tom supplied all three versions** — V3 names TN 3 in its Revision History but posts no link; the filename is printed on the superseded V2 page alone.
- **Document characteristics.** 6 pp (MCD rendition of V3). No Coding Information section, no Cross Reference section. Claims Processing Instructions names `TN 768` (V2 named TNs 26 and 27 of the same manual — not minted; current-version-only extraction governs, and the retention rule reaches rules/concepts/settings/beneficiary groups, not a superseded version's claims-processing metadata). Transmittal Information names TN 44. The NCA section names CAG-00115R and CAG-00115R2; both NCAIds were supplied by Tom, so neither stub's URL is pending. **Unsolicited findings surfaced this session (not acted on):** NCD `gem:publicationNumber` is split 43×`"100-3"` / 3×`"100-03"` post-close (42/3 before this pass) (`ncd20.29`, `ncd240.9`, `ncd310.1`) with no audit guard — 240.1 uses `"100-3"` with the majority; and `lcd33718` carries `gem:publicationNumber "100-03"`, an NCD-manual number on an LCD.

### NCD 270.1 — Electrical Stimulation (ES) and Electromagnetic Therapy for the Treatment of Wounds

*Extracted S152 (2026-07-16). `gemi:ncd270.1_r1` … `_r16`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-16 (Session 152). 16 rules at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; no inline HCPCS/ICD codes — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (ES and electromagnetic therapy for wound treatment); domain axis omitted per convention. `gemi:ncd270.1` was a `planPromote` NCD stub (minted during NCD 280.1's extraction, which cites §270.1 for Electrical Stimulation for Wounds), promoted to a fully-extracted `planDone` policy (stub collapsed from the NCD 280.1 stub block into its own top-level section; workflow entry moved `planPromote / isInEffect=True → planDone / isInEffect=True`, all four headers recomputed from the file, not incremented). Version 3 NCD, effective 07/01/2004, implemented 07/06/2004; NCDId=131, 7 pp. 6 axis-2 `rule_type` values across 17 `gem:ruleType` triples: coverage-scope (6), non-coverage (3), definition (3), service-definition (2), credentialed-actor (3), frequency (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit categories: Incident to a physician's professional Service; Outpatient Physical Therapy Services; Physicians' Services (all reuse). 55 clinical-concept links — 41 mints + 14 reuses. 4 provider-credential links — 1 mint (`credentialClinicianIncidentToAPhysician`) + 3 reuses. **No healthcare setting** (see B7), no qualification group. 22 policy-to-policy references: 18 new mints (`tn98CIM`, `tn161CIM`, `tn7NCD`, `tn1165NCD`, `tn1798NCD`, `tn1854NCD`, `tn1975NCD`, `tn2005NCD`, `tn2122NCD`, `tn2138NCD`, `tn2200NCD`, `tn2439NCD`, `tn13383NCD`, `tn13401NCD`, `tn124CP`, `pmB9711`, `pmAB02161`, `pmAB03093`) and 4 pre-existing (`tn95CIM`, `tn100CIM`, `cag00068N`, `cag00068R`). 9 change requests minted and wired via `gem:transmitsChangeRequest`.

**A multi-version policy whose retention analysis retains nothing.** Tom supplied all three renditions (V1 eff. 07/14/1997, V2 eff. 04/01/2003, V3 eff. 07/01/2004). All 16 rules are V3's own text. Both silent drops resolved against retention — see B1 and B2.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | Item/Service Description: effective 07/01/2004, electromagnetic therapy covered for the same settings and conditions as ES | coverage-scope |
| R2 | Item/Service Description: either one covered ES therapy **or** one covered electromagnetic therapy — not both | coverage-scope |
| R3 | §A ¶1: adjunctive therapies, covered only for chronic Stage III/IV pressure ulcers, arterial ulcers, diabetic ulcers, venous stasis ulcers | coverage-scope |
| R4 | §A ¶1: chronic ulcer defined (not healed within 30 days of occurrence) | definition |
| R5 | §A ¶1: covered only after ≥30 days of standard wound therapy with no measurable signs of improved healing; the period may begin while the wound is acute | coverage-scope |
| R6 | §A ¶2: standard wound care components (general) | service-definition |
| R7 | §A ¶2: standard wound care components by wound type | service-definition |
| R8 | §A ¶3: measurable signs of improved healing defined | definition |
| R9 | §A ¶3: must be discontinued at a 100% epithelialized wound bed | coverage-scope |
| R10 | §A ¶4: covered only when performed by a physician, physical therapist, or incident to a physician service | credentialed-actor |
| R11 | §A ¶4: the performing practitioner must evaluate the wound and contact the treating physician if it worsens | credentialed-actor |
| R12 | §A ¶4: wounds must be evaluated at least monthly by the treating physician | credentialed-actor, frequency |
| R13 | §B.1: not covered as an initial treatment modality | non-coverage |
| R14 | §B.2: continued treatment not covered absent measurable signs of healing within any 30-day period | non-coverage |
| R15 | §B.3: unsupervised use not covered | non-coverage |
| R16 | §C: all other uses not otherwise specified remain at local MAC discretion | coverage-scope |

**Notes**

- **B1 (retention analysis — nothing retained, and why that is a result, not an absence of one).** The **S151 cross-version retention rule** (Tom, S151) was run over both transitions, V1→V2 and V2→V3. **V2→V3:** V2's *"All other uses of electrical stimulation for the treatment of wounds are noncovered"* is **not retained** — V3 §C speaks to exactly that ground (*"All other uses … not otherwise specified"*) and gives it a different disposition, MAC discretion. That is a restatement with a changed outcome, i.e. specifically changed, not silently dropped; same shape as NCD 240.1's not-retained V1 blanket default. V2's *"Any form of electromagnetic therapy … will not be covered"* is **not retained** — TN 7's Revision-History entry reports exactly that change. **V1→V2:** V1's blanket *"ES cannot be covered by Medicare because its effectiveness has not been adequately demonstrated"* is **not retained** — TN 161's entry reports the reversal to coverage, and V2/V3 restate the residual ground narrowly (R3 + R16). The one genuine silent drop is V1's ES-modality taxonomy, handled at B2. **Δ from the Plan turn: none.** The manifest said 16 and the Generate turn produced 16 — worth stating explicitly, because S150's and S151's lesson is that a confirmed manifest is not a verified one; here the verification agreed.
- **B2 (a silently-dropped factor that was never a rule — retention's first non-rule test; Tom-confirmed).** V1's Item/Service Description enumerates the ES modality taxonomy: direct current, alternating current, pulsed current, pulsed electromagnetic induction and spinal cord stimulation as *the types of ES*; TENS as an example of AC; PEMI as including PEMF and PEE using pulsed radio frequency energy, both nonthermal; and generators creating energy through coils rather than leads or surface electrodes. V2 drops all of it and TN 161's entry reports only the coverage changes — a textbook silent drop. **But the retention rule retains rules, concepts, settings and beneficiary groups, and this was never a rule:** it is background description, it drives no evaluator decision, and under *"what belongs as a rule"* corollary #2 its content belongs on the concept individuals. So it is **retained as concepts, not as rules** — 16 concepts enter the graph carrying its content, and no `gem:PolicyRule` is minted. The defensible alternative considered: capture it as one Pattern-3 `service-definition` rule (NCD 280.6 R1 is the precedent shape, from S49 and pre-dating the S97 corollary-#2 extension). Rejected because recent practice is unambiguous — NCD 160.24's rules skip its Item/Service Description definitional prose entirely — and because minting a rule V1 never wrote as one, to preserve content the concepts already carry, would be retention manufacturing a rule rather than standing one. **Worth naming and not resolving:** V1 classifies pulsed electromagnetic induction as a *type of ES*, while V3 treats electromagnetic therapy as ES's covered alternative and allows only one of the two. Retaining V1's concepts carries that tension into the graph. `gemi:conceptPulsedElectromagneticInduction`'s description states it; nothing resolves it.
- **B3 (a concept named only inside a reported-removed rule goes with the rule — Tom-confirmed, now a general rule).** V2's *"Any form of electromagnetic therapy for the treatment of chronic wounds will not be covered"* is removed under a reported change (TN 7). Its phrase *"chronic wounds"* appears nowhere else in any version, and V3 speaks of *chronic ulcers*. So `conceptChronicWound` is **not** minted or linked. The rule this establishes: the retention rule's concept clause governs **silent** drops; where a revision history **reports** the removal of a rule, the concepts that live only inside that rule are removed with it. Without this, every reported removal would leave its vocabulary behind and the policy would accrete concepts its current text contradicts. Codified in `SKILL.md` §Cross-version retention.
- **B4 (R9 is `coverage-scope`, not `non-coverage`).** *"ES or electromagnetic therapy must be discontinued when the wound demonstrates 100% epitheliliazed wound bed"* reads as a stopping condition, and a stopping condition denies claims past the stop. It is nonetheless `coverage-scope`: CMS places it in **§A Nationally Covered Indications**, not §B, and it bounds the shape of the covered course rather than naming a non-covered thing — §B's three items are what this policy means by non-covered. The alternative (`non-coverage`) is defensible and was considered; the section placement decides it.
- **B5 (four reuses the letter of the rules would have made mints).** `conceptVenousStasisUlcers`, `conceptVenousUlcers`, `conceptGenerator` and `conceptNutritionalStatusOptimization` were **reused**. The S43 singular-normalization rule tests for a *URI collision*: normalize the source's plural to singular, and if that URI already exists with a plurality-only label difference, reuse. That test only fires when the existing URI is already singular — `conceptGenerator` collided and reused cleanly. But `conceptVenousStasisUlcers` and `conceptVenousUlcers` are **plural-form URIs** (minted at NCD 280.6, before the rule), so singular normalization produces `conceptVenousStasisUlcer` — *no* collision — and the letter of the rule mints a singular twin of a plural individual whose label differs only in plurality. `conceptNutritionalStatusOptimization` is the word-order case: it was minted from TN 48 §20.29's *"optimization of nutritional status"* — the identical phrase NCD 270.1 uses — but normalized to *"nutritional status optimization"*, so an exact-prefLabel-match test fails against the very phrase that produced it. Tom confirmed reuse in all four. **The finding is in the rule's text, not this policy:** the S43 rule states its test on URI collision but its rationale is plurality-only difference, and the two come apart on pre-rule plural URIs. `SKILL.md` §Clinical Concepts now says so. The catalog-phrasings principle is untouched — genuine phrasing differences were still minted, and this policy minted seven of them (`conceptStandardWoundTherapy` vs `conceptStandardWoundCare`, `conceptMeasurableSignsOfImprovedHealing` vs `conceptMeasurableSignsOfHealing`, `conceptGoodGlucoseControl` vs `conceptGlucoseControlOptimization`, `conceptPressureUlcer` vs `conceptDecubitusUlcer`, `conceptTranscutaneousElectricalStimulation` vs `conceptTranscutaneousElectricalNerveStimulation`, `conceptElectrode` and `conceptSurfaceElectrode` vs `conceptConventionalElectrode`, `conceptCompressionSystem` vs `conceptCompressionBandageSystem`).
- **B6 (the spelling ruling — Tom, S152 — and what it entailed).** V3 writes *"100% epitheliliazed wound bed"*; V2 writes *"100 per-cent epithelialzed wound bed"*. Both misspell *epithelialized*, and differently. Tom's ruling: **correct the spelling in the concept's prefLabel and URI; never in the rule description.** So R9 carries V3's verbatim and `gemi:conceptEpithelializedWoundBed` carries the correction. Tom confirmed the ruling is general, which **closes the S139 `autonomic dysflexia` carry-forward with no edit** — `gemi:conceptAutonomicDysreflexia` already matched it. It did entail one corpus edit: S151 recorded the S139 precedent as *"verbatim in R3 and the prefLabel, normalized in the URI only"*, so `gemi:conceptHighResolutionComputedTomography` held the source's *"computer tomography"* in its prefLabel. Corrected at S152; NCD 240.1's R3 still carries the source form. That was the only individual in the corpus the ruling changed.
- **B7 (NCD 270.1 names no healthcare setting — a wrong expectation, corrected).** `deferred_proposals[70]`'s S73 cross-corpus survey listed NCD 270.1 among the settings-naming policies, and both [70] and [95] recorded it as a deferred stub that would pick settings up at promotion — which is why the S148 handoff made the settings rebuild a **blocker** for this policy. All three renditions were read. The only occurrence of the word is V3's *"Medicare will cover electromagnetic therapy for the same settings and conditions for which ES is covered"*, where *settings* means clinical circumstances, not a place of care. No version names a place. NCD 270.1 takes zero `gem:refersToHealthcareSetting` links and is struck from [95]'s backfill set. **The generalization:** [70]'s survey matched on a word, and the word is ambiguous — the remaining deferred entries (`cag00296N`, `ncd150.5`, `tn57NCD`, `a55426`, `a58247`) inherit the same doubt and should be read, not trusted. The [95] rebuild was still owed on its own merits and was built at S152 before this was known.
- **B8 (transmittal edges — the S151 rule applied 17 times, including where the corpus is silent).** Every transmittal and Program Memorandum that describes a change takes `gem:revisesPolicy`: `tn95CIM` (New — provided the noncoverage policy), `tn98CIM` (a pagination correction — the rule counts the change, not its size), `tn100CIM` (changed TN 95's effective date), `tn161CIM` (the V2 coverage reversal), `tn7NCD` (the V3 electromagnetic-therapy expansion), `pmB9711` (suspended the policy's implementation), and the ten coding-maintenance transmittals `tn1165NCD` … `tn13401NCD` including the rescinded `tn13383NCD`. Mentions only take `gem:referencesPolicy`: `tn124CP`, `pmAB02161`, `pmAB03093` (all Claims Processing Instructions). **The maintenance transmittals are the live case:** they state *"no policy-related changes are included"* while changing the policy's coding infrastructure. That is a Change/Revision, so they take the edge. `gemi:tn1122NCD` and `gemi:tn1580NCD` — minted at NCD 160.18 for exactly this kind of update — carry no edge, because they predate the rule; they are part of the `deferred_proposals[99]` backfill, and NCD 270.1 is now the worked example of what that backfill should produce.
- **B9 (`gem:priorManualSectionNumber` — new datatype property, Tom-approved option (c)).** NCD 270.1 has been published under three manual coordinates: Pub. 6 §35-98 (V1), Pub. 6 §35-102 (V2), Pub. 100-3 §270.1 (V3) — CMS converted the Coverage Issues Manual into the NCD Manual and renumbered within it. `gem:publicationNumber` and `gem:manualSectionNumber` are single-valued current-version facts, so before S152 the corpus recorded **zero** prior coordinates and a citation written against an old number resolved to nothing. The new property is repeatable, carries the full coordinate as the superseded rendition prints it (`"Pub. 6 §35-98"`), and is **deliberately partial** — no date, no version linkage. Options rejected: prose only (not queryable); multi-valuing `gem:manualSectionNumber` (destroys *"what is the section now"* and dates nothing). First-class version individuals would subsume it and remain `deferred_proposals[98]`'s open question; Tom accepted at S152 that (c) is throwaway if (d) is ever built. TN 48 exists precisely because of this renumbering, which is why old-coordinate lookup is a live path rather than a curiosity.


### NCD 270.5 — Porcine Skin and Gradient Pressure Dressings

*Extracted S153 (2026-07-16). `gemi:ncd270.5_r1`–`gemi:ncd270.5_r2`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-16 (Session 153). 2 rules, both at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; no inline HCPCS/ICD codes — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (surgical dressings for burns and ulcers; Surgical Dressings); domain axis omitted per convention. `gemi:ncd270.5` was a `planPromote` NCD stub (minted during NCD 280.1's extraction via its "Elastic Stockings" Durable Medical Equipment Reference List entry), promoted to a fully-extracted `planDone` policy (stub collapsed from the NCD 280.1 stub block into its own top-level section; workflow entry moved `planPromote / isInEffect=True → planDone / isInEffect=True`, all four headers recomputed from the file — 62/14/13/137). Longstanding Version 1 NCD: Tracking Information posts no effective date, so the NCD 270.4 / 280.2 / 30.1 / 240.3 Other-Versions fallback fires and **1966-01-01** is taken from the Other Versions effective-between column. **Single-version** — the Other Versions table lists V1 alone ("You are here"). 2 distinct axis-2 `rule_type` values (3 `gem:ruleType` triples): coverage-scope (2), service-definition (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit category: Surgical Dressings (reuse). No provider credential, healthcare setting or qualification group. 11 clinical-concept links — 10 mints + 1 reuse (`conceptOcclusiveDressing`). No policy-to-policy references.

**The corpus's shortest two-rule NCD, and its cleanest one-rule-per-subject shape.** Each sentence-group governs exactly one dressing type, and neither conditions the other. The whole extraction turns on two questions: how finely to catalog the four indications R1 names, and whether R2's definition is a rule or a description.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | §Indications and Limitations of Coverage, sentence 1: porcine (pig) skin dressings are covered, if reasonable and necessary for the individual patient, as an occlusive dressing for burns, donor sites of a homograft, and decubiti and other ulcers | coverage-scope |
| R2 | §Indications and Limitations of Coverage, sentences 2–3: gradient pressure dressings are Jobst elasticized heavy duty dressings used to reduce hypertrophic scarring and joint contractures following burn injury; they are covered when used for that purpose | coverage-scope, service-definition |

**Notes**
- **B1 (`decubiti` → `conceptDecubitus` minted, not `conceptDecubitusUlcer` reused — Tom).** The existing individual's prefLabel is *"decubitus ulcer"*; the source writes *"decubiti"*. The S43 rule's reuse branch is plurality-only, and its S152 rationale reading adds *"or the existing individual was demonstrably minted from this same wording"* — `conceptDecubitusUlcer` was minted at TN 48 §20.29 from its own list, not from this phrase. Neither branch reaches a dropped word, so catalog-phrasings governs and the default is mint. The single-term-linkage rationale points the same way: a note saying only *"decubiti"* should link this policy without the matcher knowing that a decubitus is an ulcer. **Defensible alternative considered:** reuse, on the ground that the policy's own *"decubiti and other ulcers"* declares a decubitus to be an ulcer, and sibling NCD 270.4 — the decubitus-ulcer policy — links the existing individual, so a reuse would put the two dressings' policies on one term. Tom took the mint. Any equivalence between the two individuals is the SME taxonomy pass's business.
- **B2 (`and other ulcers` → `conceptUlcer` minted — Tom).** *"other"* is the source's quantifier over the preceding decubiti, not part of a concept's name, so the phrase names the concept *ulcer* and the fourth indication is open-ended. **Defensible alternative considered:** drop it — a bare catch-all naming no entity a provider note would carry, on the reading that the policy's indications are the three specific ones plus a residual. Rejected because the residual **is** the coverage's fourth arm and a note reading *"ulcer"* should reach this policy; dropping would make the open-ended arm the only one with no hook. Tom took the mint.
- **B3 (`burns` and `burn injury` — two individuals — Tom).** Catalog-phrasings, applied at one sentence's distance: R1's indication is a burn, R2's is the scarring and contractures that *follow* a burn injury. Two phrasings, two individuals, maximal single-term recall. **Defensible alternative considered:** one individual — the same referent named twice inside a 60-word policy, and minting both puts two near-synonyms on one document. Distinguishable: the policy uses them for different roles (a wound to dress vs. an antecedent event), which is exactly the case where a later equivalence assertion, not an extraction-time collapse, is the right instrument. Tom took the split.
- **B4 (R2 — one Pattern-3 rule, not two — Tom).** *"They are covered when used for that purpose"* is an anaphor twice over: *they* is the gradient pressure dressings of sentence 2, and *that purpose* is sentence 2's *"used to reduce hypertrophic scarring and joint contractures following burn injury"*. Split, the coverage sentence names no subject and no condition; it cannot execute. This is corollary #2's **needed-to-execute** branch (SKILL.md §Rule Patterns, corollary #2: *"If the rule that names the entity does not require the definition to execute, the definitional sentence is not a separate rule"* — here it does), and the shape is NCD 230.18 R2's exactly (definition + *"Both the test and the permanent implantation are covered"*). One IF/THEN, so one rule under the granularity heuristic. **Defensible alternative considered:** the **NCD 270.4 r1/r2 split** — a `service-definition` rule plus a `coverage-scope` rule — the nearest sibling's shape, same section title, same author, minted at S134. It works there because 270.4's coverage sentence names its own subject (*"Hydrotherapy (whirlpool) treatment for decubitus ulcers is a covered service…"*) and stands alone; 270.5's does not. **The distinction is the anaphor, not the section.** Tom took the single rule.
- **B5 (R2 — `service-definition` alongside `coverage-scope` — Tom).** B4's consequence: the definition is inside the rule string, so the tag set should say so. `gem:RuleType`'s `serviceDefinition` is *"defines a service itself"*, which sentence 2 does on its face. NCD 240.5 R1's `non-coverage` + `setting-definition` is the shape — a second tag on one rule, not a second rule. **Defensible alternative considered:** `coverage-scope` alone, per NCD 280.2 B2's no-over-tag posture — the rule's operative content is a coverage decision and the definition is the vehicle. Rejected as under-describing a string whose first sentence is a definition. Tom took both tags.
- **Single-version — the retention rule does not fire, and that is stated, not skipped.** The Other Versions table lists Version 1 alone, so there is no transition to walk. Contrast NCD 270.1 (S152), whose three versions retained nothing, and NCD 240.1 (S151), whose two retained `r10`/`r11`. A single-version policy is the only shape where the rule has no work to do; the reason is the table, not an absence of evidence.
- **The "Elastic Stockings" label is NCD 280.1's, not this policy's.** The stub was minted from NCD 280.1's Durable Medical Equipment Reference List entry *"Elastic Stockings … (See §270.5 of this manual.)"*, and `gemi:conceptElasticStocking` (prefLabel *"Elastic Stockings"*) was minted there under that label. **NCD 270.5's own text never uses the phrase**, so no `refersToClinicalConcept` link to it is made from here; the connection 280.1 draws is to this policy's Jobst elasticized heavy duty dressings. The stub's `gem:description` had already recorded the mismatch; the promotion confirms it against the document. A reader arriving from 280.1's entry expecting a stockings policy finds a dressings policy — CMS's colloquialism, faithfully carried in 280.1's own rule and not propagated here.
- **Not minted.** *"the individual patient"* (administrative, not clinical — the reasonable-and-necessary framing's beneficiary); *"reasonable and necessary"* (the §1862(a)(1)(A) standard as a bare phrase, carried in R1's verbatim, and no statute is cited so corollary #1 has nothing to anchor); *"heavy duty"* / *"elasticized"* (adjectives inside the composite `Jobst elasticized heavy duty dressing`, not fabricated as constituents).
- **No codes; no credentials; no references; publication + source.** No inline HCPCS/ICD references (NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Zero `gem:requiresProviderCredential` links — the document names no role at all, not even in a contrastive clause (contrast NCD 240.5's *"a therapist"*), so the strict-prose rule has nothing to test. Zero `gem:refersToHealthcareSetting` links — no place of care is named; §Healthcare Settings run on the document itself, per the S152 B7 lesson that a word-match survey is not a reading. Zero policy-to-policy references: the document carries no Transmittal Information, Revision History, Cross Reference, Claims Processing Instructions or NCA section, so the mint-every-referenced-policy rule mints nothing — the same shape as NCD 270.4. `publicationNumber "100-3"`; `manualSectionNumber "270.5"`; no `gem:priorManualSectionNumber` (the document prints no prior coordinate). `dc:source` set from the stub's `…?NCDId=139` to the user-supplied `…?NCDId=139&NCDver=1` — a URL confirmation at the policy's own Plan turn, explicitly a **non-finding**. Version 1; 2 pp; 96 words of substantive coverage prose. The MCD benefit-category disclaimer ("Please Note: This may not be an exhaustive list…") is not captured as a rule, consistent with NCD 240.3 / 280.2 / 30.1 / 240.5.

No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit category: Durable Medical Equipment (reuse). 54 clinical-concept links — 42 mints + 12 reuses (`conceptCane`, `conceptCognitiveImpairment`, `conceptCrutch`, `conceptDurableMedicalEquipment`, `conceptManualWheelchair`, `conceptPowerWheelchair`, `conceptPrescription`, `conceptScooterPOV`, `conceptSpasticity`, `conceptSpeciallySizedWheelchair`, `conceptVisualImpairment`, `conceptWalker`). 3 provider-credential links — 2 reuses (`credentialBeneficiaryPhysician`, `credentialPhysician`) + 1 mint (`credentialClinician`). 1 healthcare setting (`settingHome`, reuse).
