**A multi-version policy whose title and subject change wholesale across the transition.** Tom supplied both renditions (V1 "Specially Sized Wheelchairs", eff. 1966-01-01 – 2005-05-05; V2 "Mobility Assistive Equipment (MAE)", eff. 2005-05-05). Seventeen rules are V2's own text; **three are retained from V1 under the S151 retention rule** — the largest retention the corpus has carried, and the first where the newer version supplies an affirmative basis for it rather than mere silence. See B1.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | V2 §B ¶1 s1: effective 05/05/2005, MAE is reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with a personal mobility deficit sufficient to impair participation in MRADLs (toileting, feeding, dressing, grooming, bathing) in customary locations within the home | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R2 | V2 §B ¶1 s2: the presence of a mobility deficit is determined by an algorithmic process, Clinical Criteria for MAE Coverage | procedural, eligibility |
| R3 | V2 §B, Clinical Criteria ¶2: where the beneficiary's condition clearly and unambiguously precludes reasonable use of a device, no trial of that device is necessary | procedural |
| R4 | V2 decision point 1 (+a–c): does the beneficiary have a mobility limitation significantly impairing MRADL participation in the home — definition folded (prevents entirely / heightened morbidity-mortality risk / prevents completion in a reasonable time frame) | eligibility |
| R5 | V2 decision point 2 (+a, b): are there other conditions limiting MRADL participation at home (cognition, judgment, vision; comorbidity preventing effective wheelchair use) | eligibility |
| R6 | V2 decision point 3 (+a, b): can those limitations be ameliorated or compensated — caregiver compensation; non-compliance with treatment as grounds for denial | eligibility, non-coverage |
| R7 | V2 decision point 4 (+a, b): does the beneficiary or caregiver demonstrate capability and willingness to operate the MAE safely | eligibility, service-standard |
| R8 | V2 decision point 5 (+a, b): can the functional mobility deficit be sufficiently resolved by the prescription of a cane or walker | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R9 | V2 decision point 6 (+a, b): does the beneficiary's typical environment support wheelchairs including scooters/POVs | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R10 | V2 decision point 7 (+a–d): sufficient upper extremity function to propel an optimally configured manual wheelchair in the home during a typical day | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R11 | V2 NOTE after decision point 7: unable to self-propel + an available, willing, able caregiver → a manual wheelchair may be appropriate | coverage-scope |
| R12 | V2 decision point 8 (+a–c): sufficient strength and postural stability to operate a POV/scooter; POV defined (3- or 4-wheeled, tiller steering, limited seat modification) | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R13 | V2 decision point 9 (+a–d): are the additional features of a power wheelchair needed for MRADL participation | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R14 | V2 NOTE after decision point 9, s1: unable to use a power wheelchair + an available, willing, able caregiver → a manual wheelchair is appropriate | coverage-scope |
| R15 | V2 NOTE after decision point 9, s2: a caregiver's inability to operate a manual wheelchair can be considered in covering a power wheelchair | coverage-scope |
| R16 | V2 §C: beneficiaries not meeting the clinical criteria, as documented by the beneficiary's physician, are not eligible for coverage of the MAE | non-coverage, eligibility, credentialed-actor |
| R17 | V2 §D s1: all other DME not meeting the definition of MAE continues to be covered or noncovered as described in the NCD Manual, Section 280, Medical and Surgical Supplies | coverage-scope |
| R18 | **Retained (V1 ¶1).** Payment may be made for a specially sized wheelchair though more expensive than a standard one (narrow doorways / slender build); the size difference is not a deluxe feature | payment-rule, coverage-scope |
| R19 | **Retained (V1 ¶2).** A physician's certification or prescription that a special size is needed is not required where the need is determinable from the information in file or other sources | documentation, credentialed-actor |
| R20 | **Retained (V1 ¶3).** Determine the reasonable charge using the criteria of the Medicare Claims Processing Manual, Chapters 12 and 23 | payment-rule |

**Notes**
- **B1 (retention — all three of V1's rules stand; the session's central call).** The S151 rule: *where an earlier version states a rule, concept, setting or beneficiary group, a later version does not, and no revision history in any version reports the change, nothing changed.* **Applied:** TN 37 is the only transmittal in the chain — V1 posts no Transmittal Information and no Revision History at all — and TN 37's entry reports only *"Determined MAE is reasonable and necessary…"*, an **addition**. Nothing anywhere reports the removal of V1's specially-sized-wheelchair provisions, so R18–R20 stand. **What makes this case different from its two predecessors:** V2 §D supplies an *affirmative* basis on top of the silence — *"all other sections not altered here and the corresponding policies regarding MAEs which have not been discussed here remain unchanged"* — and a specially sized wheelchair **is** MAE (V2's own category includes manual wheelchairs) that V2 does not discuss. Retention here is not an inference from silence; the document says it. **The counter-argument, and why it fails.** The pull to treat a wholesale rewrite — new title, new subject, new determination — as an implicit repeal is strong, and it is exactly the pull the S151 rule exists to resist: the rule's test is **textual, not topical**. A version that fails to report a change has not made one, however different it looks. Tested against the S152 restatement-with-changed-outcome escape (NCD 270.1's V2 *"all other uses … noncovered"* against V3 §C's MAC discretion — same ground, different disposition): it does not apply, because V2 and V1 do not speak to the same ground. V2 decides **whether MAE is covered at all**; V1 decides **what is paid for a wheelchair whose size is non-standard** (R18, R20) and **what documents the size** (R19). Both can be true of one claim: the wheelchair qualifies under the Clinical Criteria, and its special size is paid for without a separate certification. Nothing in V2 contradicts a word of it. **Defensible alternative considered:** read §D's *"corresponding policies regarding MAEs"* as reaching only *other manual sections*, not V1's own superseded text — on which reading §D says nothing about V1 and the case falls back to bare silence. It still retains under S151; the alternative weakens the basis, not the outcome. Tom confirmed the retain.
- **B2 (the nine decision points are nine rules; the letters fold).** S139/NCD-160.24 discriminator: a lettered list folds to one rule when no member is cross-referenced *from inside the policy's own rules*. None is — decision point 3 opens *"If these other limitations exist"*, an outward reference to decision point 2's **question**, not to a letter, and 9a's *"compared to a POV"* names a device, not 8a. So R4–R13 each carry their sub-points inline verbatim, and no δ-prefix scaffold is used (contrast NCD 160.7's B.2 conditions, where in-rule cross-references made the letters addressable). The count comes from the IF/THEN heuristic — a downstream evaluator generates one IF per decision point, which is what the policy's own flow chart draws — and the shape is **sequential decisions** (NCD 240.2 §D precedent), each rule standing alone in order. The policy names the shape itself: *"Sequential consideration of the questions below…"*. **Defensible alternative considered:** atomize the 26 lettered sub-points into δ-scoped rules on the NCD 240.9 medium-granularity precedent, where per-criterion splitting preserved B.I/B.II nesting. Rejected — 240.9's sub-items are independently-dispositive criteria in an "all of the following are met" block; these letters are elaborations *of* a question (definitions, examples, assessment instructions), not conditions the evaluator tests separately.
- **B3 (§A's MAE definition dropped as a rule).** *"CMS … addresses numerous items that it terms “mobility assistive equipment” (MAE) and includes within that category canes, crutches, walkers, manual wheelchairs, power wheelchairs, and scooters. This list, however, is not exhaustive."* is carried in full on `gemi:conceptMobilityAssistiveEquipment`'s `gem:description` under corollary #2. The escape hatch is open because the concept is a **fresh mint** and can carry what it needs — the NCD 240.5 B2 shape exactly. R17 executes by matching the definition, not by re-reading it. The rest of §A (etiology and duration, living situations, the functional-limitation examples) is background and drops likewise; its concepts are captured. **Defensible alternative considered:** keep it as a `service-definition` rule because §D's *"not meeting the definition of MAE **as described in this instruction**"* makes the definition load-bearing — the strongest version of this argument in the corpus, since §D cites the definition explicitly rather than merely relying on it. Rejected on the same ground that decided NCD 240.5 B2: a citation to a definition is not a second rule, it is a pointer to where the definition lives, and it lives on the concept. Tom took the drop.
- **B4 (the two NOTEs are three rules).** The decision-point-7 NOTE is one IF/THEN (R11). The decision-point-9 NOTE is **two**: *"If the beneficiary is unable to use a power wheelchair, and if there is a caregiver … a manual wheelchair is appropriate"* (R14) and *"A caregiver's inability to operate a manual wheelchair can be considered in covering a power wheelchair so that the caregiver can assist the beneficiary"* (R15). Distinct antecedents pointing in opposite directions — beneficiary cannot use power → manual; caregiver cannot operate manual → power — so two IFs under the granularity heuristic, and the pair is **parallel decisions** in the sense that neither gates the other. **Defensible alternative considered:** one rule on the B8/NCD-240.2 *"either (1) by itself, or (2) in addition to"* precedent, where one IF carried two coverage shapes. Rejected: that precedent turns on a **single** antecedent; these are two.
- **B5 (§D splits — sentence 1 is a rule, sentence 2 is not).** Sentence 1 is the residual clause and takes the shape the corpus already gives residuals (NCD 240.1 R9 *"all other indications … remain noncovered"*; NCD 270.1 R16 *"all other uses … at local MAC discretion"*): an evaluator asks *is this DME, and is it MAE?* and routes on the answer, so R17. Sentence 2 (*"Also, all other sections not altered here … remain unchanged"*) asserts no coverage effect of its own — it is a meta-statement about the instruction's own scope, of a piece with the dropped *"(This NCD last reviewed May 2005)"* — so it is not a rule. It is not thereby discarded: it is the affirmative textual basis for B1, and it is quoted there and in `gem:workflowDescription` on the policy. **A sentence can be evidence for the extraction without being a rule in it.**
- **B6 (a named section container with no home — a schema gap, surfaced not filled).** R17 cites *"the NCD Manual, in Section 280, Medical and Surgical Supplies"*. GEM has no entity type for a **Pub. 100-03 section container**: `gem:CMSmanualChapter`'s twelve individuals are all Pub. 100-02, 100-04 or 100-08 chapters, and `gem:PolicyGroup` is an anchored coding scope, not a manual coordinate. So §280 is minted as nothing; R17 carries the name verbatim and `gem:referencesPolicy gemi:ncd280.1` carries the DME Reference List connection. **Consequence worth naming:** §280 is the parent of every 280.x NCD in the corpus — 280.1, 280.2, 280.3, 280.4, 280.6, 280.13, and the four remaining stubs — and the graph has no node for it, so a query for "what else lives under Section 280" is a string match on `gem:manualSectionNumber`, not a traversal. The mint-every-referenced-policy rule (S131) does not reach it because a section container is not a policy document. Flagged for Tom; not opened as a proposal this session.
- **B7 (`conceptDressingMRADL` — the corpus's first homograph collision).** V2's MRADL list names *dressing*, the act of putting on clothing. `gemi:conceptDressing` (prefLabel *"dressing"*) already exists in the wound-care sense, from the surgical-dressing corpus. This is not the plurality-only collision the singular-normalization rule handles (`conceptWhiteCane` at NCD 280.2, `conceptSeatLift` at NCD 280.4), nor the catalog-phrasings case where two phrasings name one referent — the strings are **identical** and the referents are **unrelated**. Reuse would assert a falsehood. So the URI carries a qualifier (`conceptDressingMRADL`) and, unusually, so does the prefLabel (*"dressing (MRADL)"*), because two individuals labelled *"dressing"* meaning different things would be worse than a label the source does not write. **The general shape, for the next one:** where a source term collides *exactly* with an existing individual of a different sense, disambiguate the newcomer and leave the incumbent alone — renaming the incumbent would touch policies that have nothing to do with this pass. **Defensible alternative considered:** mint `conceptDressing` … impossible; the URI is taken. Second alternative: leave the MRADL unminted and let R1's verbatim carry it — rejected under the Option-B inclusive stance, since the other four MRADLs are minted and dropping the third of five would be an artifact of a URI clash, not a reading of the policy.
- **B8 (`conceptCaregiver` — minted, and the corpus's first).** Nine `gem:ruleDescription` strings across five policies (`ncd240.4_r3`, `ncd280.6_r15`, `a52466_r3`, `lcd33612_r29`, `lcd33718_r39`, `lcd33800_r30`) name a caregiver; none minted the individual. **The distinction that licenses the mint here is dispositiveness, not novelty.** In those policies the caregiver is incidental — the party a supplier contacts for a refill, the party educated on a device, the party who may fill a nebulizer. In NCD 280.3 the caregiver's consistent availability, willingness and ability *decide coverage*, at four separate points (3a, 4, and both NOTEs), and the choice between a manual and a power wheelchair can turn on the caregiver alone (R15). A claim that turns on a caregiver should surface this NCD. **Not a `gem:ProviderCredential`:** the caregiver holds no license and the policy's own example is a family member; the grammatical-agent test that made `credentialMultidisciplinaryTeam` a credential (S39) reaches composite *clinical* actors, not lay ones. **Consequence:** the nine incidental mentions are now the odd ones out, and a corpus-consistency backfill question exists that this pass does not answer — named here rather than acted on.
- **B9 (`credentialClinician` — minted; the weakest of the three links, and named as such).** The licensing sentence is *"The beneficiary, the beneficiary's family or other caregiver, or a clinician, will usually initiate the discussion and consideration of MAE use."* *"Will usually"* is **descriptive**, not mandatory, so the strict-prose rule's canonical verb list (ordering, evaluating, qualifying, prescribing, signing) does not reach it; the link rests on the S37 responsibilities-broadening — *any current-prose mention of an activity, duty, or evidentiary contribution within the credentialed role's scope*. Initiating the consideration of MAE is such an activity. Per catalog-phrasings, minted distinct from `credentialTreatingClinician` and `credentialClinicianIncidentToAPhysician`, neither of which is this policy's phrasing. `credentialBeneficiaryPhysician` (V2 §C, *"as documented by the beneficiary's physician"*) and `credentialPhysician` (V1 ¶2, *"A physician's certification or prescription…"*) are both reuse and both solidly licensed. **Defensible alternative considered:** no link — a sentence about who *usually starts a conversation* imposes no duty, and the S35 narrowing exists precisely to stop passive mentions from licensing links. Distinguishable: the S35 case was a **recordkeeping** artifact (a signature line), where the role's clinical identity is incidental; here the clinician is the agent of the clinical activity, and only the modality is soft. Tom took the link.
- **B10 (reuse over near-duplicate — two calls against catalog-phrasings' grain).** *"muscular spasticity"* (§A) reuses `gemi:conceptSpasticity` and *"cognitive deficits"* (§A) / *"significant impairment of cognition"* (2a) reuse `gemi:conceptCognitiveImpairment`. Catalog-phrasings would mint each; both are declined. *"Muscular"* is **redundant of** spasticity (spasticity is by definition a muscular state), which is the distinction from NCD 240.5 B7's *"good pulmonary care"*, where the qualifier attributed a **standard** to the care and so had to be retained. On cognition, the corpus already carries five phrasings (`conceptCognitiveDisorder`, `conceptCognitiveDysfunction`, `conceptCognitiveImpairment`, `conceptCognitivelyIntactPatient`, `conceptImpairedCognition`) and a sixth and seventh would be accretion, not fidelity. *"Impairment of judgment"* **is** minted (`conceptJudgmentImpairment`) — no incumbent, and judgment is not cognition's synonym in the policy's own "cognition **or** judgment" phrasing. **Named honestly:** these two are the pass's softest calls; the rule they follow ("reuse when the qualifier adds nothing the incumbent lacks") is not written down anywhere, and the corpus is not consistent about it.
- **B11 (four deficit phrasings, four individuals).** *personal mobility deficit* (§B), *mobility deficit* (§B), *mobility limitation* (dp 1), *functional mobility deficit* (dp 5) — minted separately per catalog-phrasings, the NCD 270.5 B3 burn/burn-injury shape (two phrasings one sentence apart, two individuals). Only *mobility limitation* is defined by the policy. The tension with B10 is real and is the reason both are written down: **B11's four differ in their head nouns and their sections; B10's pairs differ by a redundant adjective.**
- **B12 (`settingHome` only).** §B's *"customary locations within the home"* and *"in the home"* at decision points 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 and 9, plus V1's *"the narrow doorways of a patient's home"*, make the home the policy's operative place of care — `gem:refersToHealthcareSetting gemi:settingHome`, the reuse NCD 240.2 / 240.5 / 280.6 already make for DME-in-the-home policies. Per NCD 240.9 B6 the "in the home" clauses do **not** additionally tag their rules `setting-definition`; they fold into `coverage-scope` (NCD 240.2 R1 precedent). *"Custodial care facility"* (§A) is **not** a setting: it appears once, in background prose about where beneficiaries live, and the policy rules on none of it — `gemi:conceptCustodialCareFacility`. The §Healthcare Settings survey was run on the document itself, per the S152 B7 lesson that a word-match survey is not a reading.
- **Transcription — the source mixes apostrophes and both forms are kept.** V2 renders *beneficiary's* with a typographic apostrophe (U+2019) in most places and a straight one in others, sometimes within the same lettered sub-point (decision point 3a has both; 7c and 8b have straight, 7d and 8c typographic). Both are transcribed **as printed**, per the corpus source-fidelity convention — 43 of the 1,112 pre-existing `gem:ruleDescription` strings already carry U+2019. Normalizing would be a silent edit to the source's own bytes for no reader's benefit. V1's only non-ASCII is §.
- **Not minted.** *"mobility assistance"* **is** minted (§A's own framing of the need); *"congenital cause"*, *"injury"*, *"disease"* are not — they are the etiology triple in a background sentence, naming no entity the policy rules on. *"MRADLs"* is minted as the umbrella and its five named members individually, per the Option-B inclusive stance and the NCD 180.2 enteral/parenteral precedent; the list is introduced *"such as"* and is not closed, which the concept's description records. *"reasonable and necessary"* is not minted (the §1862(a)(1)(A) standard as a bare phrase, carried in R1's verbatim, no statute cited so corollary #1 has nothing to anchor). The **flow chart** is a hyperlink (`id143c.pdf`) with no embedded image in the rendition and no separate supply, so nothing is extracted from it; R2 and the nine decision points carry what it draws.
- **Document characteristics.** V2: 7 pp (MCD rendition, footer 1/7–7/7). V1: 2 pp. V1's effective date (1966-01-01) is the **Other-Versions fallback** — its Tracking Information reads *"This is a longstanding national coverage determination. The effective date of this version has not been posted"* — the same fallback applied to NCD 270.4, NCD 280.2, NCD 30.1, NCD 240.3 and NCD 270.5; it is recorded here only, since the policy individual carries V2's coordinates. Neither version has a Coding Information section. V2's Cross Reference names §280.1; V1's names four manual chapters (Pub. 100-02 Ch 13 §30.1 and Ch 15 §110; Pub. 100-04 Ch 20 §§20.2 and 30.5.3) and is dropped as a rule — a bare navigational pointer under the executability test (L33718 D4 / NCD 280.4 B5 precedent) — with `gem:referencesPolicy` preserving the provenance. Note that Pub. 100-04 Ch 12 and Ch 23 arrive **twice**: once through V1's Cross Reference and once inside retained R20, where they are operative. The MCD benefit-category disclaimer is not captured as a rule, consistent with NCD 240.5 / 240.3 / 280.2 / 30.1 / 200.2 / 270.5. `publicationNumber "100-3"` (with the 45–3 corpus majority; §4 item 18 unaffected); `manualSectionNumber "280.3"`; no `gem:priorManualSectionNumber` (neither rendition prints a predecessor coordinate — contrast NCD 270.1). The NCA section names CAG-00274N and CAG-00461N, both already minted with verified URLs at NCD 280.1. `tn574CP`'s URL is **pending** — the Claims Processing Instructions field prints the title as a link without a filename.

### NCD 280.7 — Hospital Beds

*Extracted S155 (2026-07-16). `gemi:ncd280.7_r1` – `_r11`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-16 (Session 155). 11 rules at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; no inline HCPCS/ICD codes — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (hospital beds / Durable Medical Equipment); domain axis omitted per convention. `gemi:ncd280.7` was a `planPromote` NCD stub (minted during NCD 280.1's extraction, whose Durable Medical Equipment Reference List cites §280.7 four times — Bed Side Rails, Electric Hospital Beds, Hospital Beds, Mattresses), promoted to a fully-extracted `planDone` policy (stub collapsed from its position in the file into its own top-level section; workflow entry moved `planPromote / isInEffect=True → planDone / isInEffect=True`, all four headers recomputed from the file). Longstanding Version 1 NCD; the Other Versions table lists Version 1 only (01/01/1966 – N/A, *"You are here"*), so **no cross-version subtractive audit applies**. 4 axis-2 `rule_type` values (27 `gem:ruleType` triples): credentialed-actor (8), eligibility (8), coverage-scope (6), documentation (5). No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit category: Durable Medical Equipment (reuse). 3 provider credentials — 2 reuses (`credentialPhysician`, `credentialMedicareAdministrativeContractor`) + 1 mint (`credentialMedicalStaff`). 29 clinical-concept links — 22 mints + 7 reuses. No healthcare setting (the policy names no place of care; `settingAnywhere` is reserved for an affirmative statement, per Core Principle #10). 1 policy-to-policy reference (`tn36CIM`, reuse, with the reciprocal `revisesPolicy` added on the transmittal side).

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | A. General Requirements: prescription + such additional documentation as the MAC medical staff considers necessary must establish medical necessity — reason 1, the patient's condition requires positioning of the body in ways not feasible in an ordinary bed | documentation; eligibility; credentialed-actor |
| R2 | A. General Requirements: same establishing requirement — reason 2, the patient's condition requires special attachments that cannot be fixed and used on an ordinary bed | documentation; eligibility; credentialed-actor |
| R3 | B. Physician's Prescription: the prescription must accompany the initial claim and, with supplementing documentation when required, must establish that a hospital bed is medically necessary | documentation; credentialed-actor |
| R4 | B. Physician's Prescription: where positioning is the stated reason, the prescription or other documentation must describe the medical condition and the severity and frequency of its symptoms | documentation |
| R5 | B. Physician's Prescription: where special attachments are the stated reason, the prescription must describe the condition and specify the attachments | documentation |
| R6 | C. Variable Height Feature: MAC medical staff may cover the feature on a bed approved under subsection A — condition 1, severe arthritis and other injuries to lower extremities, the feature being required to assist the patient to ambulate | coverage-scope; eligibility; credentialed-actor |
| R7 | C. Variable Height Feature: same — condition 2, severe cardiac conditions, for patients able to leave bed who must avoid the strain of "jumping" up or down | coverage-scope; eligibility; credentialed-actor |
| R8 | C. Variable Height Feature: same — condition 3, spinal cord injuries including quadriplegic and paraplegic patients, multiple limb amputee and stroke patients, for those able to transfer from bed to a wheelchair | coverage-scope; eligibility; credentialed-actor |
| R9 | C. Variable Height Feature: same — condition 4, other severely debilitating diseases and conditions, where the feature is required to assist the patient to ambulate | coverage-scope; eligibility; credentialed-actor |
| R10 | D. Electric Powered Hospital Bed Adjustments: MAC medical staff may cover powered head/foot adjustment on frequent or immediate need for a change in body position where the patient can operate the controls, excepting spinal cord injury and brain damaged patients from that last requirement | coverage-scope; eligibility; credentialed-actor |
| R11 | E. Side Rails: bed side rails covered when an integral part of, or an accessory to, a hospital bed | coverage-scope; eligibility |

**Notes**
- **B1 (11 rules).** IF/THEN heuristic. §A and §C each open with a colon-terminated lead-in sentence over a flat bullet list, so the stem is repeated verbatim as a **Pattern-2** prefix on each bullet — the `lcd33797_r14`–`_r17` shape (*"Oxygen therapy and oxygen equipment will also be denied … if any of the following conditions are present: …"*). §A yields 2 (shared framing + per-case body: the two accepted reasons), §B 3, §C 4 (shared outcome + per-case qualifying tree), §D 1, §E 1. **Defensible alternative considered:** 8, dropping R3 as a restatement of §A's stem — refused, R3 adds *"which must accompany the initial claim"*, a material difference, so corollary #3 keeps both forms (the `L36524` R2/R3 shape). Tom-confirmed.
- **B2 (§D is one Pattern-3 rule, not two).** Sentence 2 reads *"Exceptions may be made to this last requirement in cases of spinal cord injury and brain damaged patients."* Split from sentence 1, *"this last requirement"* has no referent — the exception names its trigger but not what it excepts, so it cannot execute. Corollary #2's **needed-to-execute** branch; the shape of S153's B4 (`ncd270.5_r2`, where *"they"* and *"that purpose"* both pointed backwards). **Defensible alternative considered:** two rules, on the ground that *"Exceptions may be made"* is its own discretionary IF — the NCD 240.2 §D MAC-discretion trio (R19/R20/R21) shape. Refused on the feature the rule turns on rather than the resemblance: each of those three names its own subject; this one does not. Tom-confirmed.
- **B3 ("MAC medical staff" — the phrase is split; Tom's amendment).** §280.7 never names the bare MAC. It writes *"Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) medical staff"* (§A) and *"MAC medical staff"* (§C, §D), and the medical staff is the evaluator at all three points — which is what licenses a credential link at all. Claude's lean was a single composite mint at the full phrase (catalog-phrasings: a head-noun addition is a genuine phrasing difference). **Tom took neither the lean nor its alternative:** reuse `gemi:credentialMedicareAdministrativeContractor` for the organization **and** mint `gemi:credentialMedicalStaff` at the head noun for the clinical body. The composite-agent rule (S39) governs the shape — a multi-person, non-individual actor named as the performer of clinical work takes ProviderCredential treatment — and the bare phrase is independently attested at `ncd280.1_r62` / `_r78` (*"Refer all claims to medical staff for this determination."*). **Corpus-consistency question opened, not settled:** NCD 280.1 (**8** rules using the idiom — `r38`, `r39`, `r60`, `r62`, `r78`, `r80`, `r86`, `r103`) links only the bare MAC — licensed independently by `r94`'s own bare *"the MAC should determine"*, so it never decided this; and its rule strings were minted at **S101's rule backfill**, whose scope was rules and not credentials, which is how the phrase entered the graph eight times without ever triggering a credential call — and NCD 150.5 (`r1`, *"the Medicare Administrative Contractor's medical staff has determined"*) links no MAC-side credential at all. Same shape as §4 item 23's `conceptCaregiver` question: asserted by construction here, named rather than back-fixed.
- **B4 (person-form vs condition-form — condition-form).** §C names *"quadriplegic and paraplegic patients"*, *"stroke patients"* and §D *"brain damaged patients"*. The quadriplegia/paraplegia pair is **reused** from §B's own *"quadriplegia or paraplegia"* — the same policy names both forms — and `conceptStroke` / `conceptBrainDamage` are minted in the condition-form. The rule is S154 B10's: reuse when the qualifier adds nothing the incumbent lacks, and *"patients"* adds no clinical content. **Defensible alternative considered:** mint the patient-forms as distinct individuals per catalog-phrasings, which reads *"stroke patients"* as its own phrasing worth cataloguing. A genuine tie — S154 §3 records that this rule *"is written nowhere and the corpus is not consistent about it"*, and this pass does not fix that. Tom-confirmed.
- **B5 ("Other severely debilitating diseases and conditions" — one individual).** `conceptSeverelyDebilitatingDiseaseOrCondition`. The doublet names one open-ended residual class, not two referents. **Defensible alternative considered:** two, per NCD 280.4's B4 split of *"severe arthritis of the hip or knee"* — refused: hip and knee are distinct joints a claim can distinguish; disease and condition here are the same catch-all said twice. Tom-confirmed.
- **B6 (`conceptElectricHospitalBed` not linked).** NCD 280.1 minted it (prefLabel *"Electric Hospital Beds"*) from a DME-reference entry whose governing text is *"(See Hospital Beds §280.7 of this manual.)"* — pointing here. But §280.7 never writes the phrase: §D is titled *"Electric Powered Hospital Bed Adjustments"* and its prose covers *the adjustments*, not a bed type. Presence-not-interpretation — a policy links what it names — so `conceptElectricPoweredHospitalBedAdjustment` is minted and the sibling's label is not linked. **Defensible alternative considered:** link it, since NCD 280.1 says this is where electric hospital beds are governed. Refused: it would assert a phrasing the source does not use, which is the loss the catalog-phrasings rule exists to prevent. Same shape as `conceptMattress`, also minted at 280.1 pointing here and also unlinked — §280.7 does not mention mattresses either. Tom-confirmed.
- **B7 (TN 36 is the *same* transmittal NCD 280.4 minted).** `gemi:tn36CIM` already exists from S144. Both Revision Histories read 05/1989, *"Moved [X] from section 60-9"*, *"Effective date NA. (TN 36)"*; both policies are 280.x DME NCDs. The two entries together say what neither says alone: **CIM §60-9 was a shared durable-medical-equipment section that TN 36 broke apart**, its seat-lift payment statement going to what is now NCD 280.4 and its hospital-bed information to what is now NCD 280.7. Added `ncd280.7 referencesPolicy tn36CIM` (citing side) and `tn36CIM revisesPolicy ncd280.7` (revising side — *"Moved"* is a Change/Revision under the S151 transmittal-edge rule); the stub's description is enriched to record the second revised policy, per the `tn167CIM` precedent (S147, revising both `ncd160.2` and `ncd160.24`). Source URL stays pending under the S149 finding that CMS's public transmittal archive begins at 2000. **Defensible alternative considered:** a distinct TN 36 — no support whatever; same number, manual era, date and operation. Tom-confirmed.
- **B8 (drops).** *"ambulate"* is not minted: it is a bare verb, and its noun form *"ambulation"* is not the source's word — minting it would catalog a phrasing the policy never used, which is the mirror of the error the catalog-phrasings rule guards against. *"medical records"*, *"physicians' reports"*, *"medical necessity"* and *"initial claim"* are administrative/document vocabulary, explicitly excluded by the Clinical Concepts scope rule. *"head and foot"* and *"the controls"* are constituents of composites captured whole (`conceptElectricPoweredHospitalBedAdjustment`), not independently named concepts — and NCD 280.4's R3 (*"can be controlled by the patient"*) minted no control concept either. *"pain"* **is** minted: §A names it independently as a therapeutic purpose, and Option-B errs toward inclusion. **Defensible alternative considered:** mint `conceptAmbulation` under Option-B — a genuine tie, leaning drop on catalog-fidelity. Tom-confirmed.
- **B9 (§C's *"In well documented cases"* earns no `documentation` tag).** R6–R9 are `coverage-scope` / `eligibility` / `credentialed-actor`. The phrase qualifies the MAC medical staff's determination; it states no documentation content. Contrast §B, which says exactly what the documentation must contain and is where the policy's five `documentation` tags live. **Defensible alternative considered:** add `documentation` to R6–R9, since the phrase is a gate — defensible; the lean rests on the enumeration's gloss (*"documentation requirements"*) reading as content-bearing. Tom-confirmed.
- **B10 (deferred proposals).** Appended `NCD 280.7` to `deferred_proposals[90]` (*"MAC-discretion (contractor-discretion) coverage polarity"*, first seen NCD 260.1) — §C and §D are that pattern outright, with no national disposition either way, and the entry now stands at **four policies**, one past `worklist_schema.md`'s promotion threshold. One new entry logged, **[103] "Feature- and accessory-level coverage gated on the base item's coverage"**: §C's variable height feature is separately gated on its own clinical criteria *on top of* a bed *"approved for coverage under subsection A above"*, and §E's side rails are covered by attachment (*"when an integral part of, or an accessory to, a hospital bed"*) with no criteria of their own — two shapes of one dependency. `[64]` (device-type-conditional coverage), `[93]` (feature-upgrade payment cap), `[41]` (accessory replacement) and `[26]` (accessory utilization limits) were each considered and rejected: `[64]`'s gate is device-type characteristics distinguishing classes, not an optional add-on; `[93]` is a payment cap; `[41]` and `[26]` govern already-covered accessories. Tom-confirmed.
- **No codes; publication + source.** No inline HCPCS/ICD references and no Coding Information section (NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). `publicationNumber "100-3"` with the corpus majority (§4 item 18: 46/3 after this pass). `manualSectionNumber "280.7"`. `dc:source` refreshed from the stub's `…?NCDId=227` to Tom's `…?ncdId=227` — the user-supplied URL is canonical and the casing difference is not a finding (SKILL.md §*"Medicare URLs are not canonical; the user's URL is"*).
- **Effective date is an Other-Versions fallback.** Tracking Information reads *"This is a longstanding national coverage determination. The effective date of this version has not been posted."*; the Other Versions table supplies 01/01/1966. Same fallback as NCD 30.1, NCD 280.2, NCD 270.4 and NCD 280.3's V1. No implementation date is posted.
- **Layout finding, surfaced not fixed.** NCD 280.1's `# POLICY STUBS (cited by NCD 280.1, not yet extracted)` sub-banner is **empty**, and its four 280.x stubs — `ncd280.7` among them until this pass — sit unbannered at the tail of NCD 20.8.1's `CLINICAL CONCEPT INDIVIDUALS` sub-section, where a reader would attribute them to NCD 20.8.1. Promoting `ncd280.7` removes one of the four; `ncd280.8`, `ncd280.14` and `ncd280.16` remain orphaned and the empty banner remains empty. The move is mechanically trivial and triple-neutral, but it touches three other policies' records, so it is named rather than done unilaterally. See handoff §4.
- **Sub-section order follows SKILL.md, not the three most recent policies.** `PROVIDER CREDENTIAL INDIVIDUALS` precedes `CLINICAL CONCEPT INDIVIDUALS` per §File Layout Conventions slots 3 and 4, and per the corpus majority (15 policies). NCD 240.1 (S151), NCD 270.1 (S152) and NCD 280.3 (S154) invert them — the three most recent, which is what makes it worth writing down. See handoff §4.

### NCD 280.8 — Air-Fluidized Bed

*Extracted S156 (2026-07-17). `gemi:ncd280.8_r1` – `_r25`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-17 (Session 156). 25 rules at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; no inline HCPCS/ICD codes — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (air-fluidized beds / Durable Medical Equipment); domain axis omitted per convention. `gemi:ncd280.8` was a `planPromote` NCD stub (minted during NCD 280.1's extraction, whose Durable Medical Equipment Reference List entry *"Air-Fluidized Beds and Bead Beds"* cross-references §280.8), promoted to a fully-extracted `planDone` policy (stub collapsed from its position in the file into its own top-level section; workflow entry moved `planPromote / isInEffect=True → planDone / isInEffect=True`, all four headers recomputed from the file). Version 1 is the only version — the Other Versions table lists it alone (11/01/2000 – N/A, *"You are here"*) — so **no cross-version subtractive audit applies**. 8 axis-2 `rule_type` values (39 `gem:ruleType` triples): eligibility (13), non-coverage (7), service-definition (6), coverage-scope (4), documentation (3), credentialed-actor (3), payment-rule (2), frequency (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit category: Durable Medical Equipment (reuse). 3 provider credentials, all reuses (`credentialAttendingPhysician`, `credentialPhysician`, `credentialDMESupplier`). 63 clinical-concept links — 53 mints + 10 reuses. 2 healthcare settings — `settingHome` (reuse) + `settingInstitution` (mint). 6 policy-to-policy references — 3 reuses (`pub100_04_ch23`, `cag00017N`, `cag00017R`) + 3 transmittal mints (`tn128CIM`, `tn55CIM`, `tn44CIM`), each with the reciprocal `revisesPolicy` on the transmittal side, plus 1 change-request mint (`cr1294`, linked from `tn128CIM` via `transmitsChangeRequest`, not from the policy).

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | Indications ¶1: air fluidized beds covered for services rendered on or after July 30, 1990 | coverage-scope |
| R2 | Indications ¶2: Medicare payment for home use for treatment of pressure sores where reasonable and necessary for the individual patient | coverage-scope |
| R3 | Reasonable-and-necessary list, bullet 1: stage 3 (full thickness tissue loss) or stage 4 (deep tissue destruction) pressure sore | eligibility |
| R4 | Same list, bullet 2: patient bedridden or chair bound as a result of severely limited mobility | eligibility |
| R5 | Same list, bullet 3: in the absence of the bed, the patient would require institutionalization | eligibility |
| R6 | Same list, bullet 4: written order by the attending physician on a comprehensive assessment and evaluation after a conservative-treatment course of at least one month without progression toward wound healing, which may include an institutional period where documentation verifies the treatment was rendered | eligibility; documentation; credentialed-actor |
| R7 | Same list, bullet 5: wet-to-dry dressings for wound debridement continuing beyond 30 days do not preclude coverage, nor does debridement recurring after the first 30-day course; documentation of continued need must be available in all instances | coverage-scope; documentation |
| R8 | Same list, bullet 6: a trained adult caregiver available to assist with ADLs, fluid balance, dry skin care, repositioning, recognition and management of altered mental status, dietary needs, prescribed treatments, and management and support of the bed system and its problems such as leakage | eligibility |
| R9 | Same list, bullet 7: a physician directs the home treatment regimen and reevaluates and recertifies the need monthly | eligibility; credentialed-actor; frequency |
| R10 | Same list, bullet 8: all other alternative equipment considered and ruled out | eligibility |
| R11 | Conservative-treatment list, bullet 1: frequent repositioning with particular attention to relief of pressure over bony prominences (usually every 2 hours) | service-definition; eligibility |
| R12 | Same list, bullet 2: use of a specialized support surface (Group II) designed to reduce pressure and shear forces on healing ulcers and to prevent new ulcer formation | service-definition; eligibility |
| R13 | Same list, bullet 3: necessary treatment to resolve any wound infection | service-definition; eligibility |
| R14 | Same list, bullet 4: optimization of nutrition status to promote wound healing | service-definition; eligibility |
| R15 | Same list, bullet 5: debridement by any means (including wet to dry dressings, which do not require an *"occulsive"* covering) to remove devitalized tissue from the wound bed | service-definition; eligibility |
| R16 | Same list, bullet 6: maintenance of a clean, moist bed of granulation tissue with moist dressings protected by an occlusive covering while the wound heals | service-definition; eligibility |

**Notes**
- **B1 (Item/Service Description dropped as a rule).** *"An air-fluidized bed uses warm air under pressure to set small ceramic beads in motion which simulate the movement of fluid. When the patient is placed in the bed, his body weight is evenly distributed over a large surface area which creates a sensation of "floating.""* is a device-mechanism definition: the operative rules execute by matching the device, not by re-reading how it works. Corollary #2 — the verbatim text is enriched onto `gemi:conceptAirFluidizedBed`'s `gem:description`, appended after NCD 280.1's minting note. The NCD 240.5 B2 / NCD 30.1 B3 precedent. **Defensible alternative considered:** keep it as a `service-definition` rule, per NCD 270.4 R1, which does exactly that with its own Item/Service Description — a real precedent, not a strawman, and the reason this is a borderline at all. Refused: NCD 270.4's description states what the *service* is for coverage purposes; this one states how the *machine* works. Tom-confirmed.
- **B2 (`conceptCeramicBead`, not "small ceramic bead").** *"small"* is a size descriptor, not part of the concept's name; plurality normalizes. **Defensible alternative considered:** carry the source's full noun phrase per catalog-phrasings — refused: catalog-phrasings distinguishes *phrasings the policy uses to name a thing*, and no rule turns on the beads' size. Tom-confirmed.
- **B3 (stage parentheticals become their own concepts).** *"a stage 3 (full thickness tissue loss) or stage 4 (deep tissue destruction) pressure sore"* yields **four** individuals: `conceptStage3PressureSore`, `conceptStage4PressureSore` (head noun distributes), plus `conceptFullThicknessTissueLoss` and `conceptDeepTissueDestruction`. **Defensible alternative considered:** weld each gloss into its stage's label under the §43 qualifier rule → `conceptStage3FullThicknessTissueLossPressureSore` — refused on two counts: the §43 pattern folds a lowercase *qualifier* into the URI, and these parentheticals are named clinical findings rather than qualifiers of the sore; and splitting keeps the pair parallel to `conceptStageIIIPressureUlcer` / `conceptStageIVPressureUlcer` (NCD 270.1). Tom-confirmed.
- **B4 (three TN 48 §20.29 reuses, one refusal).** This policy's conservative-treatment list is a near-sibling of TN 48 §20.29's standard-wound-care list, which is where four of the ten reuses come from. **Reused** on the S152 *"demonstrably minted from this same wording"* reading: `conceptDebridementOfDevitalizedTissue` (TN 48: *"debridement by any means to remove devitalized tissue"*), `conceptMoistGranulationTissueBed` (TN 48: *"maintenance of a clean, moist bed of granulation tissue with appropriate moist dressings"* — word-for-word this policy's phrase), `conceptDevitalizedTissue`, `conceptFrequentRepositioning`. **Refused** for `conceptNutritionalStatusOptimization`: the source here says *"Optimization of nutrition status"*, TN 48 said *"optimization of nutritional status"* — *"nutrition"* vs *"nutritional"* is a **word change**, not the plurality or punctuation the singular-normalization rule covers, so catalog-phrasings mints `conceptOptimizationOfNutritionStatus`, in the source's word order rather than TN 48's head-noun-first normalization. **Defensible alternative considered:** reuse it and treat the adjective/noun alternation as a morphological variant of one term — a genuine tie, since nothing clinical turns on it; the lean rests on catalog-phrasings meaning what it says, and on the S152 note that TN 48's own normalization is why an exact-prefLabel test fails against its source wording. Tom-confirmed.
- **B5 (one debridement mint, one wet-to-dry mint).** `conceptWoundDebridement` covers both *"wound debridement"* and the later bare *"Should additional debridement again become necessary"* — the *"again"* is the tell that the second is a back-reference, so the pronominal-back-reference rule bars a second mint. `conceptWetToDryDressing` covers both *"wet-to-dry dressings"* (R7) and *"wet to dry dressings"* (R15): a punctuation-only difference, which the singular-normalization rule's sibling clause folds. Both rule strings stay verbatim in their source forms. **Defensible alternative considered:** two dressing individuals per catalog-phrasings, on the reading that a hyphen is a phrasing difference — refused: catalog-phrasings exists to preserve *what the policy calls a thing*, and CMS calls it the same thing twice with a typesetting slip in between. Tom-confirmed.
- **B6 (source misspells *"occulsive"*).** The debridement bullet writes *"occulsive covering"*; the maintenance bullet writes *"occlusive covering"*. R15 keeps the misspelling verbatim (S152 rule); the concept takes the correct spelling in both prefLabel and URI (`conceptOcclusiveCovering`) and records the variant. Minted distinct from `conceptOcclusiveDressing` (A52519) — a covering over a dressing is not the dressing. Note the still-open S139 carry-forward on *"autonomic dysflexia"* is the same shape and remains unresolved; this pass does not settle it, it follows the rule as written. Tom-confirmed.
- **B7 (`credentialDMESupplier` linked).** *"the written order from the attending physician is furnished to the supplier prior to the delivery of the equipment"* — the supplier receives the order and delivers the equipment, and the sequence is a payment precondition. Composite-role inference (S37 pass 7): DME benefit context + *"supplier"* in the operative sentence. **Defensible alternative considered:** no link, reading *"supplier"* as administrative vocabulary the strict-prose rule excludes — refused: the strict-prose rule excludes phrasings that name no actor, and here the supplier is an actor on whose receipt of the order payment turns. Tom-confirmed.
- **B8 (`settingInstitution` minted; no `skos:broader` asserted).** *"This month of prerequisite conservative treatment may include some period in an institution"* is a locus of furnishing, which is what `gem:HealthcareSetting` is for. **No parent** is asserted: the vocabulary has no broader place above *institution*. The interesting edge runs the other way — `settingHospital` would be `institution`'s **child** — and asserting it would edit an existing individual outside this policy's scope. Named, not done. **Defensible alternative considered:** treat *"institution"* as a `ClinicalConcept` (the counterfactual `conceptInstitutionalization` already exists) — refused: the two are different things. `conceptInstitutionalization` is the *outcome the bed averts* (R5); `settingInstitution` is *where prior treatment may have happened* (R6). Both are minted. Tom-confirmed.
- **B9 (TN 55 and TN 44 mint as CIM without a rendition).** Neither Revision-History entry posts a Coverage Transmittal Link, so the priority-1 filename test is unavailable. The **era gate** disqualifies Pub. 100-03, Pub. 100-04 and OTN outright (1992 and 1990 both precede 2003), leaving CIM (HCFA Pub. 6). Corroborated twice: this policy's own in-effect deliverer TN 128 **is** filename-verified CIM (`R128CIM.pdf`), and TN 36 (05/1989) → TN 44 (07/1990) → TN 55 (01/1992) → TN 78 (1995) → TN 128 (10/2000) is one monotonically dated CIM series across the corpus. **All three mints have a same-numbered twin already in the graph, from a different manual** — `gemi:tn128CP` (Pub. 100-04, NCD 160.24), `gemi:tn55NCD` (Pub. 100-03, NCD 160.12), `gemi:tn44NCD` (Pub. 100-03, NCD 240.1). Three for three, and every one of them a different document. The mandatory manual token is exactly what keeps each pair apart, which is why the pre-flight collision check ran clean on all three. Source URLs pending and expected to stay pending (the S148/S149 finding: CMS's public archive begins at 2000); no URL constructed by analogy. All three transmittals take `revisesPolicy` under the S151 edge rule — *"Defined"*, *"Clarified"* and *"Permitted"* are each a change. **Defensible alternative considered:** mint token-less or defer the manual assignment until a rendition surfaces — refused: the token is mandatory, and an era-gated inference with two independent corroborations is not a guess. Tom-confirmed.
- **B10 (three qualifier calls, all minting).** `conceptCoexistingPulmonaryDisease` over reusing `conceptPulmonaryDisease` (NCD 240.2.1): *"coexisting"* is clinically load-bearing — the exclusion turns on comorbidity with the pressure sore, not on pulmonary disease as such — so S154 B10's *reuse-when-the-qualifier-adds-nothing* rule does not reach it. `conceptCoughing` over reusing `conceptCough`: the gerund names the act, the noun the sign. `conceptWrittenOrder` as a ClinicalConcept rather than document vocabulary, following `conceptPhysiciansPrescription` (NCD 280.7) — the physician's order is the clinical instrument the coverage decision runs on. **Defensible alternative considered** for the last: exclude it under the Clinical Concepts scope rule, alongside *"medical records"* and *"initial claim"* (NCD 280.7 B8) — refused on the same ground NCD 280.7 kept `conceptPhysiciansPrescription`: the order is *issued by a clinician about a patient*, where a claim record is not. Tom-confirmed.
- **B11 (deferred proposals).** Appended `NCD 280.8` to `deferred_proposals[57]` (*"conservative-therapy trial-duration coverage criteria"*, first seen NCD 280.6) — R6's *"at least one month in duration without progression toward wound healing"* is that shape exactly, bringing the entry to **two policies**. Two new entries logged. **[104] "Home-environment adequacy as a coverage condition":** R20 and R21 gate coverage on the *dwelling's* load-bearing capacity and electrical service — not on the patient, not on the device. Corroborating within this policy: R25 denies payment for the very architectural adjustments that would remedy an inadequacy, so the condition is a gate, not a coverable cost. `[64]` (device-type characteristics), `[93]` (payment cap) and `[103]` (base-item/sub-item dependency) were each considered and rejected — all three are properties of the equipment or its payment, none of the premises. **[105] "Lay-caregiver availability and capability as a coverage condition":** R8 makes a trained adult caregiver's availability a hard positive gate with an enumerated duty list, and R19 makes the caregiver's unwillingness or inability a hard exclusion — the same actor on both polarities. Corroborating outside this policy: NCD 280.3's decision points 3a and 4, where the caregiver is compensatory and must demonstrate capability and willingness. Not a `gem:ProviderCredential` (NCD 280.3's call: the caregiver holds no license), so it is currently carried as `conceptCaregiver` / `conceptTrainedAdultCaregiver` plus rule prose — which is what the entry exists to revisit. `[90]` (MAC-discretion polarity) does **not** apply: this policy states national dispositions throughout and leaves the MAC nothing to decide. Tom-confirmed.
- **B12 (bullet 5 takes the list stem anyway).** R7's content is a **carve-out plus a documentation rule**, but it sits under a stem that frames the list as requirements (*"A decision that use of an air-fluidized bed is reasonable and necessary requires that:"*). The stem is applied as the Pattern-2 prefix regardless: the misfit is CMS's, and Pattern 2 preserves the source's structure rather than repairing it. Its rule types are `coverage-scope` + `documentation`, not `eligibility` — the tags follow the content even where the stem does not. **Defensible alternative considered:** capture it Pattern-1 without the stem, on the ground that a stem that misdescribes its bullet is worse than no stem — a real tension with source-fidelity, and the reason this is flagged. Refused: dropping the stem would silently assert that CMS filed this sentence outside the list, which is a bigger loss than reproducing CMS's own imprecision. Tom-confirmed.
- **B13 (drops).** *"Reasons for Denial"* is CMS-wide boilerplate injected by the MCD web view and absent from the canonical PDF — non-canonical, not extracted (the NCD 20.8.1 / S137 rule). *"medical necessity"*, *"documentation"* and *"the equipment"* are administrative or deictic, excluded by the Clinical Concepts scope rule. *"body weight"* and *"surface area"* are constituents of the dropped device-mechanism sentence (B1) and are not independently named anywhere the rules reach. Illustrative examples **are** kept as concepts where the source names them — `conceptPlasticWrap`, `conceptOcclusiveMaterial`, `conceptElectricalImprovement`, `conceptStructuralImprovement`, `conceptLeakage` — under the examples-folded rule (folded into the rule's verbatim text, minted for queryability). Option-B inclusive throughout.
- **No codes; publication + source.** No inline HCPCS/ICD references and no Coding Information section (NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). `publicationNumber "100-3"` is stated by the document itself (not a corpus-majority inference). `manualSectionNumber "280.8"`. `dc:source` refreshed from the stub's `…?NCDId=228` to Tom's `…?NCDId=228&NCDver=1` — the user-supplied URL is canonical (SKILL.md §*"Medicare URLs are not canonical; the user's URL is"*), and the identifier, type and title all match, so this is a refresh and not a collision.
- **Effective and implementation dates are both posted.** Tracking Information gives 11/01/2000 for each; no Other-Versions fallback was needed (contrast NCD 280.7, 30.1, 280.2, 270.4). The Other Versions table independently corroborates 11/01/2000 as Version 1's start.
- **Second verbatim source misspelling, in a field we do not extract.** The Revision History's TN 128 entry reads *"Effective and implementaiton dates 11/01/2000"*. It is preserved verbatim inside `gemi:tn128CIM`'s `gem:description` quotation and flagged there as the source's; no rule carries it, since Revision History is excluded from rule extraction.
- **Sub-section order follows SKILL.md.** `CLINICAL CONCEPT INDIVIDUALS` (slot 4) follows `POLICY RULE INDIVIDUALS`; no `PROVIDER CREDENTIAL INDIVIDUALS` sub-section exists, since all three credentials are reuses and slot 3 appears only for mints. The §4 item 26 drift (NCD 240.1 / 270.1 / 280.3 inverting slots 3 and 4) is not exercised by this policy.
- **Layout finding, one closer to self-resolving.** Promoting `ncd280.8` removes the third of NCD 280.1's four orphaned 280.x stubs from the tail of NCD 20.8.1's `CLINICAL CONCEPT INDIVIDUALS` sub-section. `ncd280.14` and `ncd280.16` remain orphaned, and NCD 280.1's `# POLICY STUBS (cited by NCD 280.1, not yet extracted)` sub-banner remains empty. See handoff §4 item 25.

**Notes**
- **B1 (dated headings become the Pattern-2 prefix).** Seven covered/non-covered indications carry an effective-date heading (*"Iron Poisoning (Effective for Services Performed On or After September 26, 1984)"*). Each is applied as the rule's Pattern-2 prefix rather than dropped or split into a separate `coverage-scope` rule: the date is a condition on the rule it heads, and a downstream evaluator reads it as part of the same IF. **Defensible alternative considered:** carry each date as its own rule, per NCD 280.8 R1 (*"Air fluidized beds are covered for services rendered on or after: July 30, 1990."*) — a real precedent, and the reason this is a borderline. Refused: NCD 280.8's date sentence is a free-standing sentence in the body text with no rule of its own to attach to; these are headings over rules that state their own conditions, and Pattern 2 exists for exactly that. Tom-confirmed.
- **B2 (Criterion A's five bullets fold, not fork).** R6 is one rule carrying all five clinical findings, because the source's stem is *"and meets one or more of the following criteria"* — a disjunction **inside** a conjunctive criterion. Splitting would produce five rules each falsely asserting its own sufficiency, and would lose the *"one or more"*. The IF/THEN heuristic decides it: a Python evaluator generates **one** IF for Criterion A, with an internal OR. **Contrast §B.2.e**, which forks into R24–R27: each contraindication bullet denies on its own, so each is its own IF. The two lists look alike and behave oppositely; the stem is what tells them apart. **Defensible alternative considered:** Option B split-per-item, the corpus's usual call for bulleted lists (L36524 B1, A58075 B1) — refused on the stem. Tom-confirmed.
- **B3 (§B.2.b and §B.2.c: one rule each, lead + criteria together).** Both sections read *"…as determined by the following criteria:"* and then state the criteria. The criteria are welded into their lead rule rather than forked, because neither section's criteria are independently operative — they exist only to establish the *"proven unresponsive to less invasive medical therapy"* clause of the sentence above them. R19 and R20 each carry lead + criteria as one unit. **Defensible alternative considered:** fork each into a coverage rule plus per-criterion eligibility rules — refused: the criteria have no THEN of their own, and the *"And prior to pump implantation…"* / *"…and a preliminary trial…"* conjunctions inside them would have to be reconstructed by the reader. Tom-confirmed.
- **B4 (*implantable* ≠ *implanted*: two concepts).** `conceptImplantableInfusionPump` (§B.2 heading, §B.2.a, §C.2.a) and `conceptImplantedInfusionPump` (§B.2.d, §C.2.b) are minted separately. They are different words, not the plurality-or-punctuation the singular-normalization rule folds — the S156 B4 test — and the distinction tracks the sections: *implantable* is the device's property, *implanted* its state, and §B.2.d/§C.2.b speak of pumps already in place. **Defensible alternative considered:** one individual, treating the alternation as morphological — a genuine tie, since nothing clinical turns on it. Refused on the same ground S156 refused *"nutrition"*/*"nutritional"*. In the same section, `conceptPrimaryHepatocellularCarcinoma` **mints** rather than reusing the existing `conceptHepatocellularCarcinoma` (TN 48 §260.1): *"primary"* is load-bearing here, against the metastatic disease the same sentences distinguish. Tom-confirmed.

The Plan-turn manifest carried §B.2.b's reuse and **missed** §B.2.c's; the Generate turn built the confirmed manifest and logged the gap rather than asserting an unapproved triple. Tom confirmed the reuse after the fact, so `gemi:ncd280.14 gem:refersToClinicalConcept gemi:conceptChronicIntractablePain` is now asserted — concept links **79 → 80**, reuses **6 → 7**. **The heading and the operative sentence both stand, and are not redundant:** the heading names the indication at the corpus's existing granularity, while `conceptSevereChronicIntractablePainOfMalignantOrNonmalignantOrigin` carries the sentence's full phrase, whose three qualifiers are the coverage — *severe* raises the threshold and *of malignant or nonmalignant origin* opens the indication beyond cancer, which is what separates §B.2.c from §B.1.d. **The general rule underneath it is now codified** (SKILL.md §Clinical Concepts, *"Section headings are a mint/reuse site, not only the operative sentences"*, Tom S157): a heading is CMS naming the thing, which is what catalog-phrasings protects. **The miss was only visible because §B.2.b and §B.2.c are structurally identical** — one policy happened to contain its own control. Closes handoff §4 item 32.
- **B11 (verbatim source misspelling: *"HbAlc"*) — corrected after the Generate turn, Tom-directed.** Criterion A's first bullet writes *"Glycosylated hemoglobin level (HbAlc) > 7.0%"* — lowercase **L** where the term of art is HbA**1**c. R6 keeps the source's form verbatim, always. **The concept was first minted at the source's form and that was an error.** The reasoning offered was that the two glyphs are near-indistinguishable in most typefaces, so this is a *rendering artifact* rather than a spelling error, and the S152 rule's *"where a genuine spelling error"* antecedent was therefore not satisfied. **That antecedent does not exist.** SKILL.md's rule is unconditional — source misspells → rule verbatim always, concept corrected in prefLabel *and* URI — and the artifact argument cuts the other way: if *"HbAlc"* is a typesetting artifact, then CMS's **term** is HbA1c, so the concept must carry the correction all the more. Tom's ruling (S157): *"If the latter was used in a URI, that is an error."* `gemi:conceptGlycosylatedHemoglobinLevelHbA1c`, prefLabel *"glycosylated hemoglobin level (HbA1c)"*; `ncd280.14_r6` and the `Governing text:` quotation unchanged; the policy's `gem:description`, being a summary rather than a quotation, carries the term with the source's form noted parenthetically. **The corpus is 4/4 consistent** — `conceptHighResolutionComputedTomography` (S152), `conceptEpithelializedWoundBed` (S152), `conceptOcclusiveCovering` (S156), this one. **And handoff §4 item 28's premise was wrong in the other direction too:** it carried `autonomic dysflexia` as an open 17-session ask needing Tom's one-word confirm, when S152's rule text says outright that it closed that carry-forward and `gemi:conceptAutonomicDysreflexia` has matched it since. There were never three answers. There was one answer, applied, and one invented exception. Closes handoff §4 item 28.
- **B12 (two methodology fixes, both from this session's own errors) — Tom-confirmed, codified.** **(1) The mass-conservation proof is predicate-blind.** *"31 rules × 5 base triples + 49 ruleType = 204"* never names *which* description predicate; emitting `gem:description` produced **exactly 204**, and the parse, SHACL, the set-diff and the total all agreed. `policyrule_completeness` caught it — but that check exists for `PolicyRule` specifically, and nothing asks whether 80 concept links landed on `refersToClinicalConcept` rather than `refersToHealthcareSetting`. **SKILL.md §Verification Checkpoint now requires an expected (predicate → count) histogram, derived from the emitter's own structures rather than hand-typed, diffed against the set-diff's actual.** Applied retroactively to this session: **25 predicates, 962 triples, 0 mismatches.** The hand-typed first attempt produced four spurious mismatches out of 25, every one the projection's arithmetic rather than the graph's content — which is why the rule says *derive*. **(2) Hand-escaping TTL literals is this session's most repeated error, and its over-escaped form is silent.** Under-escaping fails to parse — loud. Over-escaping parses: the literal's *value* carries a stray backslash, and rdflib round-trips it, SHACL conforms, the count and predicate are right, and only a human reading the rendered text notices. **SKILL.md §Session Close gains an emitter contract** (escape at emit time; authors write plain text) and **§Common Failure Modes gains an *over-escaped literal* row**. Corpus scan found **3 defective literals / 6 over-escaped quotes**: `credentialAttendingPhysician` and `credentialDoctorOfMedicineOrOsteopathy` (**S41**), `conceptSevereCardiacCondition` (**S155** — two sessions old, so the mode is live, not legacy). Repaired: **3 triples out / 3 in, net 0.** Everything else in the scan came back clean — 0 predicate/object-type mismatches, 0 description-predicate misuse, 0 duplicate single-valued annotations — so the blind proof has let through exactly one class, and it is the one the emitter contract eliminates.
- **B12a (the new check, and what mutation-testing did to its design).** `literal_escape_artifact` — YELLOW, autofixable; `ALL_CHECKS` 24 → **25**; variants **V69** (over-escaped → YELLOW), **V70** (correctly escaped quote ignored → GREEN; without it the check could match one backslash and rewrite all 3,117 legitimate escapes), **V71** (escaped backslash not before a quote ignored → GREEN; zero such literals exist, which is *why* the variant is needed — the corpus cannot disconfirm an over-broad pattern on its own). Suite 68 → **71**. **The mutation testing changed the design rather than confirming it.** The first autofix matched the artifact's two-backslash *tail* and collapsed it, leaving an escaped backslash then a live quote — the literal ended early and the file would not parse. **That is the exact class the check exists to catch, written into the check.** The rdflib re-parse caught it, but V69 did **not**: the wrong pattern still *fires*, so a variant asserting *"YELLOW on the defect"* passes it. The fix was structural — the check now computes its repair and **parse-probes it at detection time**, reporting RED and offering no autofix if the repair fails to parse or fails to remove the artifact — which moves the mutation into the finding's **tier**, where V69 can kill it. An idempotence assertion kills the no-op-repair mutation the same way. **4 of 5 mutations killed. M5 (drop the parse-probe) survives inherently** — under a correct pattern the probe never fires, so its absence is unobservable except in combination with a second mutation. Recorded, not papered over (S144 rule).
