### NCD 280.16 — Seat Elevation Equipment (Power Operated) on Power Wheelchairs

*Extracted S158 (2026-07-17). `gemi:ncd280.16_r1` – `_r4`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-17 (Session 158). 4 rules at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; no inline HCPCS/ICD codes and no Coding Information section — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (power seat elevation equipment / Durable Medical Equipment); domain axis omitted per convention. `gemi:ncd280.16` was a `planPromote` NCD stub (minted during NCD 280.1's extraction, whose Durable Medical Equipment Reference List entry *"Seat Elevation Equipment"* cross-references §280.16), promoted to a fully-extracted `planDone` policy (stub collapsed from the tail of NCD 20.8.1's `CLINICAL CONCEPT INDIVIDUALS` sub-section into its own top-level section; workflow entry moved `planPromote / isInEffect=True → planDone / isInEffect=True`, all five headers recomputed from the file). **Version 1, NCDId=376, 4 pp, effective 2023-05-16, implemented 2023-09-04 — both dates posted in Tracking Information, so no Other-Versions fallback.** Single-version — the Other Versions table lists Version 1 alone (05/16/2023 – N/A, *"You are here"*) — so **no cross-version retention analysis applies**. 4 axis-2 `rule_type` values (8 `gem:ruleType` triples): eligibility (2), setting-definition (2), coverage-scope (2), credentialed-actor (2). No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit category: Durable Medical Equipment (reuse). 5 provider credentials — 1 reuse (`credentialPhysicalTherapist`) + **4 mints** (`credentialLicensedCertifiedMedicalProfessional`, `credentialOccupationalTherapist`, `credentialOtherPractitioner`, `credentialDurableMedicalEquipmentMedicareAdministrativeContractor`). 33 clinical-concept links — 23 mints + 10 reuses. 1 healthcare setting (`settingHome`, reuse). 5 policy-to-policy references — 4 reuses (`cag00461N`, `pub100_02_ch15`, `pub100_04_ch20`, `pub100_04_ch23`) + **1 transmittal mint** (`tn12183NCD`, with the reciprocal `revisesPolicy` on the transmittal side). No change requests — the document names none.

**The policy is a two-leg feature determination and the legs disagree about the base item.** §B states a *national* coverage rule for the feature when the base item is a complex rehabilitative power-driven wheelchair; §D hands the *DME MAC* discretion when it is any other Medicare covered power wheelchair. §C is `N/A` — the policy denies nothing nationally, which is why no rule carries `non-coverage`.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | §B stem: effective for services on or after 05/16/2023, power seat elevation equipment is reasonable and necessary for individuals using complex rehabilitative power-driven wheelchairs when the following conditions are met | coverage-scope |
| R2 | §B condition 1 (δ-prefixed): a specialty evaluation confirming the individual's ability to safely operate the equipment in the home, performed by a licensed/certified medical professional (PT, OT, or other practitioner) with specific training and experience in rehabilitation wheelchair evaluations | eligibility; credentialed-actor; setting-definition |
| R3 | §B condition 2 (δ-prefixed): at least one of (a) weight bearing transfers in the home via upper extremities during a non-level (uneven) sitting transfer and/or lower extremities during a sit to stand transfer; (b) a required non-weight bearing transfer, e.g. a dependent transfer; (c) reaching from the power wheelchair to complete one or more MRADLs — with or without caregiver assistance, assistive equipment, or a floor or mounted lift | eligibility; setting-definition |
| R4 | §D: the DME MAC has discretion to determine reasonable and necessary coverage for individuals using Medicare covered power wheelchairs other than complex rehabilitative power-driven wheelchairs | coverage-scope; credentialed-actor |

#### Notes

- **B1 (§B decomposition — three rules, and the stem is again what decides it).** §B is one sentence plus a two-item numbered list, the second item carrying three lettered alternatives. Conjunctive conditions fork (each denies on its own); the internal disjunction folds. So: R1 = the verbatim stem; R2 and R3 = conditions 1 and 2, δ-prefixed with `[Section B scope: conditions for coverage of power seat elevation equipment for individuals using complex rehabilitative power-driven wheelchairs]`; and 2.a–c stay inside R3, because the stem reads *"At least one of the following apply"*. **NCD 240.9 §B.II.(a)(i) is the exact shape** — R15 an umbrella ending in a colon, R16–R18 δ-prefixed, R18 folding its own *"at least one of the following"*. The δ-prefix rather than Pattern 2 because the source has letter-labeled sub-items nested under numbered ones (SKILL.md §Selection rule). **The alternative was one Pattern-3 rule for all of §B** — the NCD 260.1 liver-transplant shape (*"Effective September 1, 2001, Medicare covers adult liver transplantation ... when the following conditions are met: ..."*, all conditions in one string). Defensible on a literal IF/THEN reading — §B is one IF — but the corpus does not read conjunctions that way: NCD 280.8, one policy earlier, forked eight conjunctive *"requires that"* conditions into eight rules. Tom confirmed 3.
- **B2 (a definitional pointer is not a rule).** *"Complex rehabilitative power-driven wheelchairs are defined in 42 CFR §414.202."* is carried verbatim as governing text on `gemi:conceptComplexRehabilitativePowerDrivenWheelchair`, not as a `gem:PolicyRule`. Its **whole content is a pointer** to where the definition lives, so it is a navigational pointer under § *"Scope-boundary sentences: capture vs. drop"* (it asserts no coverage effect), and SKILL.md corollary #2 puts a definition on the named entity. NCD 210.10's R15/R16/R17 are the precedent. **The alternative was a `definition` rule under corollary #4** (verbatim-cross-reference posture), on the ground that the term it defines is the gate of R1 and an evaluator cannot execute R1 without it — the strongest form of the argument, and the reason this is a borderline rather than a mechanical drop. It was rejected because the sentence carries **no operative content of its own**, which is what separates it from `gemi:a54969_r1`'s *"42 CFR Section 410.32 indicates that diagnostic tests may only be ordered by the treating physician..."* — that sentence states a rule and cites a regulation; this one only cites. Tom confirmed the drop.
- **B3 (the policy names its subject three ways and gets one individual).** §A/§B-stem/§D write *"power seat elevation equipment"*; §B.1 writes bare *"seat elevation equipment"*; the document title writes *"Seat Elevation Equipment (Power Operated) on Power Wheelchairs"*. Only the first mints (`conceptPowerSeatElevationEquipment`). §B.1's bare form is **the stem's phrase shortened two clauses later** — the policy is avoiding repetition, not naming a second concept (SKILL.md § *"Pronominal back-references are not mint-triggers"*, whose rationale reaches a shortened noun phrase as it reaches *"such tests"*). Independently, the URI the bare form wants — `gemi:conceptSeatElevationEquipment` — **is already held by NCD 280.1's own phrasing** (*"Seat Elevation Equipment (power-operated) on Medicare Covered Power Wheelchairs"*), a non-plurality collision that the S43 rule sends to the SME rather than auto-reusing. The alternative was to mint both with a distinguishing URI; it would give one policy two individuals for one device. Tom confirmed one.
- **B8 (the title is not a heading — the nearest untested edge of S157's rule).** S157 codified *"Section headings are a mint/reuse site, not only the operative sentences"* one session ago. A **document title** is not a section heading: it names the policy, and the policy individual already carries it as `gem:prefLabel`. 280.16's four section headings — *General*, *Nationally Covered Indications*, *Nationally Non-Covered Indications*, *Other* — name no clinical concept, so this policy exercises the S157 rule to a null result and the title is the only question it raises. **The alternative is real and was surfaced rather than assumed away:** S157's rationale is *"a heading is CMS naming the thing"*, and a title is CMS naming the thing more authoritatively than any heading does, so the rule's reason arguably reaches a fortiori where its text does not. Tom confirmed no.
- **B4 (a disjunction of two devices is two concepts).** *"Transfers may be accomplished with or without a floor or mounted lift"* is a suspended compound — *"a floor [lift] or mounted lift"* — and yields `conceptFloorLift` and `conceptMountedLift`. A provider note carries one or the other, never the disjunction, and the single-term-linkage rationale wants each to link a claim on its own; the shape is the concept-side sibling of the S39 slash-decompose rule for credentials. The alternative was one composite at the verbatim phrase under the composite-concepts rule, rejected because *"floor"* and *"mounted"* are not word-parts of a composite but alternatives of a disjunction. Tom confirmed two.
- **B5 (the slash rule reads roles, not adjectives).** *"licensed/certified medical professional"* mints **one** credential at the verbatim phrase. The S39 rule decomposes slash-separated **role names** (*"referring/ordering physician"*, *"physician/nurse practitioner/physician assistant"*) because two people may fill them on one claim; here the slash separates two adjectives qualifying one head noun, and neither *"licensed medical professional"* nor *"certified medical professional"* appears in the document. Tom confirmed one.
- **B6 (an acronym gloss is not a phrasing difference).** *"physical therapist (PT)"* **reuses** `gemi:credentialPhysicalTherapist` (prefLabel *"physical therapist"*). The difference is a parenthetical acronym on an identical phrase, and SKILL.md §797 drops acronym parentheticals from URIs precisely because they carry no distinguishing content — so a mint would collide on `credentialPhysicalTherapist` and need a contrived URI. Surfaced rather than auto-reused, per the S43 rule that a non-plurality collision is the SME's call. **The alternative reads catalog-phrasings' letter** (*"acronym vs. full-form ... defaults to mint"*), but that clause is written for the case where the existing prefLabel uses **only one** of the two forms; here the existing prefLabel **is** the full form the source writes, with a gloss appended. Tom confirmed reuse. *"occupational therapist (OT)"* has no existing individual and mints — the corpus's first OT credential, against three physical-therapist individuals.
- **The other two credential mints are ordinary catalog-phrasings calls, and both sit next to a near-neighbour.** `credentialOtherPractitioner` (*"other practitioner"*) against the existing `credentialOtherQualifiedPractitioner` (*"other qualified practitioner"*, NCD 210.2, a 42 CFR 410.56(a) term of art) — a word differs and the roles genuinely differ: 280.16's qualification is training in rehabilitation wheelchair evaluations, not a regulatory enumeration. `credentialDurableMedicalEquipmentMedicareAdministrativeContractor` against the existing `credentialMedicareAdministrativeContractor` (*"Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC)"*, NCD 240.2) — the source names the DME jurisdiction specifically. Both links are licensed under the strict-prose rule: §B.1's professional **performs** the required evaluation, and §D's DME MAC **determines** coverage (the NCD 240.2 MAC-discretion precedent).
- **The MRADL cluster is NCD 280.3's, reused whole.** §B.2.c is near-verbatim 280.3's sentence — *"...mobility related activities of daily living (MRADLs) such as toileting, feeding, dressing, grooming and bathing in customary locations within the home"* against 280.3's *"...mobility-related activities of daily living (MRADLs) such as toileting, feeding, dressing, grooming, and bathing in customary locations within the home"* — so six reuses follow: `conceptMobilityRelatedActivitiesOfDailyLiving` (the only difference is 280.3's hyphen — punctuation-only), `conceptToileting`, `conceptFeeding`, `conceptGrooming`, `conceptBathing`, and **`conceptDressingMRADL`**, which is S154's disambiguated homograph. That last one is the reuse worth naming: bare `gemi:conceptDressing` is held by the wound-care sense, and 280.3 minted the MRADL sense with a qualifier the source does not write **for exactly this** — the second policy to say *"dressing"* in an MRADL list. The disambiguation paid for itself four sessions later.
- **Four more reuses, three of them plurality-only.** `conceptCane` / `conceptCrutch` / `conceptWalker` (existing prefLabels *"Canes"* / *"Crutches"* / *"Walkers"*, NCD 280.1 table-source vestiges) are plurality-only collision reuses under the S43 rule, following NCD 280.3's precedent for the same three. `conceptPowerWheelchair` is the fourth and the least mechanical: its prefLabel is *"Wheelchairs (power operated)"*, NCD 280.1's DME Reference List rendering, which differs from *"power wheelchair"* by word order and plurality rather than plurality alone — but **NCD 280.3 already reuses it for its own *"power wheelchair"* prose**, and the S152 gap reading applies (*reuse when the existing individual was demonstrably minted from this same wording*), so the corpus has an answer and it is reuse.
- **Option-B inclusive on §A's device geometry.** The General section's three sentences yield five concepts and no rule (SKILL.md corollary #2; the NCD 280.14 B8 / NCD 280.8 B1 precedent that §A General is not a rule): `conceptPowerSeatElevationEquipment`, `conceptSeatedPosition`, `conceptElectromechanicalLiftSystem`, `conceptVerticalSeatToFloorHeight`, and — from the **negative** half of the definition — `conceptSeatedAngle` and `conceptSeatsAngleRelativeToTheGround`. The negative half is not decoration: *"It does not change the seated angles or the seat's angle relative to the ground"* is what separates seat elevation from tilt and recline, and the two geometries it names are different facts, so both mint.
- **Drops.** The `Cross-references:` line (Benefit Policy Manual Ch. 15; Claims Processing Manual Chs. 20 and 23) is a **navigational scope-boundary pointer** — dropped as a rule, all three chapters preserved via `gem:referencesPolicy` (§ *"Scope-boundary sentences: capture vs. drop"*, the L33718 D4 precedent). *"(This NCD last reviewed May 16, 2023.)"* is document metadata and goes in the policy's `gem:description`. *"Please Note: This may not be an exhaustive list of all applicable Medicare benefit categories for this item or service."* is CMS-wide MCD boilerplate around the Benefit Category field; the corpus carries it once, as a source note in a comment, and never as a rule. §C's *"N/A"* is a **confirmed empty section, not a gate** — the document is complete.
- **`tn12183NCD` is the first transmittal in the 280.x run the era gate did not have to adjudicate.** The Coverage Transmittal Link posts `R12183NCD.pdf`, so the manual token comes from priority 1 — a verified rendition filename — and 2023 is two decades past Pub. 100-03's start with a number far above the CIM's 167 ceiling. Contrast the five sessions behind it: S156 minted two CIM transmittals on the era gate **alone**, and S157's chain crossed the manual boundary mid-history. **The `"100-3"` / `"100-03"` split is load-bearing here for the second policy running** — `ncd280.16` carries `"100-3"` because its document says so, `tn12183NCD` carries `"100-03"` because `transmittal_manual_token` requires it of an `NCD` token; both are right under the rules as written, and the two rules still have not been reconciled (§4 item 18). The edge is `gem:revisesPolicy` under the S151 transmittal-edge rule: TN 12183 **created** §280.16, and New is a change — the same V1-delivering application as `tn143CIM` at S157. The document names no Change Request, so none is minted; TN 12183's own pass will find it.
- **`deferred_proposals[103]` meets its second policy and is kept `logged` (B7).** *"Feature- and accessory-level coverage gated on the base item's coverage"* was logged at S155 from NCD 280.7's variable height feature; 280.16 is shape (a) — a feature gated on its own clinical criteria on top of a covered base item — and **sharpens it twice**: the feature's gate is national rather than MAC-discretionary, and §D names the base item's **coverage status** explicitly (*"Medicare covered power wheelchairs"*), which 280.7 never does. It also shows the dependency **coming apart inside one policy**: §B gates on the base item being **used**, §D on its being **covered**, so the proposal's own title is literally true of only one of the two legs, and any schema shape has to say which it means. `gemi:conceptMedicareCoveredPowerWheelchair` is minted specifically to carry §D's phrasing distinct from `conceptPowerWheelchair`. **Kept `logged` rather than promoted**: three instances now exist (280.7, 280.1's table entries, 280.16) but no shape has converged across them, and the obvious candidate — a concept-to-concept dependency link — is both premature concept structuring and a claim §B never makes. The alternative was to promote to `approved` on the 3-policy threshold; the cost is committing a shape on three heterogeneous instances five policies before the checkpoint that would review it. Scheduled there, alongside [99] and [100]. Tom confirmed `logged`.
- **Layout finding, closed.** Promoting `ncd280.16` removes **the last of NCD 280.1's four orphaned 280.x stubs** from the tail of NCD 20.8.1's `CLINICAL CONCEPT INDIVIDUALS` sub-section. §4 item 25 is closed by this pass; NCD 280.1's `# POLICY STUBS (cited by NCD 280.1, not yet extracted)` sub-banner is now empty **and correct** — every stub it once held has been promoted. Sub-section order follows SKILL.md: `PROVIDER CREDENTIAL INDIVIDUALS` (slot 3) precedes `CLINICAL CONCEPT INDIVIDUALS` (slot 4), and both appear because both families have mints.

### A55426 — Standard Documentation Requirements for All Claims Submitted to DME MACs - Policy Article

Categorized 2026-07-18 (Session 161). 78 rules. Single-domain policy (cross-cutting DMEPOS documentation/process); domain axis omitted per convention. The DME MAC **Standard Documentation Requirements (SDR)** article — the cross-cutting article every DMEPOS LCD and LCD-related Policy Article points to for the general (non-policy-specific) requirements: ORDERS/SWO/WOPD, the Final Rule 1713 Required List + face-to-face encounter, general documentation / R&N / medical-record rules, continued medical need + continued use, claim narratives + date spans, refill documentation, the three Proof-of-Delivery methods, correct HCPCS coding + NOC billing, equipment retained from a prior payer, and repairs vs. replacement (incl. prosthesis-specific rules) + signatures. **Full extraction at S161 reversing the prior deliberate zero-outcome stub** (handoff §4 item 38); closes `deferred_proposals[18]` (SDR framework, `approved → complete`). No codes appear in current prose except the **EY modifier** (`hcpcs:EY`); the entire Coding Information section is literal N/A. No new axis-2 rule_type values introduced — all categorizations use the existing vocabulary.

#### Notes

- **B1 (the precedence pointer is operative, so it is a rule — R1).** *"The information in the LCDs and/or related policy articles supersede this document. Where there are differences between the policies and this article, the LCDs and/or related policy articles shall take precedence."* is captured as a `procedural` / `coverage-scope` conflict-resolution rule rather than dropped as a navigational preamble: it tells a downstream evaluator which of two applicable documents governs on conflict, which is operative content, not a pointer to where content lives. The `***IMPORTANT***` sentence that introduces it (*"All Policy Specific Documentation Requirements are located in the LCD-related Policy Article"*) is the navigational half and is dropped. Tom confirmed capture.
- **B2 (the DME MAC jurisdiction table is logged, not a rule).** The Contractor Information table — the four DME MACs (Jurisdictions A/B/C/D: Noridian J-A and J-D, CGS J-B and J-C) and the states each covers — is dropped as framing and **logged as a new `deferred_proposals` "DME MAC jurisdictions" candidate** (contractor-to-state assignment structured data; distinct from `[90]`'s MAC-discretion coverage-polarity proposal). Tom directed: log it.
- **B3 (statutory / CFR / Final-Rule citations fold, they are not minted).** SSA §§1861(r), 1861(aa)(5), 1834(a)(1)(E)(iv), 1834(h)(5), 1848(k)(3)(B); 42 CFR 424.57, 410.38, 410.78, 414.65, 414.40, 414.202; 45 CFR 162.1002; Final Rule 1713 (84 Fed. Reg. Vol 217); and CMS-1780-F are carried as `statutory-framing` on the rule they support (R6, R16, R19, R26, R28, R42, R50, R59), **not** minted as graph entities — GEM has no class for a CFR/USC/Federal-Register citation. Tom confirmed fold.
- **B4 (credentials — two mints, chiropractor stays text).** `credentialOrthotist` and `credentialProsthetist` mint (R28, R77); `credentialTreatingPractitioner`, `credentialPhysician`, `credentialPhysicianAssistant`, `credentialNursePractitioner`, `credentialClinicalNurseSpecialist`, `credentialDMESupplier` reuse. The **chiropractor** appears only as *prohibited from prescribing DMEPOS* (R8) — a prohibition, not a required credential — so it is kept as R8 text and **not** minted as a credential individual. Tom confirmed.
- **References — the full catalog minted (D1).** Unlike the peer PAP article A52467, which captured only its substantive in-text references, A55426's Associated-Documents catalog **is** its substantive reference set: as the SDR article it governs every DMEPOS policy, so all **59 LCD-related Policy Articles + 59 LCDs** are linked via `gem:referencesPolicy` (100 minted as `planPromote` stubs, URL pending; 18 already extracted), together with **NCD 280.1** (correct-coding generic categories) and the two cited manual chapters — **Pub. 100-08 Ch. 3** (Program Integrity Manual; minted `gem:CMSmanualChapter` with the user-supplied URL) and **Pub. 100-02 Ch. 15** (Benefit Policy Manual; already in graph). 121 references total. This is a deliberate departure from the A52467 precedent, justified by A55426's unique cross-cutting scope and directed by Tom.
- **`planDone` corrected in meaning, not in value.** The prior stub was honestly `gem:planDone` under the pre-S48 completeness standard (it had been read in full and, under the then-current home-oxygen domain scope, correctly yielded no in-scope content). S48's rule-documentation promotion and the `[85]` rule-form-complement campaign moved the standard; this extraction satisfies the current one. `gem:nextPlannedStep` stays `gem:planDone`, now truthfully. (Handoff §4 item 38; the S160 lesson that *`planDone` is a claim about a standard, and the standard moved*.)
- **Drops (framing).** The Contractor Information jurisdiction table (B2, logged), the AMA/AHA/ADA copyright blocks, the `***IMPORTANT***` navigational preamble, the *"'All claims' refers to..."* scope gloss, the Public-Versions table, and the Revision History (no policy-document references in it — only Final Rules and CFR, which fold per B3). The `Article Text` opening (*"Many errors reported in Medicare audits..."*) is framing; its operative content is R25 (7-year retention).

### A52514 — Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment - Policy Article

Categorized 2026-07-18 (Session 161). 97 policy-scope rules (plus the pre-existing anchor-scope `gemi:a52514_group1_r1`). Single-domain policy (home oxygen equipment payment/coding/documentation); domain axis omitted per convention. The DME MAC Policy Article companion to L33797, carrying the **non-medical-necessity, statutory coverage and payment rules** for home oxygen: reasonable useful lifetime (RUL), the 36-month rental and months 37-60 / 61+ payment structure, oxygen-contents and accessories payment/bundling, maintenance & servicing (M&S), break-in-service, relocation/travel, competitive-bidding replacement, Final Rule 1713 F2F/WOPD, the Group I/II/III initial and continued-payment documentation criteria, repairs/replacement (RA modifier), the GA/GY/GZ/KX/N1-N3 and QA-QR modifier-selection logic, the E-code coding-guideline definitions, and coding verification review (CVR). **Additive extraction at S161** completing item 38: the article's codes (30 covered + 2 excluded HCPCS), 28 clinical concepts, 6 references, 14 modifiers, and the N3-anchored ICD-10 `PolicyGroup` were already in the graph from the prior partial pass and are untouched; only the policy-scope `gem:PolicyRule` individuals were added. **Closes eight deferred proposals** — `[5]` liter-flow, `[9]` RUL, `[10]` rental cap/payment-phase, `[11]` break-in-service, `[12]` competitive bidding, `[13]` M&S, `[14]` oxygen contents, `[17]` modifier-selection — all `approved`/`implemented` → `complete`. No new axis-2 rule_type values introduced.

### NCD 100.3 — 24-Hour Ambulatory Esophageal pH Monitoring

*Extracted S162 (2026-07-18). `gemi:ncd100.3_r1` – `_r2`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-18 (Session 162). 2 rules at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; no inline HCPCS/ICD codes and no Coding Information section — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (24-hour ambulatory esophageal pH monitoring / Diagnostic Tests (other)); domain axis omitted per convention. Fresh mint (not a promoted stub; Tom supplied the PDF and URL directly). **Version 1, ncdid=108, 2 pp, effective 1985-06-11 — no implementation date is posted, so none is asserted.** Single-version — the Other Versions table lists Version 1 alone (06/11/1985 – N/A, *"You are here"*) — so **no cross-version retention analysis applies**. 3 axis-2 `rule_type` values (3 `gem:ruleType` triples): service-definition (1), coverage-scope (1), eligibility (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit category: Diagnostic Tests (other) (reuse). 0 provider credentials — the policy names no actor. 7 clinical-concept links — **7 mints**, 0 reuses. 0 healthcare settings. 0 policy-to-policy references — the document cites nothing. No change requests.

**A two-sentence prose NCD in the NCD 20.8.1 mould.** The Item/Service Description defines the procedure (R1); the Indications and Limitations of Coverage sentence is the coverage gate (R2). There is no denial anywhere in the document, so no rule carries `non-coverage`.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | Item/Service Description: 24-hour ambulatory esophageal pH monitoring is a diagnostic procedure placing an indwelling electrode into the lower esophagus to determine the presence of gastric reflux and measure abnormal esophageal acid exposure | service-definition |
| R2 | Indications and Limitations of Coverage: covered for patients suspected of having gastric reflux, but only where the patient presents diagnostic problems associated with atypical symptoms, or symptoms are suggestive of reflux but conventional tests have not confirmed it | coverage-scope; eligibility |

#### Notes

- **B1 (*"conventional tests"* mints a concept — confirmed).** The coverage gate names *"conventional tests"* as the diagnostic modality whose non-confirmation is one of the two coverage triggers. Minted as `conceptConventionalTest` (singular-normalized). The existing `conceptConventionalTherapy` / `conceptConventionalTreatment` / `conceptConventionalCare` are a different noun and do not match under strict-prose, so the catalog-phrasings rule defaults to mint. **The alternative was to treat it as too generic to catalog** — rejected because it is load-bearing in the coverage condition and a provider note could carry the phrase. Tom confirmed mint.
- **B2 (*"atypical symptoms"* mints a concept — confirmed).** A clinical finding named in the coverage condition (*"diagnostic problems associated with atypical symptoms"*). Clinical under Option B and claim-readable — a provider note could carry it. Minted as `conceptAtypicalSymptoms`. Tom confirmed mint.
- **B3 (R1 service-definition kept, not dropped — confirmed).** SKILL.md corollary #2 drops a pure definitional sentence when its content is already carried on a named entity — and `conceptAmbulatoryEsophagealPhMonitoring` does carry the definition on its `gem:description`. But this NCD names no HCPCS code, so nothing external carries the procedure's identity, and the NCD 20.8.1 template keeps its service-coverage sentence as R1 even where concepts exist. **The alternative was to drop R1 and let the concept description hold the definition** — defensible, but it would leave the policy with a single rule and lose the source's own two-part structure (definition + gate). Tom confirmed keep.
- **The document title is not a concept mint site.** *"24-Hour Ambulatory Esophageal pH Monitoring"* names the policy and is carried on `gemi:ncd100.3`'s `gem:prefLabel`; the procedure concept `conceptAmbulatoryEsophagealPhMonitoring` mints from the operative Item/Service Description prose, not from the title (SKILL.md §*"A document title is not a section heading"*, the NCD 280.16 B8 precedent).
- **Drops.** The *"Please Note: This may not be an exhaustive list of all applicable Medicare benefit categories…"* line and the *"Links in PDF documents are not guaranteed to work…"* line are CMS-wide MCD boilerplate and are not extracted. There is no Coding Information section, no Revision History, and no Associated Documents list — the document is complete as read, and every absence is a confirmed empty section, not a gate.

Single IF/THEN — the identical text in V2 and V3 is one rule.
- **B2 (cross-version retention — V1 rules NOT retained; Decision A "minimal", Tom-confirmed).** Tom supplied V1 (effective 2005-03-15), V2 (2021-01-01) and V3 (2023-04-10). V1 carried substantial coverage content — abarelix (Plenaxis) as a palliative treatment in advanced symptomatic prostate cancer under an all-of gate (GnRH agonist therapy not appropriate; patient declines surgical castration; and one of neurological-compromise risk, ureteral/bladder-outlet obstruction, or severe bone pain from skeletal metastases persisting on narcotic analgesia), plus the FDA-labeling conditions (physician attestation, post-marketing risk-management-program enrollment, ability to diagnose/manage advanced prostate cancer and treat anaphylaxis, 30-minute observation). All of it is absent from V3. **None of it is retained:** V2 is an intervening version that explicitly documents *and* effects the removal (the "no NCD is appropriate at this time" restatement-with-changed-outcome — the NCD 270.1 §C shape), so under the SKILL.md §"Cross-version retention" framework V1's rules are not carried under either reading. Per the 180.2 / 240.2.2 B2 pattern the superseded content is change-log only, flagged here for the paused multi-version-management discussion, not modeled in the graph.
- **B3 (concepts — minimal, Tom-confirmed lean).** Only concepts the surviving V3 text names are minted/linked: `conceptAbarelix` (new; first abarelix concept in the corpus) and `conceptProstateCancer` (reuse — already minted, sourced to `ncd210.1`; reuse is the policy-side `refersToClinicalConcept` edge only, its single mint `dc:source` is untouched). The ~13 V1-only concepts (GnRH agonist/antagonist, leuprolide, goserelin, Plenaxis, clinical flare, the three palliative-indication findings, the physician-attestation conditions, anaphylaxis, etc.) are **not** minted — they belong to the superseded V1 content excluded under B2. The rejected alternative (mint the full V1 concept set) would populate the graph from retired, non-in-effect prose against the current-version-only posture.
- **B4 (transmittals / CR / NCA — minimal, Tom-confirmed lean).** Only what the live V3 Tracking Information surfaces is wired: **`tn11892NCD` reused** (already minted by NCD 240.2.2 at S134 and re-used by NCD 180.2 at S143) — added the reciprocal `revisesPolicy gemi:ncd110.19` (it now revises all three retired sections) and extended its description; NCD 110.19 links to it via `referencesPolicy`. **`cag00238N` newly minted** as an `NCAdocument` stub (`planPromote`, `isInEffect true`) — the "Original Consideration for Abarelix for the Treatment of Prostate Cancer (CAG-00238N)" named in V3's National Coverage Analyses section; its decision memo is dated 2005-03-15 and produced NCD 110.19's original coverage determination. **The V1/V2 deliverers are named in the policy description prose only and are not minted** — Transmittal 34 (CR 3775) and claims-processing Transmittal 612 delivered V1; Transmittal 10838 delivered V2 — consistent with current-version-only extraction and the S151 exclusion of superseded-version transmittal metadata (V3 surfaces neither, and has no Revision History). The rejected alternative (mint the full V1/V2 delivery chain) would create stubs for transmittals no in-effect field cites.
- **B5 (no benefit-category round-trip — contrast 180.2 B7).** All three versions carry the same two benefit categories (Incident to a physician's professional Service; Inpatient Hospital Services), so unlike NCD 180.2 (Prosthetic Devices → No Benefit Category → Prosthetic Devices) there is no round-trip to record; both categories are reuse.
- **CAG-00238N source URL.** Resolved by web search to the final (proposed=N) decision-memo rendition, `…/ncacal-decision-memo.aspx?proposed=N&ncaid=129`, matching the corpus NCA-stub convention (e.g. `cag00060N`).
- **Cross-reference / codes.** No inline HCPCS/ICD codes. No policy-to-policy cross-references beyond `tn11892NCD` and `cag00238N` — V3 cites no other NCD. `publicationNumber "100-3"`; `manualSectionNumber "110.19"`; `dc:source` = the user-supplied `…?ncdid=306&ncdver=3&`. No new axis-2 vocabulary. 3 benefit categories (all reuse). 5 provider credentials (1 mint — `credentialAuxiliaryPersonnel`; 4 reuse — physician, PA, NP, CNS). 0 clinical-concept mints (both `conceptAcupuncture` and `conceptChronicLowBackPain` reused). 14 policy references (`cag00452N` + 13 transmittals). Nationally Covered Indications — effective for services on/after 2020-01-21, acupuncture covered for cLBP; the cLBP 4-part definition (>=12 weeks, nonspecific, not surgery-associated, not pregnancy-associated) and the utilization limits (up to 12 visits in 90 days; +8 sessions on demonstrated improvement; <=20 treatments annually; discontinue if not improving/regressing) are captured verbatim in the single rule | coverage-scope, frequency |

Practitioners — who may furnish acupuncture: physicians (§1861(r)(1)); PAs, NPs/CNSs (§1861(aa)(5)), and auxiliary personnel meeting state requirements + ACAOM-accredited masters/doctoral degree + current unrestricted state acupuncture license; auxiliary personnel supervised per 42 CFR §§410.26/410.27 | credentialed-actor |

**Notes**
- **B1 (parent→child reference, Tom-confirmed lean).** NCD 30.3 V2's B/C sections point to "NCD section 30.3.3"; the parent now carries a one-way `gemi:ncd30.3 gem:referencesPolicy gemi:ncd30.3.3` (no reciprocal from 30.3.3), matching the sub-section reference convention used for `ncd240.2.1`/`.2.2` → `ncd240.2`. The stale sentence in `ncd30.3`'s description ("recorded on the worklist as pending, not minted") was corrected to record that 30.3.3 was minted and linked this session.
- **B2 (rule granularity — 4 rules; caps folded, Tom-confirmed lean).** The utilization caps (12/90d, +8, <=20/yr, discontinue-if-not-improving) are folded into the coverage rule R2 rather than split into a standalone rule. **Implementation note (differs from the plan-turn wording):** the plan floated capturing the caps as `gem:restrictionType` facets, but that mechanism is unavailable — `gem:restrictionType`'s `rdfs:domain` is the *deferred/unbuilt* `gem:CoverageRestriction` class, and no `gem:PolicyRule` in the corpus carries it. Per the verbatim-capture posture the caps are captured as prose inside R2's `ruleDescription`, and R2 is dual-typed `coverage-scope` + `frequency` to mark their utilization-limit nature. The rejected alternative (a separate `frequency` rule) is a defensible next-best reading but adds a rule boundary the single covered-indication section does not itself draw.
- **B3 (credentials — 1 mint + 4 reuse; requirements in rule prose, Tom-confirmed lean).** Physician, PA, NP, and CNS credential individuals already exist (physician `dc:source ncd280.1`; PA/NP/CNS `dc:source ncd210.1`) and are reused via the policy-side `requiresProviderCredential` edge only (their mint `dc:source` untouched). Only **`credentialAuxiliaryPersonnel`** is newly minted (`dc:source ncd30.3.3`). The furnishing requirements (ACAOM degree, unrestricted state license, 42 CFR supervision) are captured verbatim in R3's `ruleDescription`, not modeled as separate credential/qualification-group individuals (Option-A minimal; the corpus has no `gem:QualificationGroup` precedent for degree/license bundles here). The rejected alternative (mint a `credentialAcupuncturist` actor) would invent an actor the source does not name — the source lists the four statutory actor classes plus auxiliary personnel, all subject to the same license/degree gate.
- **B4 (dry needling not minted — Tom-confirmed lean).** "Dry needling" appears only inside R4's non-coverage clause ("all types of acupuncture including dry needling for any condition other than cLBP are non-covered"); it is captured verbatim in the rule and not minted as a clinical concept — it is a technique named to scope the exclusion, carrying no coding hook, and no covered indication references it.
- **B5 (transmittal edges — `tn10128NCD revisesPolicy ncd30.3.3`, per the plan-turn lean and the S151 rule).** TN 10128 (Pub. 100-03) *created* NCD 30.3.3, and under the S151 transmittal-edge rule a transmittal that CREATES a section takes `gem:revisesPolicy` ("New" is a Change; the pre-S151 "a first version has nothing to revise" reading is explicitly retired — SKILL.md §Transmittals). So `tn10128NCD gem:revisesPolicy gemi:ncd30.3.3` is asserted (added to the existing `tn10128NCD` block, which now revises both `ncd30.3` and `ncd30.3.3`), reciprocated by `ncd30.3.3 gem:referencesPolicy gemi:tn10128NCD`. The remaining transmittals — the quarterly ICD-10 maintenance updates that state no policy change, and the Pub. 100-04 claims-processing renditions (`tn768CP` precedent) — carry no `revisesPolicy`-to-policy edge and are linked by the policy's `referencesPolicy` only, matching the `ncd160.18` revision-history pattern; `revisesPolicy` is otherwise reserved for the rescind-replace chains between transmittal stubs. *Process note: mid-build I briefly drifted toward a uniform-`referencesPolicy` reading on the "first version" rationale; SKILL.md §Transmittals shows that is the retired reading, so the plan-turn lean stands — B5 is confirmed as leaned, not adjusted.*
- **Transmittal / CR inventory (S131 mint-every-referenced-policy).** 8 new transmittal stubs (`tn10817NCD`, `tn11068NCD`, `tn11179NCD`, `tn11545NCD`, `tn11584NCD`, `tn12903NCD` — Pub. 100-03 ICD-10 maintenance; `tn10337CP`, `tn12185CP` — Pub. 100-04 claims-processing), 4 new CR stubs (`cr12279`, `cr12480`, `cr12822`, `cr13818`), 1 new NCA stub (`cag00452N`). 5 existing transmittals referenced: `tn10128CP`, `tn11264NCD`, `tn11342NCD`, `tn11391NCD` referenced without edit; `tn10128NCD` gained a `gem:revisesPolicy gemi:ncd30.3.3` edge (B5). Rescind-replace chains wired between transmittal stubs: `tn11179NCD revisesPolicy tn11068NCD` (CR 12480), `tn11584NCD revisesPolicy tn11545NCD` (CR 12822), `tn10337CP revisesPolicy tn10128CP` (deny-claims BR change to CR 11755). Every delivering transmittal asserts `transmitsChangeRequest`; shared CRs accumulate inbound edges (CR 11755 now has three deliverers — `tn10128NCD`/`tn10128CP`/`tn10337CP` — its `dc:source` unchanged at `tn10128NCD`); each CR's `dc:source` is its in-effect delivering transmittal. All maintenance transmittal URLs are Source-URL-pending (the 30.3.3 page links only R10128NCD); `tn12185CP`'s delivering CR is not stated on the page, so it carries no `transmitsChangeRequest`.

**Notes**
- **B1 (R2 rule type — `non-coverage` only, Tom-confirmed lean).** R2's "within the meaning of §1862(a)(1) of the Social Security Act" is read as the standard non-coverage phrasing rather than a scope-defining statutory reference, so R2 carries `ruleType_nonCoverage` alone. The rejected alternative (add `statutory-framing`) fails the S81 B2 test — the statute is the boilerplate reasonable-and-necessary hook, not the syntactic subject or the framework being applied to a determination.
- **B2 (transmittal edges, Tom-confirmed lean).** Three transmittals named across the two versions, all wired under the S131 mint-every-referenced-policy rule. **`tn11NCD`** (Pub. 100-03 NCD-Manual rendition R11NCD) is Version 1's Transmittal Information entry — it established the 2004-04-16 non-coverage — so it takes `gem:revisesPolicy gemi:ncd30.3.1` ("New"/establishing is a Change under the S151 transmittal-edge rule) and delivered CR 3250; minted as a new `planPromote` stub. **`tn10128NCD`** (Pub. 100-03 R10128NCD) is Version 2's Transmittal Information entry; it bumped 30.3.1 to Version 2 (adding the A. General definition and the A/B/C/D restructure — a Change), so it **gains** a `gem:revisesPolicy gemi:ncd30.3.1` edge (its existing block now revises `ncd30.3`, `ncd30.3.1`, and `ncd30.3.3`). **`tn10128CP`** (Pub. 100-04 claims-processing rendition) is named in Claims Processing Instructions and **gains** a `gem:referencesPolicy gemi:ncd30.3.1` edge (the `tn768CP` precedent). All three reciprocate via `ncd30.3.1 gem:referencesPolicy`. The rejected alternative for `tn10128NCD` (`referencesPolicy` only, on the view that the fibromyalgia *substance* did not change) understates that the transmittal restructured the section and added a definitional rule.
- **Cross-version retention (V1 → V2 — nothing retained).** The V1 non-coverage rule is a **restatement**, so Version 2's text governs (one rule, not two; the S151 "restatement is not an absence" rule). V1's "General" section is the 1980 initial-noncoverage historical narrative — **non-rule background** (fails the "what belongs as a rule" test), and its only concepts (acupuncture, fibromyalgia) are already carried, so no concept is stranded. No silent drop requires retention and no revision history reports a change to the fibromyalgia disposition. Result: **nothing retained**, paralleling NCD 270.1's outcome. The 05/2020 Revision-History entry on this page (cover acupuncture for cLBP; TN 10128 / CR 11755) is the **parent NCD 30.3** coverage change swept onto this sub-section's page; it effects no change to 30.3.1 and mints no rule here (CR 11755 stays wired to the parent via the existing `tn10128NCD`/`tn10128CP` deliverers, untouched).
- **Transmittal / CR inventory (S131).** 1 new transmittal stub (`tn11NCD`, Pub. 100-03) + 1 new CR stub (`cr3250`, delivered by `tn11NCD`, its single in-effect deliverer). 3 existing individuals edited: `tn10128NCD` (+`revisesPolicy ncd30.3.1`), `tn10128CP` (+`referencesPolicy ncd30.3.1`), and `cag00174N` reused unchanged (this NCD's own originating NCA — Original Consideration for Acupuncture for Fibromyalgia). `tn11NCD`'s `dc:source` (R11NCD) was de-mangled from the Version 1 page's PDF line-break artifact (`Regulations-andGuidance` → `Regulations-and-Guidance`) to the canonical CMS transmittal URL (per the S152 PDF-artifact de-wrapping convention).
- **Cross-reference / codes.** No inline HCPCS/ICD codes (no CPT mint needed). `publicationNumber "100-3"`; `manualSectionNumber "30.3.1"`; `dc:source` = the user-supplied `…?ncdid=283&ncdver=2&`. Version 2, effective 2020-01-21, implementation 2020-06-24; 3 pp. (Edit-log bullet omitted, matching the S164/S165 acupuncture-section precedent; item 20 leaves the Edit-log line unchecked and owed.)

- **B1 (R2 rule type — `non-coverage` only).** R2's "within the meaning of §1862(a)(1) of the Social Security Act" is read as the standard non-coverage phrasing rather than a scope-defining statutory reference, so R2 carries `ruleType_nonCoverage` alone — the same call as NCD 30.3.1 R2 (S174 B1) and the standard reasonable-and-necessary hook.
- **B2 (transmittal edges).** Three transmittals named across the two versions, all wired under the S131 mint-every-referenced-policy rule — **all three already exist in the graph** (minted/carried by the 30.3 / 30.3.1 / 30.3.3 extractions), so this pass mints no new transmittal or CR stub. **`tn11NCD`** (Pub. 100-03 R11NCD) is Version 1's Transmittal Information entry — it established the 2004-04-16 non-coverage — so it **gains** `gem:revisesPolicy gemi:ncd30.3.2` (its block now revises both `ncd30.3.1` and `ncd30.3.2`) and its already-present CR 3250 covers this delivery. **`tn10128NCD`** (Pub. 100-03 R10128NCD) is Version 2's Transmittal Information entry; it bumped 30.3.2 to Version 2 (adding the A. General definition and the A/B/C/D restructure — a Change), so it **gains** `gem:revisesPolicy gemi:ncd30.3.2` (its block now revises `ncd30.3`, `ncd30.3.1`, `ncd30.3.2`, `ncd30.3.3`). **`tn10128CP`** (Pub. 100-04 claims-processing rendition) is named in Claims Processing Instructions and **gains** `gem:referencesPolicy gemi:ncd30.3.2` (the `tn768CP` precedent). All three reciprocate via `ncd30.3.2 gem:referencesPolicy`.
- **Cross-version retention (V1 → V2 — nothing retained).** The V1 non-coverage rule is a **restatement**, so Version 2's text governs (one rule, not two; the S151 "restatement is not an absence" rule). V1's "General" section is the 1980 initial-noncoverage historical narrative — **non-rule background** (fails the "what belongs as a rule" test), and its only concepts (acupuncture, osteoarthritis) are already carried, so no concept is stranded. No silent drop requires retention and no revision history reports a change to the osteoarthritis disposition. Result: **nothing retained**, paralleling NCD 30.3.1 and NCD 270.1. The 05/2020 Revision-History entry on this page (cover acupuncture for cLBP; TN 10128 / CR 11755) is the **parent NCD 30.3** coverage change swept onto this sub-section's page; it effects no change to 30.3.2 and mints no rule here (CR 11755 stays wired to the parent via the existing `tn10128NCD`/`tn10128CP` deliverers, untouched).
- **Transmittal / CR inventory (S131).** 0 new transmittal stubs, 0 new CR stubs — every referenced document already exists. 3 existing individuals edited: `tn11NCD` (+`revisesPolicy ncd30.3.2`), `tn10128NCD` (+`revisesPolicy ncd30.3.2`), `tn10128CP` (+`referencesPolicy ncd30.3.2`). `cag00175N` reused unchanged (this NCD's own originating NCA — Original Consideration for Acupuncture for Osteoarthritis, already in the graph from the NCD 30.3 extraction). `cr3250` reused unchanged (its first-mint description names 30.3.1; left as-is per the shared-node first-mint-provenance convention, Tom-confirmed at the Plan turn).
- **Cross-reference / codes.** No inline HCPCS/ICD codes (no CPT mint needed). `publicationNumber "100-3"`; `manualSectionNumber "30.3.2"`; `dc:source` = the user-supplied `…?ncdid=284&ncdver=2&`. Version 2, effective 2020-01-21, implementation 2020-06-24; 3 pp. (Edit-log bullet omitted, matching the S164/S165/S174 acupuncture-section precedent; item 20 leaves the Edit-log line unchecked and owed.)

**Notes**

### NCD 110.3 — Anti-Inhibitor Coagulant Complex (AICC)

No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit category: Blood Clotting Factors for Hemophilia Patients (reuse). No provider credential, healthcare setting, or qualification group. 4 clinical-concept mints, 0 reuse. | Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | §Indications and Limitations: AICC has Medicare coverage when furnished to patients with hemophilia A and inhibitor antibodies to factor VIII who have major bleeding episodes and who fail to respond to other, less expensive therapies (coverage grant + patient-qualifying criteria) | coverage-scope, eligibility |

**Notes**
- **B1 (rule typing — coverage-scope + eligibility).** The single coverage sentence bundles the coverage grant (what is covered: AICC) and the full patient-qualification (who qualifies: hemophilia A, factor VIII inhibitor antibodies, major bleeding episodes, and failure of other less-expensive therapies) in one rule, with no separate criteria rules to carry the "who." Both types therefore ride on R1 — the VNS `ncd240.2`-family R3 / STI-screening / lymphedema-CVI eligibility pattern for "covered for patients with [clinical criteria]." *Contrast* the scope-only grants (e.g. `ncd240.2_r1`, "covered ... when the patient exhibits hypoxemia as defined below") that defer their criteria to standalone eligibility rules. The safe-and-effective efficacy characterization is background carried on `conceptAICC`, not a separate `serviceStandard` rule.
- **B2 (concepts — 4 mints; Option-B inclusive).** Mint `conceptAICC` (the drug; acronym URI per the `conceptALS` / `conceptCOPD` precedent; no HCPCS code in the rendition, so a `ClinicalConcept`, not a coded item), `conceptHemophiliaA`, `conceptFactorVIIIInhibitorAntibodies`, `conceptMajorBleedingEpisode`. **Not minted:** generic "hemophilia" (sentence-1 background; the rule-relevant form is "hemophilia A", which subsumes it — not minted as a separate umbrella, Tom's S181 call); "other, less expensive therapies" (a comparative/economic catch-all naming no clinical entity — the prior-therapy-failure requirement lives in R1's text).
- **B3 (effective date — Other-Versions fallback).** The Tracking Information posts no effective date ("This is a longstanding national coverage determination. The effective date of this version has not been posted."); 1966-01-01 is taken from the Other Versions effective-between column (01/01/1966 - N/A, "You are here") — the same Other-Versions fallback applied to NCD 270.4, 280.2, 30.1, 240.3 and 270.5. Single-version policy, so the S151 cross-version retention rule has no transition to walk.
- **B4 (no lineage).** The rendition carries no Transmittal Information, Revision History, Cross Reference, Claims Processing Instructions or NCA section, and names no other policy — so no transmittal/CR/NCA stubs are minted and nothing is added to or removed from the worklist for references. The policy was not a prior stub.

- **B2 (two parallel rules — IF/THEN heuristic).** The single coverage paragraph yields two IF/THENs on the route axis: sublingual → deny (R1), injection → cover (R2). *Extracted S185 (2026-07-21). `gemi:ncd110.14_r1` – `gemi:ncd110.14_r18`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-21 (Session 185). 18 rules at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; no inline HCPCS/ICD codes — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (apheresis / therapeutic pheresis); domain axis omitted per convention. `gemi:ncd110.14` minted fresh (not a prior stub) as the live **Version 1** (single-version, in effect). Axis-2 `rule_type` values used across the 18 rules: coverage-scope (16), service-definition (1), eligibility (6), setting-definition (1), credentialed-actor (3) — 26 `gem:ruleType` triples. No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit categories: Incident to a physician's professional Service, Outpatient Hospital Services Incident to a Physician's Service, Physicians' Services (all reuse). 1 provider credential (`credentialPhysician`, reuse). 4 healthcare-setting links (`settingHospital`, `settingInpatientHospital`, `settingOutpatientHospital` reuse; `settingPhysicianDirectedClinic` newly minted, ⊂ `settingClinic`). 31 clinical-concept links (28 mints, 3 reuse). 2 policy references (the delivering-transmittal stubs `tn59CIM` and `tn4CIM`), plus their `revisesPolicy` reciprocal edges.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | §A General: for Medicare coverage, apheresis is defined as an autologous procedure (blood taken, processed, and returned as a continuous procedure), as distinguished from preoperative donation — a coverage-scoping definition | coverage-scope, service-definition |
| R2 | §B Indications: plasma exchange for acquired myasthenia gravis | coverage-scope |
| R3 | §B: leukapheresis in the treatment of leukemia | coverage-scope |
| R4 | §B: plasmapheresis in the treatment of primary macroglobulinemia (Waldenstrom) | coverage-scope |
| R5 | §B: treatment of hyperglobulinemias, including (but not limited to) multiple myelomas, cryoglobulinemia and hyperviscosity syndromes | coverage-scope |
| R6 | §B: plasmapheresis or plasma exchange as a last resort treatment of thromobotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) *(source misspelling retained)* | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R7 | §B: plasmapheresis or plasma exchange in the last resort treatment of life threatening rheumatoid vasculitis | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R8 | §B: plasma perfusion of charcoal filters for treatment of pruritis of cholestatic liver disease *(source misspelling retained)* | coverage-scope |
| R9 | §B: plasma exchange in the treatment of Goodpasture's Syndrome | coverage-scope |
| R10 | §B: plasma exchange for glomerulonephritis associated with antiglomerular basement membrane antibodies and advancing renal failure or pulmonary hemorrhage | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R11 | §B: chronic relapsing polyneuropathy for patients with severe or life threatening symptoms who have failed to respond to conventional therapy | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R12 | §B: life threatening scleroderma and polymyositis when the patient is unresponsive to conventional therapy | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R13 | §B: Guillain-Barre Syndrome | coverage-scope |
| R14 | §B: treatment of last resort for life threatening systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) when conventional therapy has failed to prevent clinical deterioration | coverage-scope, eligibility |
| R15 | §C Settings: apheresis covered only in a hospital setting (inpatient or outpatient) or a nonhospital setting (e.g., a physician directed clinic) meeting the following conditions | coverage-scope, setting-definition |
| R16 | §C: a physician (or a number of physicians) is present to perform medical services and to respond to medical emergencies at all times during patient care hours | credentialed-actor |
| R17 | §C: each patient is under the care of a physician | credentialed-actor |
| R18 | §C: all nonphysician services are furnished under the direct, personal supervision of a physician | credentialed-actor |

**Notes**
- **B1 (§A autologous scope kept as a rule — Tom-confirmed).** R1 captures §A's "For purposes of Medicare coverage, apheresis is defined as an autologous procedure …" as a coverage-scope + service-definition rule: it bounds coverage (excludes the preoperative-donation procedure) rather than merely describing the service. The first descriptive sentence (the mechanism of apheresis) is carried on `conceptApheresis`'s `gem:description` under corollary #2, not as a rule. *Alt considered:* 0 §A rules, all definitional content on the concepts — rejected because the autologous constraint is a coverage boundary an evaluator applies, not pure term-matching.
- **B2 (§B granularity — 13 rules; Tom-confirmed).** The §B "Apheresis is covered for the following indications:" list yields one IF/THEN per indication (13 parallel alternative paths to a shared coverage outcome; several carry distinct embedded gates — last resort, life threatening, conventional-therapy failure). Captured as 13 Pattern-2 rules (R2–R14) with the lead-in repeated as a natural-prose prefix; the non-exhaustive "including (but not limited to)" sub-list stays folded inside R5's verbatim string. *Alt considered:* one folded rule — defensible but loses the per-indication IF/THEN granularity the heuristic counts; the NCD 240.2 B4 alternative-qualifying-paths precedent favors the split.
- **B3 (§C granularity — 4 rules; Tom-confirmed).** R15 = the setting-scope gate (coverage-scope + setting-definition); R16–R18 = the three physician conditions gating the nonhospital setting, captured Pattern-2 (heading repeated) as credentialed-actor. The three conditions are three distinct evaluator checks under one heading. *Alt considered:* fold the gate and conditions into one Pattern-3 rule — rejected for the same IF/THEN reason.
- **B4 (concepts — 28 mints + 3 reuse; Option-B inclusive, Tom-confirmed).** Reuse `conceptPolymyositis`, `conceptGuillainBarreSyndrome`, `conceptConventionalTherapy` (exact prefLabel match). "acquired myasthenia gravis" and "chronic relapsing polyneuropathy" mint fresh rather than reusing the bare `conceptMyastheniaGravis` / `conceptPolyneuropathy` — a word added is a mint under catalog-phrasings. The blood constituents (plasma, leukocyte, platelet, whole blood) and the glomerulonephritis-clause entities (antiglomerular basement membrane antibodies, renal failure, pulmonary hemorrhage) are captured; bare "cells" is dropped as generic. The aliases "pheresis" / "therapeutic pheresis" are recorded on `conceptApheresis`'s description, not minted separately (the latter is also the document title, not a mint site — S158). Singular normalization applied to hyperglobulinemia, hyperviscosity syndrome, multiple myeloma, and leukocyte.
- **B5 (settings — institution reach by entailment; Tom-confirmed).** Named places: hospital, inpatient hospital, outpatient hospital (reuse) + physician directed clinic (new, ⊂ `settingClinic`). The source's "hospital … or … nonhospital setting, e.g., a physician directed clinic" ≡ any institutional setting: this is delivered by **entailment**, since `settingHospital` and `settingClinic` both sit under `settingInstitution`, so a query on `settingInstitution` reaches this policy. No standalone `settingNonhospital` negation and no direct `settingInstitution` link are asserted; the physician requirement is the operative gate (`credentialPhysician` + R16–R18). *Alts considered and rejected:* mint `settingNonhospital` (a negation is not a positively-assertable place a provider note carries) and/or assert `settingInstitution` directly (would over-claim SNF/hospice the source never names).
- **B6 (transmittal lineage — S151 edge rule, CIM era gate; Tom-confirmed).** Two transmittals, both CIM (HCFA Pub. 6), `publicationNumber "6"`, `gem:planPromote`, source URL pending: `tn59CIM` (07/1992, the Version 1 deliverer) and `tn4CIM` (02/1986, the earlier indication-adding transmittal). Each describes the change it made to this policy, so each takes `revisesPolicy` → `ncd110.14` (`tn4CIM` as superseded-revision lineage, `check_proposal_b` Category E); the policy asserts the reciprocal agnostic `referencesPolicy` to both (mint-every-referenced-policy, S131). Era gate: 07/1992 and 02/1986 both predate Pub. 100-03/100-04/100-20 (and 1986 predates the CR system) → CIM; `tn59CIM` fits the CIM monotonic dated series (TN 57 → 59 → 60) and `tn4CIM` is the earliest CIM in the corpus. Predates the CMS Change Request system → no CR.
- **B7 (source misspellings — S152 unconditional; Tom-confirmed).** Three source errors corrected in the concept prefLabels/URIs and retained verbatim in the source-facing text: "plataelets" (§A) → `conceptPlatelet` (variant recorded on its `gem:workflowDescription`, as §A prose is carried in summary on `conceptApheresis`); "thromobotic" (§B) → `conceptThromboticThrombocytopenicPurpura`, verbatim kept in `ncd110.14_r6`; "pruritis" (§B) → `conceptPruritusOfCholestaticLiverDisease`, verbatim kept in `ncd110.14_r8`.
- **B8 (single version — no cross-version walk).** Other Versions lists Version 1 only (07/30/1992 - N/A, "You are here"), so the S151 cross-version retention rule has no transition to test. TN 4's 1986 additions predate the MCD version series (which begins at V1 = 1992) and are captured only as `tn4CIM`'s revision-lineage, not as a separate GEM version.
- **Source / boundary.** Canonical source is `…?ncdid=82&ncdver=1` (Tom-supplied). `publicationNumber "100-3"`; `manualSectionNumber "110.14"`. Version 1, effective 1992-07-30; no implementation date posted; 3 pp; benefit categories Incident to a physician's professional Service, Outpatient Hospital Services Incident to a Physician's Service, Physicians' Services (all reuse). `policies_processed` 89 —> 90. ### NCD 110.18 — Aprepitant for Chemotherapy-Induced Emesis

*Extracted S186 (2026-07-21). `gemi:ncd110.18_r1` – `gemi:ncd110.18_r8`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-21 (Session 186). 8 rules at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; no inline HCPCS/ICD codes — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (aprepitant antiemetic regimen for chemotherapy-induced emesis); domain axis omitted per convention. `gemi:ncd110.18` minted fresh (not a prior stub) as the in-effect **Version 2** (effective 2013-05-29); Version 1 (effective 2005-04-04) is documented, not minted as a separate individual, per the single-in-effect-version convention. Axis-2 `rule_type` values across the 8 rules: coverage-scope (4: R2, R3, R4, R8), definition (1: R1), non-coverage (3: R5, R6, R7) — 8 `gem:ruleType` triples, one per rule. No new axis-2 vocabulary. `gemi:ncd110.18_r8` additionally carries `gem:delegatesCoverageTo gemi:credentialMedicareAdministrativeContractor` (the Section D MAC-discretion delegation), matching the NCD 180.2 / NCD 200.2 delegation pattern; no policy-level `requiresProviderCredential`. Benefit category: Oral Anti-Emetic Drugs (reuse). No healthcare-setting links. 28 clinical-concept links (26 mints, 2 reuse: `conceptIrinotecan`, `conceptOxaliplatin`). 40 policy references (38 transmittals + 2 NCAs); Change Requests are linked from their delivering transmittals, not from the policy.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | §A General: CMS defines highly / moderately emetogenic chemotherapy as agents so designated in at least two of the three NCCN / ASCO / ESMO-MASCC guidelines | definition |
| R2 | §B: on/after 2013-05-29, the oral three-drug regimen (oral aprepitant + oral 5HT antagonist + oral dexamethasone) is reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries receiving any of 20 named anticancer chemotherapeutic agents | coverage-scope |
| R3 | §B: between 2005-04-04 and 2013-05-28, the oral antiemetic three-drug combination is reasonable and necessary only for patients receiving one or more of 9 named agents (date-bounded historical leg) | coverage-scope |
| R4 | §B: the oral three-drug regimen must be administered immediately before and within 48 hours after the chemotherapeutic agents | coverage-scope |
| R5 | §C: aprepitant cannot function alone as a full replacement for intravenously administered antiemetic agents for patients receiving highly and/or moderately emetogenic chemotherapy | non-coverage |
| R6 | §C: Medicare does not cover under Part B oral antiemetic drugs in combination regimens administered in part via an oral route and in part via an intravenous route | non-coverage |
| R7 | §C: Medicare does not cover under Part B aprepitant when it is used alone for anticancer-chemotherapy-related nausea and vomiting | non-coverage |
| R8 | §D: MACs may determine coverage for other all-oral three-drug regimens of aprepitant or any other FDA-approved oral NK-1 antagonist with an oral 5HT antagonist and oral dexamethasone, for the listed or other FDA-approved highly/moderately emetogenic agents | coverage-scope |

**Notes**
- **B1 (§B historical 9-agent leg kept as one date-bounded rule — Tom-confirmed, D1).** Version 2's §B restates the Version 1 coverage as a closed 2005-04-04 → 2013-05-28 window over nine agents. R3 captures it as a single coverage-scope rule with the date window verbatim in the rule text. This documents the historical leg explicitly rather than dropping it; because the in-effect V2 rendition self-documents the window, no cross-version silent-deletion finding arises. *Alt considered:* omit the historical leg as superseded — rejected because V2 states it verbatim and source-fidelity keeps it.
- **B2 (§B current 20-agent list folds to one rule — Tom-confirmed, D2).** The on/after-2013-05-29 coverage over twenty agents is one coverage-scope rule (R2); the agent list is an eligibility gate a downstream evaluator reads as a set-membership test, not twenty parallel IF/THEN rules. *Alt considered:* one rule per agent (20 rules) — rejected under the IF/THEN heuristic: a single "IF the beneficiary is receiving any of {list}" statement generates one evaluator branch, not twenty.
- **B3 (§A emetogenicity definition as one rule — Tom-confirmed, D3).** R1 captures §A's classification of highly / moderately emetogenic chemotherapy (designation in ≥ 2 of the 3 NCCN / ASCO / ESMO-MASCC guidelines) as a single `ruleType_definition` rule — it defines terms the coverage rules use rather than granting or denying coverage itself. The three guideline bodies stay in R1's verbatim text and are **not** minted as clinical concepts (they are standards organizations, not clinical entities — parallels the non-mint of the Joint Commission in NCD 240.1).
- **B4 (§D MAC delegation — R8 delegatesCoverageTo).** §D lets MACs determine coverage for other all-oral NK-1-antagonist regimens. R8 is typed coverage-scope and carries `gem:delegatesCoverageTo gemi:credentialMedicareAdministrativeContractor`, following the NCD 180.2 / NCD 200.2 pattern where the delegation hangs off the rule and no policy-level `requiresProviderCredential` is asserted.
- **B5 (concepts — 26 mints + 2 reuse; Option-B inclusive, Tom-confirmed).** The 20-agent list is captured as 20 individual agent concepts (18 mints; reuse `conceptIrinotecan`, `conceptOxaliplatin` by exact prefLabel match) so a claim naming any agent surfaces this policy. ### NCD 150.9 — Arthroscopic Lavage and Arthroscopic Debridement for the Osteoarthritic Knee

*Extracted S187 (2026-07-21). `gemi:ncd150.9_r1` – `gemi:ncd150.9_r7`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-21 (Session 187). 7 rules at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; the policy names no ICD-10, HCPCS or CPT codes at all). Single-domain policy (arthroscopic lavage / debridement of the osteoarthritic knee); domain axis omitted per convention. `gemi:ncd150.9` minted fresh (never worklisted, no prior stub) as **Version 1** — the Other Versions table lists Version 1 only (06/11/2004 – N/A, "You are here"), so the cross-version retention rule has no second version to test and no silent-deletion audit applies. Axis-2 `rule_type` values across the 7 rules: definition (3: R1, R2, R5), non-coverage (3: R3, R4, R5), coverage-scope (1: R6), credentialed-actor (1: R6), documentation (1: R7) — 9 `gem:ruleType` triples over 7 rules (R5 and R6 each carry two). No new axis-2 vocabulary. `gemi:ncd150.9_r6` additionally carries `gem:delegatesCoverageTo gemi:credentialLocalContractor`; no policy-level `requiresProviderCredential`. Benefit categories (all reuse): Incident to a physician's professional Service; Inpatient Hospital Services; Physicians' Services. No healthcare-setting links. 42 clinical-concept links (40 mints, 2 reuse: `conceptOsteoarthritis`, `conceptPain`). 2 policy references (TN 14, CAG-00167N); CR 3281 is linked from its delivering transmittal, not from the policy.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | Item/Service Description: debridement, when used alone or not otherwise specified, may include low volume lavage or washout | service-definition |
| R2 | Item/Service Description: the American College of Rheumatology's definition of a patient diagnosis of osteoarthritis of the knee — presenting with pain and meeting at least 5 of 9 enumerated criteria | definition |
| R3 | §B: arthroscopic lavage used alone for the osteoarthritic knee is not reasonable or necessary and is not covered | non-coverage |
| R4 | §B: arthroscopic debridement for osteoarthritic patients presenting with knee pain only is not reasonable or necessary and is not covered | non-coverage |
| R5 | §B: arthroscopic debridement and lavage with or without debridement for patients presenting with severe osteoarthritis is not covered, with severe osteoarthritis defined through the Outerbridge classification scale (grades III and IV) | non-coverage, definition |
| R6 | §C: all other indications of debridement, for the subpopulation of patients without severe osteoarthritis of the knee presenting with symptoms other than pain alone — (1) mechanical symptoms, (2) limb and knee joint alignment, (3) less severe and/or early degenerative arthritis — remain at local contractor discretion | coverage-scope, credentialed-actor |
| R7 | §C: Medicare contractors may require operative notes, reports of standing x-rays, or arthroscopy results to define the patient's knee condition | documentation |

**Notes**

- **B1 (debridement-scope sentence captured, not dropped — Tom-confirmed).** *"Debridement, when used alone or not otherwise specified, may include low volume lavage or washout."* is captured as R1 (`service-definition`) rather than dropped under corollary #2. It is not a bare definition of debridement: it decides whether a debridement claim that included low-volume lavage falls under R3's noncovered *"lavage used alone"* leg, so it drives an evaluator decision and corollary #2 does not reach it. *Alt considered:* drop as descriptive, content carried on `gemi:conceptDebridement` — defensible on a reading of the sentence as pure item/service description, but it would strand the one clause that separates R1's scope from R3's.
- **B2 (ACR 5-of-9 diagnosis definition as one folded rule — Tom-confirmed).** R2 captures the American College of Rheumatology definition and its nine criteria as a single Pattern-3 rule with the list folded. Parallel to NCD 110.18's B3: the naming guideline body (ACR) stays inside the rule text and is **not** minted as an individual (a standards organization, not a clinical entity), and the five-of-nine threshold is the countable test the §B denials depend on — which is why the content is not left to `gemi:conceptOsteoarthritisOfTheKnee` under corollary #2. *Alt considered:* drop under corollary #2 — rejected because a description on the concept cannot carry an operative counting threshold.
- **B3 (Pattern-2 prefix scope for the three §B bullets — Tom-confirmed).** R3–R5 each carry the section heading **plus** the whole *"After thorough discussions … are not covered by the Medicare program:"* framing sentence as their prefix. The three bullets are sentence fragments with no verb of their own, so the heading-only form used at NCD 270.1 — where each bullet was a complete sentence — would leave them uninterpretable as rules. *Alt considered:* heading-only prefix (`B. Nationally Noncovered Indications:`), rejected on that ground; the cost of the choice is ~60 words of framing repeated three times.
- **B4 (Outerbridge definition folded into R5, not split — Tom-confirmed).** The seven-sentence Outerbridge block defining severe osteoarthritis sits inside bullet 3's own parenthesis and spans the page 2 / page 3 break in the rendition. It is folded into R5's verbatim string, and R5 carries `definition` as a second `gem:ruleType` to record the definitional content. *Alt considered:* a separate `definition` rule for the Outerbridge block with R5 keeping only the bullet clause — rejected because it would cut a single source sentence in half.
- **B5 (`delegatesCoverageTo` target — `credentialLocalContractor` minted; Tom-confirmed).** §C's *"remain at local contractor discretion"* is a contractor-discretion disposition under S167, so R6 carries `gem:delegatesCoverageTo`. The 2004 text predates the Medicare Administrative Contractor and never uses the term, so the S167/S168 delegatee `gemi:credentialMedicareAdministrativeContractor` — used in all 15 other delegation rules, every one of whose sources names the MAC — was **not** reused. `gemi:credentialLocalContractor` is minted at this policy's own source phrase under verbatim source-phrase routing. *Alts considered:* reuse `gemi:credentialMedicareContractor` (prefLabel "Medicare contractor" — the phrase §C's *next* sentence uses, a plurality-only match, same actor), or reuse `credentialMedicareAdministrativeContractor` for corpus consistency. Both are consolidations by meaning rather than by phrasing; equivalence among the three individuals is an SME assertion (`skos:closeMatch` / `skos:exactMatch`) left for the taxonomy pass. No policy-level `requiresProviderCredential`: a contractor is not a performer of the service (the NCD 110.18 / 180.2 / 200.2 pattern).
- **B6 (plural normalization — Tom-confirmed).** `conceptMechanicalSymptom`, `conceptLooseBody` and `conceptSynovialFluidSign` are singular-normalized from the source's *"mechanical symptoms"*, *"loose bodies"* and *"Synovial fluid signs"* per the S43 rule; no URI collision arose, so no plurality-only reuse was triggered. Noted because the first and third read oddly as singulars and the graph carries pre-rule plural individuals (e.g. `conceptAtypicalSymptoms`) that were not retroactively renamed. *Alt considered:* keep inherently-plural terms of art plural — rejected as an exception the S43 rule does not carry.
- **B7 (disjunctive findings split — Tom-confirmed).** Outerbridge Grade I's *"softening or blistering of joint cartilage"* yields `conceptSofteningOfJointCartilage` + `conceptBlisteringOfJointCartilage`, and Grades II–III's *"cartilage fragmentation or fissuring"* yields `conceptCartilageFragmentation` + `conceptCartilageFissuring`. Each member is independently observable and a provider note may name only one, which is the single-term-linkage rationale for separate individuals. *Alt considered:* capture each disjunction whole as one composite — rejected because the composite is a disjunction, not a compound concept carrying meaning beyond its parts (contrast "nocturnal oxygen desaturation").
- **B8 (`conceptJointDisease` minted — Tom-confirmed).** *"Osteoarthritis is a chronic and painful joint disease caused by degeneration."* names the genus, which is minted under the Option-B inclusive stance. *Alt considered:* drop as definitional-genus noise — rejected; Option B errs toward inclusion and the downstream medical review prunes.
- **Drops.** §A *"Nationally Covered Indications — Not applicable."* is a null section and yields no rule (the NCD 280.14 §D precedent). The §B lead sentence (*"The clinical effectiveness … has not been verified by scientifically controlled studies."*) is rationale for the determination, not an evaluator criterion. The arthroscopy, lavage and loose-body definitional sentences of the Item/Service Description are dropped under corollary #2 — their content is carried on `conceptArthroscopy`, `conceptLavage`, `conceptIrrigation`, `conceptLooseBody` and `conceptDebridement`. *"(This NCD last reviewed June 2004.)"* is an administrative annotation. Excluded from the concept set as document or administrative vocabulary: operative notes, arthroscopy results, "the patient's knee condition"; and "Over 50 years of age" as a demographic criterion rather than a clinical concept. "Clinical investigators" and "the orthopedic community" appear only as consultees in CMS's own deliberative process, not as performers of a required step, so neither is minted as a provider credential.
- **References (S131 mint-every-referenced-policy).** TN 14 (Transmittal Information field and Revision History), CR 3281 (Revision History) and CAG-00167N (National Coverage Analyses) — all three minted as `planPromote` stubs. The policy asserts `gem:referencesPolicy` to TN 14 and CAG-00167N; the CR is linked from its delivering transmittal via `gem:transmitsChangeRequest`, not from the policy (the NCD 160.18 / 110.18 precedent). TN 14 created the section, so it takes `gem:revisesPolicy` → `ncd150.9` under the S151 transmittal-edge rule ("New" is a change) and its Revision History entry describes the change it made. Change-propagation observation: **reflected** — the TN 14 Revision-History entry restates exactly the coverage carried by the live §B and §C text.
- **Source URLs.** Only TN 14 carries a verified `dc:source` (`R14NCD.pdf`, verbatim in the rendition's Coverage Transmittal Link, line-wrapped after `Regulations-and-` and rejoined without an inserted space per the S102 de-hyphenation rule). CR 3281 takes its delivering transmittal's IRI per the CR sourcing convention. CAG-00167N is minted Source-URL-pending — the rendition prints the NCA title without a resolvable NCAId and no URL was constructed by analogy (Tom's standing instruction).
- **Source / boundary.** Canonical source is `…?ncdid=285&ncdver=1` (Tom-supplied). `publicationNumber "100-3"`; `manualSectionNumber "150.9"`.
