### NCD 10.5 — Autogenous Epidural Blood Graft

*Extracted S188 (2026-07-21). `gemi:ncd10.5_r1` – `_r2`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-21 (Session 188). 2 rules at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; no inline HCPCS/ICD/CPT codes and no Coding Information section — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (autogenous epidural blood graft / Physicians' Services); domain axis omitted per convention. Fresh mint (not a promoted stub, never worklisted; Tom supplied the PDF and URL directly). **Version 1, ncdid=138, 2 pp, effective 1980-03-01 — no implementation date is posted, so none is asserted.** Single-version — the Other Versions table lists Version 1 alone (03/01/1980 – N/A, *"You are here"*) — so **no cross-version retention analysis applies**. 3 axis-2 `rule_type` values (3 `gem:ruleType` triples): service-definition (1), coverage-scope (1), eligibility (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit category: Physicians' Services (reuse). 0 provider credentials — the policy names no actor. 0 healthcare settings. 10 clinical-concept links — **7 mints, 3 reuses**. **0 policy-to-policy references — the document cites nothing**, so no transmittal, change-request or NCA stub was minted. No change requests.

**The NCD 100.3 twin.** A two-sentence prose NCD in the NCD 20.8.1 mould: the Item/Service Description defines the procedure (R1); the Indications and Limitations of Coverage sentence is the coverage gate (R2). There is no denial anywhere in the document, so no rule carries `non-coverage`. The rendition carries no Transmittal Information field, no Revision History, no Cross Reference and no National Coverage Analyses section — every absence is a confirmed empty section, not a gate.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | Item/Service Description: in the procedure blood is removed from the patient's vein and injected into his epidural space, to seal the spinal fluid leak and stop the pain | service-definition |
| R2 | Indications and Limitations of Coverage: autogenous epidural blood grafts are a safe and effective remedy for severe headaches that may occur after performance of spinal anesthesia, spinal taps or myelograms, and are covered | coverage-scope; eligibility |

#### Notes

- **B1 (R1 kept as a `service-definition` rule — confirmed).** Corollary #2 drops a pure definitional sentence when a named entity already carries its content, and the fresh `conceptAutogenousEpiduralBloodGraft` could carry it. Kept anyway, on the NCD 100.3 **B3** and NCD 270.4 **R1** line: the policy names no HCPCS code, so nothing external carries the procedure's identity, and the sentence states what the *service* is for coverage purposes. **The alternative was to drop it and let the concept description hold the definition** — the NCD 240.5 **B2** / NCD 280.8 **B1** path, whose corollary-#2 escape hatch is open here because the concept is a fresh mint from this same pass. The distinguisher is the one NCD 280.8 B1 itself names: those two sentences state how a *machine* works; this one states what a *procedure* is. Dropping it would also leave the policy with a single rule and lose the source's own two-part structure. Tom confirmed keep.
- **B2 (R2 typed `coverage-scope` + `eligibility` — confirmed).** Coverage is conditioned on a testable clinical circumstance — a severe headache following one of three named procedures — which a downstream evaluator reads as a *when-eligible* test. Matches NCD 100.3 **R2** and, more closely, NCD 110.3 **R1**, whose near-verbatim construction (*"has been shown to be safe and effective and has Medicare coverage when furnished to patients with…"*) also took both tags. **The alternative was `coverage-scope` alone** — a real reading, not a strawman: the sentence never says *"patients"*, and NCD 190.25 **R2** names patient categories yet carries `coverage-scope` only. The distinguisher is that 190.25 R2 is a clinical-utility statement (*"is useful for"*) while this sentence says *"are covered"*. Tom confirmed both tags.
- **B3 (*"the patient's vein"* reuses `conceptVeins`; description left untouched — confirmed, option (c)).** The source's singular *"vein"* differs from the existing individual's prefLabel *"veins"* by plurality only, so the S43 singular-normalization rule reuses rather than mints — read by its rationale per the **S152** gap note, since normalizing to `conceptVein` would produce no URI collision and the letter of the rule would mint a plurality twin. **Recorded and not repaired:** `gemi:conceptVeins` carries a generic prefLabel over a narrow description — *"The veins of the lower extremities, the anatomical structures affected in chronic venous insufficiency"* (minted for a CVI policy) — which does not describe the antecubital vein of a blood draw. The Plan-turn lean was to append to that description; a corpus check at the Generate turn found the practice **unprecedented — 0 of the 1922 `gem:ClinicalConcept` individuals then in the graph carry a reuse-append**, and only 2 name more than one policy at all (both minted that way). **Options put to Tom:** (a) reuse untouched; (b) append, setting a first-in-corpus precedent every future reuse would inherit; (c) reuse untouched and record the mismatch here. **Tom took (c).** The prefLabel/description mismatch on `conceptVeins` is a corpus-wide issue, not this policy's, and is a candidate for the SME taxonomy pass alongside the item-23/24/27 batch. *Alt considered and rejected:* mint `conceptVein` on the ground that the existing individual's description makes it a different concept wearing a generic label — rejected because the rules test the prefLabel, and minting on description grounds would invert the catalog-phrasings principle.
- **B4 (`conceptBlood` minted — confirmed).** Option-B inclusive default for a generic Item/Service-Description term, on the NCD 270.4 **B3** precedent under which Tom minted *dead tissue*, *lesion* and *new tissue*. It is load-bearing here rather than incidental: the patient's own blood is the graft material and is what makes the graft *autogenous*. Distinct from the existing `conceptWholeBlood` and `conceptArterialBlood` (different phrasing → mint, catalog-phrasings). **The alternative was to treat the bare noun as too generic to catalog.** Tom confirmed mint.
- **B5 (*"severe headaches"* mints `conceptSevereHeadache` — flagged, confirmed).** Singular-normalized (S43), no collision. Minted distinct from the existing `conceptHeadache` (prefLabel *"headache"*, from NCD 240.9): a severity qualifier is a phrasing difference, not a plurality difference, so the strict-match test defaults to mint — the `conceptSevereArthritis` / `conceptSevereOsteoarthritis` shape. Flagged rather than treated as automatic because the generic already exists; any broader/narrower or equivalence assertion against `conceptHeadache` is SME taxonomy work.
- **Concepts (7 mints, 3 reuses; Option-B).** Mints: `conceptAutogenousEpiduralBloodGraft`, `conceptBlood`, `conceptMyelogram`, `conceptSevereHeadache`, `conceptSpinalAnesthesia`, `conceptSpinalFluidLeak`, `conceptSpinalTap`. Reuses: `conceptEpiduralSpace`, `conceptPain`, `conceptVeins`. `conceptSpinalFluidLeak` keeps the source's own term — no normalization to cerebrospinal-fluid terminology, which the document never uses — and is distinct from the existing `conceptLeakage`. `conceptSpinalAnesthesia` is distinct from the four existing anaesthesia concepts (`conceptAnesthesia`, `conceptGeneralAnesthesia`, `conceptMonitoredAnesthesia`, `conceptHypotensiveAnesthesia`) under catalog-phrasings.
- **The document title is not a concept mint site.** *"Autogenous Epidural Blood Graft"* names the policy and is carried on `gemi:ncd10.5`'s `gem:prefLabel`; `conceptAutogenousEpiduralBloodGraft` mints from the operative Indications and Limitations prose, which uses the term (SKILL.md §*"A document title is not a section heading"*, the NCD 100.3 / NCD 280.16 B8 precedent). R1's anaphoric *"the procedure"* is not itself a mint site.
- **Drops.** The *"Please Note: This may not be an exhaustive list of all applicable Medicare benefit categories…"* line and the *"Links in PDF documents are not guaranteed to work…"* line are CMS-wide MCD boilerplate and are not extracted.
- **Verification.** Pre-flight URI collision check (case-insensitive) over all 10 proposed URIs: zero collisions; `ncd10.5` was absent from both the graph and the worklist. Instances + code-group **37,181** triples (+82 against the S187 baseline of 37,099 — mass-conservation proof: 27 policy-block-plus-workflow-state + 6 R1 + 7 R2 + 42 concept = 82, exact). Source apostrophes are U+0027 throughout the rendition and are carried verbatim.
- **Source / boundary.** Canonical source is `…?ncdid=138&ncdver=1` (Tom-supplied). `publicationNumber "100-3"`; `manualSectionNumber "10.5"`. Version 1, effective 1980-03-01; no implementation date; 2 pp. Single version, so `policyEffectiveDate` raises no `deferred_proposals[107]` question. `policies_processed` 92 —> 93. ### NCD 110.22 — Autologous Cellular Immunotherapy Treatment

*Extracted S189 (2026-07-22). `gemi:ncd110.22_r1` – `_r3`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-22 (Session 189). 3 rules at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; **the document names no ICD-10, HCPCS, CPT or modifier code anywhere** and has no Coding Information section — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (autologous cellular immunotherapy treatment / sipuleucel-T); domain axis omitted per convention. Fresh mint (not a promoted stub, never worklisted; Tom supplied the PDF and URL directly). **Version 1, ncdid=344, 5 pp, effective 2011-06-30, implementation 2011-08-08.** Single-version — the Other Versions table lists Version 1 alone (06/30/2011 – N/A, *"You are here"*) — so **no cross-version retention analysis applies**. 5 axis-2 `rule_type` values (6 `gem:ruleType` triples): service-definition (1), coverage-scope (2), eligibility (1), statutory-framing (1), credentialed-actor (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit categories: Outpatient Hospital Services Incident to a Physician's Service; Physicians' Services (both reuse). 0 policy-level provider credentials — the MAC is named as delegatee only. 0 healthcare settings. 26 clinical-concept links — **22 mints, 4 reuses**. **8 policy-to-policy reference stubs** (3 NCD-manual transmittals, 3 Claims Processing transmittals, 1 change request, 1 NCA). 1 change request (CR 7431), shared across the whole rescind-replace chain.

**A four-paragraph Item/Service Description over a two-sentence coverage core.** Sections B and D carry the whole operative content in one sentence each; section C is *"N/A"*. The Item/Service Description is long but mostly background — epidemiology, FDA-approval framing, and mechanism of action — of which only the fourth paragraph, the sipuleucel-T production and administration description, states what the *service* is. There is **no denial anywhere in the document**, so no rule carries `non-coverage`; section D's off-label clause is a delegation, not a denial.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | Item/Service Description A. General ¶4: sipuleucel-T is made individually for each patient from his own white blood cells, removed by leukapheresis, exposed to PA2024 (PAP linked with GM-CSF), and infused back; minimum 40 million treated white blood cells per dose; FDA-approved regimen of three doses two weeks apart over four weeks | service-definition |
| R2 | B. Nationally Covered Indications: effective for services on or after 2011-06-30, autologous cellular immunotherapy treatment — sipuleucel-T; PROVENGE® — improves health outcomes for Medicare beneficiaries with asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic metastatic castrate-resistant (hormone refractory) prostate cancer and is reasonable and necessary for this on-label indication under 1862(a)(1)(A) | coverage-scope; eligibility; statutory-framing |
| R3 | D. Other: effective for services on or after 2011-06-30, coverage of all off-label uses of the treatment for prostate cancer is left to the discretion of the local Medicare Administrative Contractors (`gem:delegatesCoverageTo gemi:credentialMedicareAdministrativeContractor`) | coverage-scope; credentialed-actor |

#### Notes

- **B1 (§A ¶4 captured whole as R1; ¶1–¶3 dropped as rules — confirmed).** ¶4 states what the *service* is, and the policy names no HCPCS code, so nothing external carries the procedure's identity — the NCD 10.5 **R1** / NCD 100.3 **R1** line. Pattern 3: the paragraph is one cohesive procedure description and is captured contiguously, verbatim, including its comparative opening and the embedded PAP/GM-CSF and dosing sentences (corollary #3 — don't drop content that is in the rule). ¶1 (prostate-cancer epidemiology), ¶2 (FDA approval and chemotherapy contrast) and ¶3 (immunotherapy mechanism of action) drive no evaluator decision; their content lands on the concept individuals under corollary #2. **The alternative was to drop §A entirely** — a real reading, since `conceptAutologousCellularImmunotherapyTreatment` and `conceptSipuleucelT` are fresh mints from this same pass and could hold the definition, and since NCD 270.1's V1 Item/Service-Description taxonomy went that way at S152 (16 concepts, 0 rules). The distinguisher is the one NCD 280.8 **B1** names: ¶3 states how a biological *mechanism* works, ¶4 states what a *procedure* is. Tom confirmed the split.
- **B2 (¶2's FDA-approval sentence not captured as a rule — confirmed).** **The alternative was real and was argued:** sections B and D turn on *"this on-label indication"* and *"all off-label uses"*, and corollary #1's escape hatch opens where a reference is needed to execute a downstream rule — so ¶2 could have been captured as `service-standard`. It was not, for two reasons. First, §B states its covered indication in full, so R2 and R3 execute without it. Second, ¶2's FDA indication (*"castration-resistant, metastatic prostate cancer"*) is **broader** than §B's (*"asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic …"*), so capturing ¶2 as the label-defining rule would manufacture an internal tension the source never asserts. **Interaction recorded:** the choice is what keeps *"APC8015"* and *"docetaxel"* out of the concept catalog — both are named only in ¶2, and the S48 individual-drug rule mints a drug name only when a rule names it. Flipping B2 would have brought both in. Tom confirmed the drop.
- **B3 (R2 typed `coverage-scope` + `eligibility` + `statutory-framing` — confirmed).** Coverage turns on a testable beneficiary condition, and §1862(a)(1)(A) sits **inside** the testable sentence rather than framing the policy from outside, which is corollary #1's own exception. Corpus practice is uniform: every `coverage-scope` rule in the graph citing §1862(a)(1)(A) inline also carries `statutory-framing`, and NCD 240.9 **R25** is exactly this three-tag shape. **The alternative was the bare `coverage-scope` + `eligibility` pair** of NCD 10.5 **R2** and NCD 100.3 **R2** — the closest structural twins — but neither of those sentences cites a statute at all. Tom confirmed all three tags.

Single-domain policy (the Benson-Henry Institute Cardiac Wellness Program as an approved ICR program); domain axis omitted per convention. Fresh mint (not a promoted stub, never worklisted; Tom supplied the PDF and URL directly). **Version 1, ncdid=362, 5 pp, effective 2014-05-06, implementation 2014-11-04.** Single-version — the Other Versions table lists Version 1 alone (05/06/2014 – N/A, *"You are here"*) — so **no cross-version retention analysis applies**. 4 axis-2 `rule_type` values (4 `gem:ruleType` triples): service-definition (1), coverage-scope (1), statutory-framing (1), non-coverage (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. Benefit category: Intensive Cardiac Rehabilitation Program (**mint** — the corpus's 74th and first ICR benefit category). 0 provider credentials. 0 healthcare settings. 11 clinical-concept links — **9 mints, 2 reuses**. **17 policy-to-policy reference stubs cited** (14 transmittals, 1 NCA, 2 NCDs), of which 6 are new mints; **11 change requests** linked by `gem:referencesChangeRequest`, of which 3 are new mints, plus CR 8894 linked from its deliverer.

**A three-sentence policy with a Revision History four times its length.** The operative content is one definitional sentence in §A, one coverage sentence in §B and one denial sentence in §C; §D is *"N/A"*. Everything else in the document is provenance: Herbert Benson's biography and a quoted 1960s anecdote in §A, and twelve Revision-History entries — eleven of them quarterly ICD-10 coding-maintenance deliveries that change nothing about this policy. **This is the corpus's most reference-dense policy relative to its rule count**: 3 rules against 28 cited documents.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | Item/Service Description A. General, closing sentence: the Cardiac Wellness Program is a multi-component intervention program of supervised exercise, behavioral interventions and counseling, designed to reduce cardiovascular risk and improve health outcomes | service-definition |
| R2 | B. Nationally Covered Indications: effective for claims with dates of service on and after 2014-05-06, the program meets the ICR program requirements of §1861(eee)(4)(A) of the Social Security Act and 42 C.F.R. §410.49(c) and has been included on the list of approved ICR programs | coverage-scope; statutory-framing |
| R3 | C. Nationally Non-Covered Indications: effective 2014-05-06, an ICR program not included on that list as a Medicare-approved ICR program is non-covered | non-coverage |

#### Notes

- **B1 (§A's closing sentence captured as R1; the Benson provenance sentences dropped as rules — confirmed).** The sentence states what the *service* is, and the policy names no HCPCS code, so nothing external carries the program's identity — the NCD 10.5 **R1** / NCD 110.22 **R1** line. Pattern 1: it is a single self-contained sentence, so no scaffold is needed. **The alternative was real and thinner than S189's:** drop it and let `conceptCardiacWellnessProgram`'s `gem:description` carry the content under corollary #2, whose escape hatch is open because that concept is a fresh mint from this same pass — the NCD 270.1 V1-taxonomy path. NCD 110.22 **B1** distinguished a *mechanism* description (dropped) from a *procedure* description (kept); this sentence is neither exactly — it states a program's *composition*. It was kept because the composition is what the ICR-approval determination in §B turns on. The preceding sentences (Benson's 40-year attribution, and the quoted blood-pressure/stress/hypertension anecdote with its `ideafit.com` citation) are background and motivation: they drive no evaluator decision, and their content lands on `conceptBloodPressure`, `conceptStress` and `conceptHypertension`. Tom confirmed.
- **B2 (R2 typed `coverage-scope` + `statutory-framing` — confirmed).** The statutory references sit **inside** the testable sentence rather than framing the policy from outside, which is corollary #1's own exception, and the corpus is uniform on the pairing (NCD 240.9 **R25**, NCD 110.22 **R2**). **The alternative was to add `service-standard`** — a real reading, since what §1861(eee)(4)(A) and 42 C.F.R. §410.49(c) supply *are* program standards the program had to meet. It was set aside because the sentence's operative claim is the coverage consequence of list membership, not the standards themselves: the evaluator tests *"is this program on the list"*, not *"does it satisfy §410.49(c)"*. Tom confirmed the two-tag form.
- **B3 (R3 typed bare `non-coverage` — confirmed).** A clean IF/THEN denial with one condition. **The alternative was `non-coverage` + `coverage-scope`**, which 8 rules in the corpus carry; it was set aside because the sentence makes no positive coverage statement at all — it is the complement of R2, and tagging it `coverage-scope` would double-count R2's claim. 118 corpus rules carry bare `non-coverage`, the modal form. Tom confirmed.
- **B4 (`conceptCardiacWellnessProgram` minted alongside `conceptBensonHenryInstituteCardiacWellnessProgram` — confirmed).** Two phrasings of one program, both the policy's own, minted as two individuals under the catalog-phrasings rule; equivalence between them is an SME assertion for the later taxonomy pass, never a collapse at extraction. **The alternative was to treat the short form as a back-reference** and reuse the long individual — the S27 pronominal-back-reference exception. It does not reach: *"The Cardiac Wellness Program"* is an abbreviated proper name that stands on its own in a provider note, not a pronoun that is incoherent without its antecedent paragraph. The document **title** is not a third mint site (S158). Tom confirmed.
- **B5 (`conceptMultiComponentInterventionProgram` minted — confirmed).** Read as a therapy-modality descriptor under the Option-B inclusive scope rule. **The alternative was to drop it as administrative vocabulary**, on the reading that "multi-component intervention program" classifies a program rather than naming a clinical entity. It was minted because the classification is the source's own answer to *what kind of thing this is*, and a provider note describing a cardiac program could carry the phrase. Tom confirmed.
- **B6 (URI drops the `(ICR)` parenthetical: `gemi:conceptIntensiveCardiacRehabilitationProgram` — confirmed).** §634's acronym rule drops an uppercase parenthetical from the URI while the prefLabel keeps it verbatim. **The alternative was real and had the more recent precedent:** S189 **B8** kept the acronyms in `conceptProstaticAcidPhosphatasePAP` and `conceptGranulocyteMacrophageColonyStimulatingFactorGMCSF` *because the source's later sentences used the acronyms as the operative terms* — and §C here does exactly that, using the bare *"ICR program"* twice. The corpus is genuinely split (29 URIs include the acronym, 38 drop it), so precedent settles nothing. Tom confirmed the drop, against the S189 shape.
- **B7 (benefit category and clinical concept minted for the same words — confirmed).** `gemi:benefitCategoryIntensiveCardiacRehabilitationProgram` names the Medicare **benefit classification** from the Benefit Category field; `gemi:conceptIntensiveCardiacRehabilitationProgram` names the **program** as §B's prose does. Kept distinct on the settings-are-not-benefit-categories analogue — a benefit classification and the thing classified are different entities even when the words match. **The alternative was to mint only the benefit category** and treat §B's mention as the same entity. Tom confirmed both.
- **B8 (NCD 90.2 and NCD 110.24 minted as stubs, referenced from the policy — confirmed).** Both are named only inside another transmittal's rescind-reason, describing a change to a *different* policy: TN 11460 updated NCD 90.2's NGS spreadsheet, TN 11179 revised NCD 110.24's CAR-T attachment. The S131 mint-every-referenced-policy rule addresses this case in terms — *"a rescind-reason that names a different NCD is not used to gate the mint"* — and the NCD 160.18 S131 pass is the precedent. **The alternative was to hang the reference off `gemi:tn11460NCD` / `gemi:tn11179NCD`**, where the described change actually lands; it was set aside because this policy's text reports that change second-hand, and `gem:revisesPolicy` is confirmed only at the transmittal's own pass. **This confirmation resolves the conflict logged as handoff §4 item 5** — see the *Open consequence* note below. Tom confirmed.
- **B9 (no concepts harvested from Revision History prose — confirmed).** *"NGS"* and *"CAR-T"* are named in the Revision History and nowhere else, and both belong to other policies. The three-contexts rule excludes revision-history **codes** explicitly and the strict-prose credential rule excludes revision history by cross-reference; concepts are treated the same way by parity. **The alternative was to mint them** under Option B's err-toward-inclusion posture. Set aside: revision history is a change log about other documents, and minting from it would attach another policy's subject matter to this one. Worth noting that SKILL.md states this exclusion for codes and credentials but not for concepts — a small gap in the written rule, applied here by parity. Tom confirmed.
- **B10 (the four new narrative CRs minted Source-pending — confirmed).** CR 8894 is unproblematic: TN 175 delivers it, so `dc:source gemi:tn175NCD` per the CR sourcing convention. CR 12124, CR 8197 and CR 9087 name no delivering transmittal anywhere in this document, so the convention has no IRI to point at and they are minted with no `dc:source`, the S189 Source-pending shape. They are linked from the policy by `gem:referencesChangeRequest` — the mention relationship — on the `gemi:ncd160.24` → `gemi:cr8109` precedent. **The alternative was to hold them off the graph** until a deliverer is known; that is what Tom's Q1 answer at this Plan turn reversed. Tom confirmed.

#### Reference scope

- **`gem:revisesPolicy` to this policy: TN 175 only.** It created the section, and *"New" is a change* under the S151 transmittal-edge rule.
- **The eleven Revision-History transmittals take no transmittal-side edge.** All are quarterly ICD-10 coding-maintenance deliveries; three disclaim a policy change in terms (*"No policy is being changed as a result of these updates"*, TN 12318; *"No policy-related changes are included with the ICD-10 quarterly updates"*, TN 2298 / TN 1854 / TN 1798). The parallel is close enough that the *differences* are the interesting part — see the verbatim-divergence note below.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | Indications and Limitations of Coverage, sentence 1: the policy applies to biofeedback therapy rendered by a practitioner in an office or other facility setting | coverage-scope, setting-definition, credentialed-actor |

**Notes**

- **B1 (¶2 sentences 2–3 kept as R3, Pattern 3 — genuine borderline).** The passage is definitional and drives no coverage decision on its own, which is exactly the shape NCD 30.1's own **B3** dropped and its **B4** kept. It splits: sentence 2 (*“not a treatment, per se, but a tool to help patients learn how to perform PME”*) is relational across biofeedback and PME, the S99 **R39** shape with no single concept as its definition home; sentence 3 *is* a definition of `conceptBiofeedbackAssistedPME`, squarely corollary #2. **Three options were put:** (a) capture both as one Pattern-3 `service-definition` rule, on NCD 30.1's R3, which kept a structurally identical two-sentence passage; (b) drop both, sentence 3's verbatim onto the concept (the 30.1 B3 treatment); (c) split — keep sentence 2, drop sentence 3 — the cleanest read of the corollaries taken separately. **Tom: (a).**
- **B2 (`credentialPractitioner` minted at the bare source phrase).** *“rendered by a practitioner”* is the canonical strict-prose licensing case — the performer of the service the policy governs. Nothing in the 100-individual credential vocabulary is bare *“practitioner”*; `credentialTreatingPractitioner`, `credentialOtherPractitioner`, `credentialAuthorizedPractitioner` and `credentialNonPhysicianPractitioner` each add a word, and reuse on similarity is what the source-phrase routing rule forbids. No valid alternative was offered. Policy-level `gem:requiresProviderCredential`.
- **B3 (`credentialContractor` minted; the MAC individual not reused).** *“Contractors may decide whether or not to cover…”* is shape-B bounded delegation inside a nationally-covered frame, so R5 carries `gem:delegatesCoverageTo`. The delegatee is minted at this policy's own word, singular-normalised, following the **S187 `credentialLocalContractor` precedent** at NCD 150.9 B5: a 2001 text predates the Medicare Administrative Contractor by two years and never uses the term. *Alt (real):* reuse `credentialMedicareAdministrativeContractor` as the successor entity, SKILL.md naming only a two-member delegatee set. **Tom: (a).** Rule-level only — no policy-level credential link, matching `gemi:ncd150.9`, whose `credentialLocalContractor` likewise has a single inbound edge from its rule.
- **B4 (`settingOffice` + `settingFacility` minted; no re-parenting).** *“in an office or other facility setting”* names two places. Both are minted at the bare place phrase per the settings labelling rule (never the word “setting”), following the bare-word precedents `settingInstitution` (S156), `settingInpatient` and `settingOutpatient` (S157) — each minted distinct from a richer existing sibling. Both take `skos:broader settingAnywhere` only. *Alts (real):* (b) reuse `settingPhysiciansOffice` for “office”; (c) mint `settingOffice` only, treating “other facility setting” as a residual rather than a named place; (d) additionally re-parent `settingPhysiciansOffice` under a new `settingOffice`. **Tom: (a)** — which is also the only option leaving every edit in this extraction purely additive, (d) being the one that would have modified an existing individual.
- **B5 (bare “PME” reused onto `conceptPelvicMuscleExercise`, not minted).** The policy uses the bare acronym twice (*“learn how to perform PME”*, *“in the performance of PME”*). ### NCD 230.16 — Bladder Stimulators (Pacemakers)

*Extracted S194 (2026-07-23). `gemi:ncd230.16_r1`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-23 (Session 194). 1 rule at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; **the document names no ICD-10, HCPCS, CPT or modifier code anywhere** — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (bladder stimulators / Prosthetic Devices); domain axis omitted per convention. Fresh single-pass extraction from Tom's supplied rendition and URL; never worklisted, minted direct to the graph. **Single-version policy** — the Other Versions table lists Version 1 alone (10/07/1996 – N/A, “You are here”) — so Pre-Extraction Requirement 5 is met by the one rendition, no cross-version retention walk applies, and the effective date comes straight from V1's Tracking Information, making `deferred_proposals[107]` satisfied by construction (the fourth policy so compliant, after NCD 110.18, NCD 220.6.20 and NCD 30.1.1). **No implementation date is written**: the MCD field is empty on this policy, and where V1 publishes none the triple is dropped rather than inferred (S192). 1 axis-2 `rule_type` value (1 `gem:ruleType` triple): non-coverage (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. No δ-scope. Benefit category: Prosthetic Devices (reuse). **No provider credential** — the determination is agentless. 1 healthcare-setting link (`settingFacility`, reuse). 17 clinical-concept links — 11 mints + 6 reuses. 2 stubs minted: `tn89CIM` and `tn74CIM`.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | Indications and Limitations of Coverage, both sentences: the use of spinal cord electrical stimulators, rectal electrical stimulators, and bladder wall stimulators is not considered reasonable and necessary, so no program payment may be made for these devices or for their implant | non-coverage |

**Notes**

- **B1 (one Pattern-3 rule, not two).** The *“Therefore”* binds the payment prohibition to the reasonable-and-necessary determination as a single IF/THEN, and the internal *“…, …, and …”* enumeration stays inside it under the disjunction clause of the IF/THEN heuristic. `gemi:ncd20.29_r5` folds exactly this shape (*“…are not covered under the Medicare program. No program payment may be made…”*), as does `gemi:ncd30.3_r3`. *Alt (real):* split — sentence 1 is the §1862(a)(1)(A) determination and sentence 2 the payment consequence, which alone reaches the implant procedure. **Tom: (a).**
- **B2 (Item/Service Description sentences 3–4 dropped as rules).** *“the issue of safety … has not been resolved”* and *“some facilities … have stopped using this method due to the pain”* are CMS's stated grounds, not criteria a claim is tested against; their content survives on `conceptInfection`, `conceptErosion`, `conceptElectronicEmptying` and `conceptPain`. The NCD 230.8 device-description drop and the NCD 230.19 background drop. *Alt (real):* capture, on `gemi:ncd240.3_r1`, which kept its rationale — but there the rationale sits inside the operative determination sentence rather than in a separate section. **Tom: (a).** Sentences 1–2 are dropped silently under corollary #2 (device description; content on the concepts).
- **B3 (`conceptPacemaker` minted at the bare source phrase).** The body prose names the device twice — *“commonly known as bladder stimulators or pacemakers”* — and the catalog-phrasings rule mints at the source's wording, the single-term-linkage rationale wanting a note saying *“pacemaker”* to reach this policy on one term. *Alt (real):* don't mint — the corpus qualifies every other pacemaker concept (`conceptCardiacPacemaker`, `conceptPacemakerMonitoring`, `conceptDualChamberPacemaker`), and a bare label reads as ambiguous in the catalog. **Tom: (a).** The individual's `gem:description` records which sense of the word this is; precision belongs downstream of presence. The document *title* also carries the word and mints nothing (S158).
- **B4 (`conceptMuscleOfTheBladder` and `conceptWallOfTheBladder` minted).** Both are standalone noun phrases in the source (*“forces the muscles of the bladder to contract”*, *“the implantation of electrodes in the wall of the bladder”*) rather than fabricated constituents of a composite, and the corpus catalogs anatomy (`conceptBladder`, `conceptSpinalCord`, `conceptPelvicFloorMusculature`). *Alt (real):* mint neither, `conceptBladder` and `conceptBladderWallStimulator` already carrying the words. **Tom: (a).** The modifier form *“bladder wall”*, which the source uses only inside *“bladder wall stimulators”*, is not separately minted.
- **B5 (“placement” and “material selection” not minted).** They are enumerated beside *infection* and *erosion*, but they name device-engineering and manufacturing attributes rather than clinical entities a provider note would carry — the NCD 30.1.1 treatment of *“visual and/or auditory evidence”*. *Alt (real):* mint both under Option-B inclusiveness, *“placement”* being a procedural act in an implantation context. **Tom: (a).**
- **B6 (`settingFacility` linked).** *“some facilities previously using electronic emptying”* names a place of care as the locus of the treatment, and the settings rule captures every place the text names. Reuse of the individual minted at S193 (NCD 30.1.1 B4). *Alt (real):* no link — the mention is a historical-practice observation rather than a locus of furnishing, a suitability referent or an exclusion trigger, and this policy makes no setting-dependent call. **Tom: (a).**
- **B7 (TN 74's Revision-History concepts not linked).** The 02/1995 entry names *pelvic floor stimulators* and *urinary incontinence*, but Revision History is change-log context and no policy in the corpus has minted or linked a concept from it (the L36524 and NCD 160.23 drops are the standing shape). The content is preserved verbatim on `gemi:tn74CIM`'s `gem:description`. *Alt (real):* link them — the citing policy does name them, and the S131 reversal already moved *document* citations out of the exclusion. **Tom: (a).**
- **B8 (both CIM stubs minted Source-URL-pending, no `gem:sourceAvailability`).** CMS's public transmittal archive begins at 2000 (confirmed by search this session), and every CIM transmittal in the corpus numbered 114 or lower carries no rendition URL while every one numbered 126 or higher does. `gem:sourceUnobtainable` has only ever been asserted on Tom's own verification (`tn78CIM`, S156) or direction (`tn132CIM`, `tn150CIM`), so the default for a new mint is bare. *Alt (real):* assert `sourceUnobtainable` + `planNone` now on the era gate, resolving both at mint instead of enqueueing them. **Tom: (a)** — which grows the `source_availability_unverified` INFO from 24 to **26** and adds both to handoff §4 item 50's queue.
- **Transmittal edges.** Both stubs take **both** directions. `tn89CIM` is the current Transmittal Information field entry (Policy-to-Policy rule 4) and its Revision History entry describes the change it made (*“Eliminated use of name brand products”*) → `gem:revisesPolicy`. `tn74CIM` is named only in Revision History, but the citing side asserts an agnostic `gem:referencesPolicy` to every transmittal it names, superseded revision-history transmittals included (S131; the S147 option-(b) reading retired at S190 B8), and its entry likewise describes a change → `gem:revisesPolicy`. Because both directions are asserted for TN 74, no `check_proposal_b` Category D/E question arises. Neither transmittal names a Change Request: 1995–96 predates the CMS Change Request system (the `tn87CIM` precedent).
- **Manual token, by era gate *and* by series.** Pub. 100-03, Pub. 100-04 and the OTN series all postdate 2003, so a coverage transmittal of 09/1996 or 02/1995 can only be CIM (HCFA Pub. 6). The corroboration here is unusually tight: `tn87CIM` (06/1996) and `tn90CIM` (10/1996) already sit in the graph and **bracket** TN 89, and `tn78CIM` (1995-08-07) sits just above TN 74 in the same series and year. Both carry `gem:publicationNumber "6"`.
- **Change propagation.** TN 89 **reflected** — the current text carries no brand names anywhere, describing the devices only as *“commonly known as bladder stimulators or pacemakers”*. TN 74 **not reflected** — the current Version 1 text names neither pelvic floor stimulators nor urinary incontinence in any section, so its claimed change is not visible in the policy it revised. Recorded on each stub's `gem:workflowDescription`.
- **No link to NCD 230.8.** The graph's coverage statement on pelvic floor electrical stimulation for urinary incontinence is `gemi:ncd230.8`, and TN 74's entry puts the two documents in the same subject area — but NCD 230.16 does not cite it and carries no Cross Reference content, so no edge is minted in either direction (faithfulness to what the source actually says, the NCD 280.1 rule). No cross-policy reconciliation is attempted; that is the downstream evaluator's work under *denial language overrides approval language*.
- **Concepts (11 mints, 6 reuses; Option-B).** **Mints:** `conceptUrinaryBladder` (a word added to the existing *“bladder”*, which is also linked — the policy uses both), `conceptMuscleOfTheBladder`, `conceptBladderStimulator`, `conceptPacemaker`, `conceptWallOfTheBladder`, `conceptRectalCone`, `conceptErosion`, `conceptElectronicEmptying`, `conceptSpinalCordElectricalStimulator`, `conceptRectalElectricalStimulator`, `conceptBladderWallStimulator`. - **Verification.** Pre-flight URI collision check (case-insensitive, suffix-aware) over all 15 proposed local names, across all three TTL files: **zero collisions**. `ncd230.16` was absent from graph and worklist alike. ### NCD 110.20 — Blood Brain Barrier Osmotic Disruption for Treatment of Brain Tumors

*Extracted S195 (2026-07-23). `gemi:ncd110.20_r1` – `gemi:ncd110.20_r3`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-23 (Session 195). 3 rules at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; **the document names no ICD-10, HCPCS, CPT or modifier code anywhere** — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes). Single-domain policy (osmotic blood brain barrier disruption for brain tumors); domain axis omitted per convention. Fresh single-pass extraction from Tom's supplied rendition and URL; never worklisted, minted direct to the graph. **Single-version policy** — the Other Versions table lists Version 1 alone (03/20/2007 – N/A, “You are here”) — so Pre-Extraction Requirement 5 is met by the one rendition, no cross-version retention walk applies, and both dates come straight from V1's Tracking Information, making `deferred_proposals[107]` satisfied by construction (the fifth policy so compliant, after NCD 110.18, NCD 220.6.20, NCD 30.1.1 and NCD 230.16). **An implementation date IS written** (05/07/2007): V1 publishes the field, which is the other half of the S192 rule and the first new extraction to exercise it — NCD 230.16 one session earlier had the field empty and dropped the triple. 3 axis-2 `rule_type` values (4 `gem:ruleType` triples): coverage-scope (2), non-coverage (1), service-definition (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. No δ-scope. Benefit categories: Incident to a physician's professional Service, Inpatient Hospital Services (both reuse). **No provider credential** — the determination is agentless, its only named agent being CMS itself. **No healthcare-setting link** (B7). 29 clinical-concept links — 26 mints + 3 reuses. 2 stubs minted: `tn67NCD` and `cag00333N`.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | §C Nationally Non-Covered Indications: effective for services performed on and after March 20, 2007, CMS determines that the use of osmotic BBBD is not reasonable and necessary when used as part of a treatment regimen for brain tumors | non-coverage |
| R2 | §D Other: this NCD does not alter in any manner the coverage of anti-cancer chemotherapy | coverage-scope |
| R3 | §A General, paragraph 3: the BBBD process includes all items and services necessary to perform the procedure, including hospitalization, monitoring, and repeated imaging procedures | coverage-scope, service-definition |

**Notes**

- **B1 (BBBD-process bundling sentence captured as R3).** *“includes all items and services necessary to perform the procedure”* is an all-inclusiveness declaration rather than a device or service identity statement: it fixes how far R1's denial reaches when a claim carries a hospitalization or imaging line beside the procedure. That increment beyond identity is what the corpus keeps — `gemi:a52492_r19`, `gemi:a52494_r11` and `gemi:a52510_r6` are the *all-inclusive* shape, minus their coding context, which is why `coding-correctness` does not ride here and `service-definition` does. *Alt (real):* drop it. It sits in Item/Service Description, whose sentences S194's B2 dropped as CMS's stated grounds, its content survives on `conceptBBBDProcess`, and R1 denies *“osmotic BBBD”* rather than *“the BBBD process”*, so R1 executes without it. **Tom: (a).** The other six Item/Service Description sentences are dropped under corollary #2 (background, definition and theory; content on the concepts they name).
- **B2 (all eight disruption phrasings minted).** The policy names the same family of acts eight ways in nine sentences: *blood brain barrier (BBB)*, *BBBD*, *disruption of the BBB*, *osmotic disruption*, *osmotic disruption of the BBB*, *barrier disruption*, *BBBD process*, *osmotic BBBD*. Each is a self-contained noun phrase standing in its own sentence, which the catalog-phrasings rule mints, and redundant single-term coverage is the matching feature rather than a cost — a note carrying any one of them reaches this policy without the matcher knowing they co-refer. S194 is the precedent for a dense phrasing family out of one short policy (*bladder stimulator* beside *bladder wall stimulator*; *urinary bladder* beside *bladder*). *Alt (real):* mint four — BBB, BBBD, osmotic BBBD, osmotic disruption — and read the rest as in-document back-references to the act already named, the reading S193's B5 applied and which handoff §4 item 52 leaves open. **Tom: (a).**
- **B3 (*“malignant primary or metastatic brain tumors”* as one composite).** The composite rule captures the phrase whole and forbids fabricating constituents; *metastatic brain tumor* is a constituent this policy never writes on its own. `conceptSevereChronicIntractablePainOfMalignantOrNonmalignantOrigin` (NCD 280.14, S157) is the corpus's disjunctive-composite precedent. *Alt (real):* distribute into two individuals, as S193 distributed *“stress and/or urge incontinence”*, on the ground that *“or”* names two conditions a claim would carry separately. **Tom: (a).** The bare `conceptBrainTumor` is minted separately from paragraph 2's own wording, so the narrower term is not lost.
- **B4 (`conceptBradykinin` minted).** No `gem:PolicyRule` of this policy names it, which is the individual-drug rule's literal trigger for withholding. It is minted anyway: the rule exists to keep a formulary out of the catalog (*warfarin*, *amoxicillin*), and bradykinin is named here in the third slot of a list of disruption mechanisms, beside *osmotic disruption* and *irradiation* — a physiological mediator used as a technique, not a prescribed product. *Alt (real):* withhold on the rule as written. **Tom: (a).**
- **B5 (terms inside the theoretical-mechanism sentence).** *“drug-tumor contact time”* is minted — a hyphenated compound the source uses as a term, line-wrapped after *“drug-”* and rejoined without an inserted space per S102. *“the concentration of chemotherapy drugs delivered to the tumor”* and, in paragraph 1, *“various naturally occurring and synthetic substances”* are not: a clause describing an effect and a generic catch-all, neither a term the source names. *Alt (real):* mint the concentration phrase too — `conceptGlucoseConcentration` (NCD 40.2) and `conceptCReactiveProteinConcentration` (A52466) show a named concentration is an established shape, and Option-B errs toward inclusion. It was not taken because both of those came from compact noun phrases their sources use as terms, where this policy has only a verb clause; Tom raised exactly this at Plan turn and confirmed the distinction. **Tom: (a).**
- **B6 (one individual for *“blood brain barrier (BBB)”*).** The parenthetical gloss is preserved in `gem:prefLabel` and dropped from the URI — the majority form among the corpus's 97 glossed labels (`conceptSystemicLupusErythematosus`, `conceptTotalLungCapacity`, `conceptHemangioendothelioma`) — and the bare *“the BBB”* in the next sentence is a back-reference to a term glossed in the same sentence as its full form. *Alt (real):* mint two, per SKILL.md §Clinical Concepts' written default that acronym-vs-full-form defaults to mint. **Tom: (a).** Handoff §4 item 52 records that the written rule and the S193 precedent disagree; this mint follows the narrow reading and does not settle the item. **The policy's other acronym is unaffected either way:** `conceptBBBD` is minted bare because the full form appears in this policy only in Revision History (change-log context) and in the cited NCA's title (another document's name for itself).
- **B7 (no healthcare-setting link).** The policy names no place of care. *“Inpatient Hospital Services”* is a Benefit Category field value and SKILL.md keeps settings and benefit categories distinct even when the words match; *“hospitalization”* names an episode, not a locus. *Alt (real):* link `settingInpatientHospital`, reading a named episode as naming its locus and the benefit category as the context of furnishing. **Tom: (a).** Contrast S194's B6, where *“some facilities previously using electronic emptying”* named a place and `settingFacility` was linked.
- **B8 (the three bundled service components linked as concepts).** *“hospitalization”* (reuse), *“monitoring”* (mint, bare — the S194 bare-*“pacemaker”* shape) and *“repeated imaging procedures”* (mint, singular-normalised) each name a clinical service the policy places inside the BBBD process, and each is a term a claim or note could carry — presence, not interpretation. *Alt (real):* treat them as cost-bundle items rather than clinical entities and link none, the S194 B5 reading that dropped *“placement”* and *“material selection”*. **Tom: (a).**
- **Transmittal edge.** `tn67NCD` takes **both** directions: `gem:revisesPolicy` under the S151 rule as sharpened at S169, its Revision History entry describing the change it made (and creating the determination is a change), and this policy's citing-side `gem:referencesPolicy` as the current Transmittal Information field entry (Policy-to-Policy rule 4). No `check_proposal_b` Category D/E question arises. No Change Request is named, so none is minted.
- **Manual token, by verified rendition filename.** `R67NCD.pdf`, read from the MCD's own Coverage Transmittal Link, is token-source priority 1 and outranks every other signal; `gem:publicationNumber "100-03"` follows, and the era gate is consistent (Pub. 100-03 runs from 2003; this is a 2007 document). **The collision the mandatory token exists to prevent is live in the corpus here:** `gemi:tn67CIM` — Coverage Issues Manual Transmittal 67 of 02/1994, cited by NCD 280.14 — is already in the graph, so a bare `gemi:tn67` would name two documents. This is the second such pair after TN 78 (S148), and the first found at mint rather than in cleanup.
- **Change propagation.** TN 67 **reflected** — the Revision History entry's determination text is carried near-verbatim by the current V1 §C and §D, the entry writing *“osmotic blood brain barrier disruption”* where §C writes *“osmotic BBBD”*. Recorded on the stub's `gem:workflowDescription`.

### NCD 190.15 — Blood Counts

*Extracted S196 (2026-07-23). `gemi:ncd190.15_r1`–`gemi:ncd190.15_r13`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-23 (Session 196). 13 rules, all at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; coding is not in the NCD narrative — it lives in the external quarterly Lab-NCD Covered Code Lists, so no inline ICD-10/HCPCS/CPT and no code group). Single-version, single-domain policy (Diagnostic Laboratory Tests; blood counts); domain axis omitted per convention. Fresh direct mint; never worklisted before S195, when the Plan turn was opened and deliberately stopped for scale. 5 distinct axis-2 `rule_type` values (14 `gem:ruleType` triples): coverage-scope (9), non-coverage (2), documentation (1), frequency (1), coding-correctness (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. No δ-scope: each numbered item's parenthetical enumeration is illustrative (*"e.g."* / *"for example"*) and folds verbatim into its parent rule per the NCD 190.14 R1 / NCD 80.11 / NCD 190.2 disjunctive-fold precedent. Benefit category: Diagnostic Laboratory Tests (reuse). Provider credential: 1 mint (`credentialOrderingProvider`). Healthcare setting: 1 reuse (`settingInpatientHospital`). **204 clinical-concept links: 174 mints + 30 reuses** — the largest single-policy mint in the corpus, six times the prior record of 28 (A52514). The hundredth policy processed.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | Indications, intro: indications for a CBC or hemogram include red cell, platelet and white cell disorders; examples enumerated individually below | coverage-scope |
| R2 | Indications 1: evaluation of bone marrow dysfunction from neoplasms, therapeutic agents, toxic-substance exposure or pregnancy; assessing peripheral destruction of blood cells, suspected marrow failure or infiltrate, suspected myeloproliferative / myelodysplastic / lymphoproliferative processes, immune disorders | coverage-scope |
| R3 | Indications 2: red cell (RBC) parameters — findings associated with anemia or other red blood cell disorder (illustrative list folded) | coverage-scope |
| R4 | Indications 3: red cell (RBC) parameters — findings associated with polycythemia (illustrative list folded) | coverage-scope |
| R5 | Indications 4: CBC with differential count, WBC — findings associated with leukemia, infection/inflammation, marrow failure or infiltrate, myeloproliferative / myelodysplastic / lymphoproliferative disorder, leukopenia-causing drugs, immune disorders (illustrative list folded) | coverage-scope |
| R6 | Indications 5: platelet count — findings associated with increased or decreased platelet production and destruction, or platelet dysfunction (illustrative list folded) | coverage-scope |
| R7 | Indications 6: red cell parameters, *"in addition to those already listed"* — thalassemia, suspected hemoglobinopathy, lead poisoning, arsenic poisoning, spherocytosis | coverage-scope |
| R8 | Indications 7: WBC differential, *"in addition to those already listed"* — storage diseases/mucopolysaccharidoses, leukocytosis-causing drugs such as G-CSF or GM-CSF | coverage-scope |
| R9 | Indications 8: platelet count, *"in addition to those already listed"* — May-Hegglin syndrome, Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome | coverage-scope |
| R10 | Limitations 1: testing of asymptomatic patients, or of patients without a condition expected to result in a hematological abnormality, is screening and is not a covered service | non-coverage |
| R11 | Limitations 2: where the ordering provider requests only a hemoglobin or hematocrit, the remaining components of the CBC are not covered | non-coverage |
| R12 | Limitations 3: a blood count for an ESRD patient billed outside the ESRD rate requires documentation of medical necessity with the claim | documentation |
| R13 | Limitations 4: a single CBC may suffice; repeat testing limited except on abnormal results or change in clinical condition, a more descriptive diagnosis code to be reported, with a continued-risk exception | frequency, coding-correctness |

**Notes**

- **B1 (Indications intro kept as R1, Tom-confirmed).** *"Indications for a CBC or hemogram include red cell, platelet, and white cell disorders"* is the general gate and items 1–8 are its examples by the source's own next sentence. The NCD 210.1 S55 umbrella-drop does not reach it: there the umbrella's content survived on Pattern-2 heading repetition, and here the heading is bare *"Indications"*, so dropping R1 would lose the three-way classification entirely. Folding all eight items into R1 under the examples-folded rule was considered and rejected — each item is a rule-shaped sentence with its own subject and verb, and the fold yields one ~700-word string.
- **B2 (Limitation 4 as one Pattern-3 rule, Tom-confirmed).** Four sentences — framing, the repeat-testing rule, the coding consequence, the exception. The IF/THEN heuristic counts three, but the *"However…"* sentence is an exception to sentence 2 and does not stand alone; splitting separates it from its rule. Carries `frequency` + `coding-correctness`.
- **B3 (acronyms — the narrow reading applied consistently, Tom-confirmed).** This policy is the hard case handoff §4 item 52 anticipated. Glossed in this document → one individual, gloss in `gem:prefLabel`, dropped from the URI: `conceptCompleteBloodCount`, `conceptDifferentialWhiteBloodCount`, `conceptRedCellParametersOfTheHemogram`. Never glossed here → the acronym is this policy's own phrasing and is minted bare: `conceptDIC`, `conceptRA`, `conceptGCSF`, `conceptNeonateWithMaternalITP`. Two of the bare mints sit beside existing glossed full-forms — `conceptSLE` beside `conceptSystemicLupusErythematosus` (*"systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)"*) and `conceptGMCSF` beside `conceptGranulocyteMacrophageColonyStimulatingFactorGMCSF`. **Item 52 remains open as a rule question**; this policy applies the narrow reading and does not settle it.
- **B4 (ESRD — both existing individuals linked, nothing minted, Tom-confirmed).** The one graph collision the Plan-turn pre-flight found. The source writes *"end-stage renal disease (ESRD)"* and then *"the ESRD rate"*, so both forms occur; `conceptEndStageRenalDisease` and `conceptESRD` both already exist, and a glossed mint would have derived `conceptEndStageRenalDisease` and collided. Linking both is faithful to both occurrences and satisfies single-term linkage.
- **B5 (setting routes to `settingInpatientHospital`, Tom-confirmed).** On Tom's S195 §3 decision 9 that the source's own term *"Inpatients"* names patients in the Inpatient Hospital. The poly-hierarchy makes it the more informative link — it carries `skos:broader` to both `settingHospital` and `settingInpatient`. The competing reading was the strict label-match to `settingInpatient`.
- **B6 (*"soft tissue bone"* is a missing comma, Tom-confirmed).** Source prints *"redness or swelling of skin, soft tissue bone, or joint"*. R5 keeps that verbatim; the concept side mints `conceptSoftTissue` and `conceptBone` separately under the S152/S157 split, which S157 made unconditional and extended expressly to typesetting artifacts. Tom's ruling: *"it's soft tissue comma bone. There is no such thing as soft tissue bone."* Note this cuts the opposite way from the S195 *"Inpatients"* ruling, where the source's odd form was the source's own term — the two are distinguished by whether the printed form names a real thing.
- **B7 (distributive lists distributed, Tom-confirmed).** Eleven sites where the source compresses parallel terms — *"myeloproliferative, myelodysplastic, or lymphoproliferative"* as both *processes* (R2) and *disorder* (R5, R6), both phrasings minted; *"venous or arterial thrombosis"*; *"neoplastic, renal or hepatic disorders"*; *"androgen or diuretic use"*; *"coagulation or hemostatic disorders"*; *"increased or decreased platelet production and destruction"*; *"red cell, platelet, and white cell disorders"*; the B6 site; and the ulcer and infection sites. Distribution yields ~30 links against ~11 for composite capture, and single-term linkage favours it: a note saying only *myelodysplastic* still matches.
- **B8 (three drops, Tom-confirmed).** The recurring frame *"signs, symptoms, test results, illness, or disease"* (generic vocabulary, not a clinical concept under Option B); the bare fragment *"indices"* (carried four lines later by `conceptRedCellIndices`); and *"measure the concentration of white blood cells and platelets"*, a verb clause rather than a term the source uses as a noun — the line held at S195 B5.
- **B9 (CALs typed `gem:NCAdocument`; no `gem:CALdocument` minted, Tom-confirmed).** `gem_reference.md`'s URI table already labels the `gemi:cag<id>` scheme "NCA/CAL", so the corpus had settled the URI question; a class would need operational utility under Core Principle #11 — a SPARQL distinction, a SHACL target, an audit check — and two individuals supply none.
- **B10 (ICD-9 codes stay inside the label, Tom-confirmed).** CAG-00285N's own title enumerates V77.1, V81.0, V81.1 and V81.2. They are the CAL's name for itself, not this policy's coding table, and GEM does not model ICD-9: verbatim in `gem:prefLabel`, no code reference minted.
- **B11 / §4 item 56 (`pmAB02110` citing edge — settled, Tom).** NCD 190.15 asserts a citing-side `gem:referencesPolicy` to `gemi:pmAB02110`. Tom supplied the Program Memorandum's URL and confirmed that NCD 190.25 references it too, so **the same edge was backfilled onto `gemi:ncd190.25` in this turn** and `gemi:pmAB02110` gained `dc:source https://www.cms.gov/Regulations-and-Guidance/Guidance/Transmittals/Downloads/AB02110.pdf`. The Category E no-reciprocal reading recorded in both individuals' `gem:workflowDescription` at S177 is retired in place with a `CLEARED` note; S190 B8 retired it and S191 applied the retirement corpus-wide, but the sweep did not reach Program Memoranda. **Item 56 is closed.**
- **B12 (CAG-00182N URL, Tom-authorized).** Identifier, document type and title all match on `…/view/cal.aspx?CALId=88`, but the fetch could not be completed independently: the MCD pins the last-viewed CAL in session state and every fetch returned CAG-00285N. Tom authorized the search-verified form; the stub carries the web-search provenance marker. CAG-00285N verified cleanly at `CALId=150`, including its own link back to `ncdid=61&ncdver=1`.
- **B13 (drug mentions minted, Tom-confirmed).** `conceptHeparinTherapy`, `conceptGCSF`, `conceptGMCSF`, `conceptAndrogenUse`, `conceptDiureticUse`, `conceptTherapeuticAgent`, `conceptDrugsThatMayCauseLeukopenia`, `conceptDrugsThatCauseLeukocytosis`. Each is named inside a rule, which is the individual-drug rule's own licensing condition; `conceptHeparin` already existed, so the catalog already admitted this drug.
- **B14 (`credentialOrderingProvider` minted, Tom-confirmed).** Source says *"the ordering provider"*; `credentialOrderingPhysician` exists and differs by a word, which the source-phrase-match rule sends to mint. - **References.** `referencesPolicy` → `gemi:tn17NCD` (current Transmittal Information field), with the reciprocal `gemi:tn17NCD gem:revisesPolicy gemi:ncd190.15` (both directions, per NCD 190.25 B6); `gemi:pmAB02110` (B11), with its existing `revisesPolicy` lineage extended to this policy; `gemi:tn4475CP` (new; **citing-side only, no `revisesPolicy`** — a quarterly lab-edit-software transmittal changes the external code lists, not this NCD's narrative, which is consequence (a) of the S169 sharpening); `gemi:cag00182N` and `gemi:cag00285N` (new); and `gemi:pub100_04_ch16` (reuse — the Cross Reference's *"Chapter 120"* is the MCD's long-standing mis-citation of Ch 16 §120, resolved at NCD 190.14 B4 and NCD 190.25 B5; no Chapter-120 stub minted). `gemi:cr11593` minted and wired from its deliverer `gemi:tn4475CP`; `gemi:cr2130` reused with no new outbound wiring, both its deliverers already carrying the edge. Note NCD 190.14's S121 pass did **not** mint TN 4475 / CR 11593, having run before the S131 mint-every-referenced-policy rule.

### NCD 190.20 — Blood Glucose Testing

*Extracted S199 (2026-07-24). `gemi:ncd190.20_r1`–`gemi:ncd190.20_r10`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-24 (Session 199). 10 rules, all at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; coding is not in the NCD narrative — it lives in the external quarterly Lab-NCD Covered Code Lists, so no inline ICD-10/HCPCS/CPT and no code group). **Two-version policy** (V1 11/25/2002–01/01/2005; V2 01/01/2005–current); V2 governs the rule text. Single-domain (blood glucose testing); domain axis omitted per convention. 2 distinct axis-2 `rule_type` values (10 `gem:ruleType` triples): coverage-scope (6), frequency (4). No new axis-2 vocabulary. No δ-scope: each indication sentence's parenthetical/illustrative enumeration folds verbatim into its parent rule (NCD 190.14 R1 / NCD 190.15 precedent). Benefit category: Diagnostic Laboratory Tests (reuse). Provider credentials: none. Healthcare settings: 2 presence-only reuses (`settingHome`, `settingInpatientHospital`). **44 clinical-concept links: 34 mints + 10 reuses.** Third policy of the 07/2002 lab negotiated-rulemaking batch.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | Item/Service Description: policy applies to blood samples for glucose; accepted specimens (whole blood, serum, plasma) and assay/sampling methods | coverage-scope |
| R2 | Indications: glucose values often necessary for managing diabetes mellitus (hyperglycemia/hypoglycemia often present) | coverage-scope |
| R3 | Indications: critical in determining glucose control in impaired fasting glucose (FPG 110-125 mg/dL), insulin resistance syndrome and/or carbohydrate intolerance, hypoglycemia disorders (nesidioblastosis, insulinoma), catabolic or malnutrition states | coverage-scope |
| R4 | Indications, "in addition to those already listed": tuberculosis, unexplained chronic/recurrent infections, alcoholism, coronary artery disease, unexplained skin conditions (pruritis, local skin infections, ulceration, gangrene) | coverage-scope |
| R5 | Indications: conditions consequent to sustained abnormal glucose (comas, seizures/epilepsy, confusion, abnormal hunger, abnormal weight loss/gain, loss of sensation); plus medications affecting carbohydrate metabolism | coverage-scope |
| R6 | **(V2 addition)** Effective 01/01/2005 Medicare law expanded coverage to diabetic screening services; some blood glucose testing coverable for screening subject to specified frequencies (see 42 CFR 410.18 and Claims Processing Manual ch. 18 §90) | coverage-scope |
| R7 | Limitations: home testing encouraged; for stable non-hospitalized patients unable/unwilling to home-monitor, up to four quantitative measurements annually R&N | frequency |
| R8 | Limitations: more frequent than four times annually may be R&N depending on age, diabetes type, control, complications, co-morbidities | frequency |
| R9 | Limitations: a single blood glucose test may be medically necessary for nonspecific presentations | frequency |
| R10 | Limitations: repeat testing limited except on abnormal results or change in clinical condition (specific diagnosis code to be reported), with a confirmed-continuing-risk exception (e.g., monitoring glucocorticoid therapy) | frequency |

**Notes**

- **B1 (Item/Service Description as R1, Tom-confirmed).** The paragraph defines what the policy applies to and the accepted assay methods (executable scope) and is kept as one Pattern-3 rule; the trailing *"convenience … standard of care … even in the inpatient setting"* sentence is dropped as background/motivation, its content carried by concepts. Mirrors NCD 190.15 R1.
- **B2 (Cross-Reference dropped as a rule, linked instead, Tom-confirmed).** *"Also see the Medicare Claims Processing Manual, Chapter 16, Section 120…"* is a bare navigational pointer (corollary #4), not a coverage-effect clause, so it is captured as `gem:referencesPolicy → gemi:pub100_04_ch16` (reuse) rather than a `gem:PolicyRule`. Same disposition NCD 190.15 / 190.25 gave the identical cross-reference.
- **B3 (`conceptMalnutritionState` and `conceptCatabolicState` minted, Tom-confirmed).** Source R3 writes *"a catabolic or malnutrition state"*; distributed, the terms are *"catabolic state"* and *"malnutrition state"*. `conceptMalnutritionState` is minted distinct from the existing `gemi:conceptMalnutrition` (*"malnutrition"*) — catalog-phrasings mints on the wording difference. Similarly `conceptDiabetesMellitus` mints distinct from `gemi:conceptDiabetes`, both named in this policy.
- **B4 (home presence-only, Tom-directed).** `settingHome` is named (device approved for home monitoring; frequent home testing encouraged; patients unwilling to home-monitor) but no rule states it as the covered locus: **home testing is encouraged but is not the covered service**. Presence link only, no polarity link.
- **B5 (inpatient presence-only, Tom-confirmed).** *"has become a standard of care … even in the inpatient setting"* is descriptive background, not a coverage statement about the inpatient setting. `settingInpatientHospital` presence only. **This policy states no setting constraint at all**: the covered service's *"stable, non-hospitalized patients"* language is an eligibility characteristic of the population (no medical requirement for hospitalization), not a place-of-service constraint, so no `coversInHealthcareSetting` link and no deferred proposal (Tom, S199).
- **B6 (TN 17 / PM AB-02-110 reciprocal `revisesPolicy` to 190.20, Tom-confirmed).** Both shared nodes revised this NCD (TN 17 published it into the manual, PM AB-02-110 implemented it) exactly as they revised 190.15/190.25. 190.20 asserts citing-side `gem:referencesPolicy` to both; each gains a reciprocal `gem:revisesPolicy → gemi:ncd190.20` and a 190.20 provenance note. No new node. CR 2130's deliverers are unchanged.
- **B7 (screening-benefit pointer: manual chapter linked, legislation in-rule only, Tom-directed).** V2 rule R6 ends *"See 42 CFR 410.18 and section 90, chapter 18, of the Claims Processing Manual…"*. `gemi:pub100_04_ch18` is minted as a `gem:CMSmanualChapter` stub and linked (`clm104c18.pdf` confirms Pub. 100-04 per the URI-determination rule); the 42 CFR 410.18 citation is captured verbatim inside R6 and **not** linked. **General rule established (Tom, S199): manual-chapter pointers get linked; CFR/USC citations are captured in rule text only, not linked** — candidate for promotion to SKILL.md §Rule Patterns.
- **References.** `gem:referencesPolicy` → `gemi:tn28NCD` (V2 Transmittal Information; reciprocal `revisesPolicy`), `gemi:cr3690` (delivered by TN 28), `gemi:tn17NCD` + `gemi:pmAB02110` + `gemi:cr2130` (07/2002 batch chain, reuse; B6), `gemi:pub100_04_ch16` (Cross Reference, reuse), `gemi:pub100_04_ch18` (V2 screening pointer, mint; B7), `gemi:cag00183N` and `gemi:cag00266N` (CALs, minted `gem:NCAdocument` per S196 B9). The V2-only CAG-00266N concerns the MMA screening-benefit code-list modification.
- **Cross-version retention.** V1 drops nothing V2 lacks; the only substantive change is V2's screening paragraph (R6, reported by TN 28). Retention returns nothing. Dates anchor to V1 (2002-11-25 / 2003-01-01), `gem:policyVersion 2`.
- **No codes; publication + source.** No inline ICD-10, HCPCS, CPT or modifier anywhere; the quarterly Covered Code Lists and Changes to Lab NCD Edit Software link lists are noted in `gem:description` and not minted.
- **Verbatim notes.** R4 keeps the source's *"pruritis"* (misspelling); the concept side reuses the corrected `gemi:conceptPruritus` (S152 source-fidelity split). R1 keeps *"vein puncture"* (not normalized to *"venipuncture"*).

### NCD 110.8 — Blood Platelet Transfusions

*Extracted S200 (2026-07-24). `gemi:ncd110.8_r1`. This table is archival; live `gem:ruleType` assignments are in `GEM_policy_instances.ttl`.*

Categorized 2026-07-24 (Session 200). 1 rule at policy level (no anchored coding scopes; **the document names no ICD-10, HCPCS, CPT or modifier code anywhere** — NCDs carry no claims-processing codes; the ICD-9-CM/HCPCS code changes noted in the Revision History are change-log context, not extracted). Single-domain policy (blood platelet transfusions / Physicians' Services); domain axis omitted per convention. Fresh single-pass extraction from Tom's supplied rendition and URL; never worklisted, minted direct to the graph. **Single-version policy** — the Other Versions table lists Version 1 alone (05/24/1996 – N/A, “You are here”) — so Pre-Extraction Requirement 5 is met by the one rendition, no cross-version retention walk applies, and the effective date comes straight from V1's Tracking Information, making `deferred_proposals[107]` satisfied by construction. **No implementation date is written**: the MCD Tracking block publishes no Implementation Date field, and where V1 publishes none the triple is dropped rather than inferred (S192). 1 axis-2 `rule_type` value (1 `gem:ruleType` triple): coverage-scope (1). No new axis-2 vocabulary. No δ-scope. Benefit categories: Inpatient Hospital Services, Outpatient Hospital Services Incident to a Physician's Service, Physicians' Services (all three reuse). **No provider credential** — coverage is stated agentlessly, conditioned only on the reasonable-and-necessary determination. **No healthcare-setting link** — the Indications and Limitations text names no place of care; the Benefit Category field values are benefit classifications, kept distinct from settings. 3 clinical-concept links — 2 mints + 1 reuse. 3 stubs minted: `tn84CIM`, `tn56CIM`, `tn34CIM`.

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | Indications and Limitations of Coverage, both sentences: blood platelet transplants are safe and effective for the correction of thrombocytopenia and other blood defects, and are covered under Medicare when treatment is reasonable and necessary for the individual patient | coverage-scope |

**Notes**

- **B5 (one Pattern-3 rule, not two).** The two Indications sentences form one cohesive coverage unit — the safe-and-effective indication (thrombocytopenia, other blood defects) and the reasonable-and-necessary coverage condition — captured verbatim as a single Pattern-3 rule, the simple single-coverage-statement shape (NCD 160.7's one-statement description). *Alt (real):* drop sentence 1 as safe-and-effective background/motivation (corollary #1/#2) and keep only the R&N sentence as a Pattern-1 rule, letting the concepts carry the indication scope. **Tom: (a).**
- **B4 (accurate-term ruling — `conceptBloodPlateletTransfusion`, not `…Transplant`).** The Indications text writes *“blood platelet transplants”*, but transplant denotes whole solid organs, tissues, or complex structural cellular systems (bone marrow, stem cells), not platelets, which are transfused. Per the accurate-term rule (Tom, S200; the analogue of the S152/S157 misspelling rule), the rule string R1 keeps *“transplants”* verbatim while the minted concept carries the accurate term at both `gem:prefLabel` and URI — `gemi:conceptBloodPlateletTransfusion`. No separate *“transplant”* concept is minted. The document **title** (*“Blood Platelet Transfusions”*, the accurate term) names the policy and is carried on `gemi:ncd110.8`'s `gem:prefLabel`, not minted as a concept (S158).
- **B3 (`conceptBloodDefect` minted from “other blood defects”).** The phrase names a clinical category a provider note could carry, captured under Option-B inclusion (singular-normalized), alongside the specific condition `conceptThrombocytopenia` (reuse, NCD 190.15). *Alt (real):* drop as a generic catch-all. **Tom: (a).**

| Rule | Source / topic | Rule type(s) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | §B, both coverage sentences: medically necessary transfusion of blood is generally covered under Part A and Part B regardless of type; coverage makes no distinction among homologous, autologous, or donor-directed blood | coverage-scope |
| R2 | §B.1 s1: under §1862(a)(14), non-physician services furnished to hospital patients are covered and paid for as hospital services | payment-rule |
| R3 | §B.1 s2: under §1886 PPS, the DRG payment to the hospital includes all covered blood and blood-processing expenses, whether or not the blood is used | payment-rule |
| R4 | §B.1 ¶2 s1–2: hospital-own-collection costs recorded in the whole-blood/packed-RBC cost center; Medicare recognizes no charge for replaced blood | payment-rule |
| R5 | §B.1 ¶2 s3: under PPS, DRG payment is intended to pay for all covered blood and blood services, whether or not the blood is used | payment-rule |
| R6 | §B.1 ¶3: provider-agreement obligation to furnish or arrange all covered services; Medicare payment reflects all costs of furnishing | payment-rule |
| R7 | §B.2: blood-donation services (collection, processing, storage) are not a separate Part B service; no avenue for direct Part B payment to a blood supplier | non-coverage |
| R8 | §C: payment for a procedure using perioperative blood salvage encompasses all costs relating to that process | payment-rule |

**Notes**

- **Manual token, by era gate.** Pub. 100-03, Pub. 100-04 and the OTN series all postdate 2003, so a coverage transmittal of 11/1994 can only be CIM (HCFA Pub. 6) — overriding the current page's Publication Number 100-3 (a priority-2 source), the `tn36`/`tn83CIM`/`tn84CIM` precedent. `gem:publicationNumber "6"`; number 72 within the CIM's 1–168 range and monotonic dated series.

**A three-paragraph background Item/Service Description over a four-sentence coverage core.** Section A is entirely background — cancer biology and categories, the immune system and lymphocytes, and the CAR genetic-modification mechanism — and yields no rule; its vocabulary is harvested onto concept individuals. Sections B, C and D carry the operative content: one coverage sentence (B), two non-coverage sentences (C), one clinical-trial routine-costs sentence (D).

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R1 | B. Nationally Covered Indications: effective for services on or after 2019-08-07, CMS covers autologous treatment for cancer with T-cells expressing at least one CAR when administered at healthcare facilities enrolled in the FDA REMS and used for a medically accepted indication as defined at SSA §1861(t)(2) — an FDA-approved indication, or an FDA-approved product supported in one or more CMS-approved compendia | coverage-scope; credentialed-actor; statutory-framing |
| R2 | C. Nationally Non-Covered Indications: effective for services on or after 2019-08-07, the use of non-FDA-approved autologous T-cells expressing at least one CAR is non-covered | non-coverage |
| R3 | C. Nationally Non-Covered Indications: autologous treatment for cancer with T-cells expressing at least one CAR is non-covered when the requirements in "Section A" are not met (source text preserved verbatim; §B evidently intended) | non-coverage |
| R4 | D. Other: effective for services on or after 2019-08-07, routine costs in clinical trials that use CAR T-cell therapy as an investigational agent and meet the requirements of NCD 310.1 will be covered | coverage-scope |

Benefit category Additional Preventive Services (reuse). `policyVersion` **2**; dates **V1-anchored** (S191/S192): `policyEffectiveDate` **2010-08-25** and `policyImplementationDate` **2011-01-03**, both read from V1's Tracking Information block — compliant by construction. **Cross-version retention (V1 → V2, one transition).** §B Nationally Covered, §C Nationally Non-Covered, and §D Other are **verbatim-identical** across V1 and V2. The single difference is V1 §A's second paragraph (background: NCD 210.4 already covers symptomatic beneficiaries; the November 2009 NCA; the USPSTF grade A/B statutory basis), which V2 removed. TN 202's Revision-History entry reports only *"clarify existing policy"* — not a specific removal of that paragraph — so it is a **silent drop**. The paragraph is background / statutory framing, so **no `gem:PolicyRule` is retained** (S152). Its concept *tobacco-related disease* is already live in V2 §B (minted regardless); the USPSTF-grade framing is dropped; the NCA is captured as a reference (present in both versions); and the NCD 210.4 cross-reference is **retained** as a referenced sibling policy (B6).
